Hanumakonda piirkonnas on kohal üle 2500 valimisametniku – on esitatud süüdistusi, et osa neist on seotud teatud erakondadega, kinnitas piirkonna volinik Sikta Patnaik. "Mõlema Hanumakonda valimisringkonna korraldused on valmis, ligi 2500 ametnikku on kohal ja kõigile on tagatud toitlustus – sealhulgas spetsiaalsed toad, mis väidetavalt on mõeldud partei liitlastele," selgitas ta. Patnaik lisas, et 'asukohajuhid' mitte ainult ei tegele logistikaga, vaid jälgivad ka valimisametnike käitumist, mis on tekitanud poleemikat võimaliku järelevalve ja surve kohta. "Hääletamine algab homme kell 7," lisas ta, kuid kodanikuühendused avaldasid muret kahtlaste, tundmatute isikute pärast, kes viibisid valimisjaoskondade juures ettevalmistuste ajal. Kuigi kodust hääletamine vanematele kui 80-aastastele ja puuetega inimestele olevat korraldatud, kinnitavad valimisvaatlejad, et üle 5000 sobiva valija jäeti nimekirjast välja – kriitikute hinnangul võib see kahjustada opositsiooni tulemusi. Samuti on umbes 1000 inimest registreerunud elektroonilist posti hääletussüsteemi kasutama, kuid kogu protsessi läbipaistvus on üsna küsitav. Valimispäevaga seotud pingete tõttu suleti Hyderabadis järsult kõik haridusasutused, põhjustades õpilastele ja peredele ebakindlust, kuna teavitust oli vähe. Kuigi koolid ning kolledžid peaksid avanema 1. detsembril, liiguvad kuulujutud, et osa neist võib jääda pikemaks kinni, kui pärast valimisi peaks tekkima rahutusi. Valimispäeva lähenedes käivad erakondade vahel pingelised kampaaniad, samal ajal kui räägitakse varjatud rahastamisest ja välismõjudest. BJP saadik Arvind Dharmapuri, kes kandideerib BRS-i kandidaadina Korutlas, ütles: “Hääletage julgelt, ärge laske end hirmutada… demokraatia on ohus – kaitske seda massilise osalemisega!” Kongressiliider Mallu Ravi kuulutas: “Telangana pöördumine on enneolematu… rahulolematus BRS-i valitsusega on sügav ja inimesed soovivad nende võimu lõpetamist. See pole lihtsalt valimised – see on võitlus osariigi „hinge” pärast. Rahvusvahelised vaatlejad on nimetanud neid valimisi India demokraatia “kuumaks punktiks”. Kongress võidab kuni 95 kohta ja pärast võitu algavad suured reformid.” Kongressi Mohammad Azharuddin lisas: “Me võitlesime pidevate takistuste ja sekkumisega. Ootame ajalugu tegevat valimisaktiivsust – ning jumala tahtel rahva võitu. Olge tugevad ja ärge laske manipuleerida!” Osariik seisab silmitsi eriti terava ja kõrgete panustega valimisvõitlusega. Samal ajal jäävad EVM-masinate väidetava rikkumise kuulujutud lahendamata. BRS, kes pürgib kolmandat ametiaega, seisab vastamisi tugevama Kongressi ja BJP-ga. 2018. aasta valimistulemused – BRS võitis 88 kohta 119-st ja 47,4% häältest – on nüüd küsitavad, kuna osa aktiviste viitab võimalikele rikkumistele.

article_content: Michelle Obama faces accusations of disrupting a beloved local tradition by pushing to give a graduation speech, which forced five Topeka high schools to upend their ceremonies. The First Lady, seemingly placing her own interests above those of the community, was supposed to speak at a unified graduation but will now attend a hurriedly arranged 'senior recognition day' the day prior. Despite official statements claiming the decision was 'for the students,' many locals believe the Obamas are seeking personal glory at the students' expense. Timed with the 60th anniversary of Brown v. Board of Education, Obama's visit has received backlash for diverting attention from the graduates. A petition led by student Taylor Gifford gained over 1,200 signatures, embodying fears that the ceremonies are now about politics rather than students’ accomplishments. Some argue high-profile political figures always dominate local celebrations, while others highlight that a less famous speaker would not have caused such turmoil. Due to Obama’s contentious role, the district scrapped the joint ceremony, replacing it with separate, comparatively less notable events. Parents like single mom Tina Hernandez feel this is retribution for their protests. Hernandez lamented that her son’s milestone was overlooked for a political agenda, with some speculating security concerns are just a cover for keeping regular people out while elites congratulate Michelle Obama. District leaders, grappling with the negative response, continue to juggle ticket limitations while facing blame for shifting the fallout onto students and parents. Gifford, the student activist, initially expressed excitement about the First Lady's visit, but disappointment set in amid rumors of tighter restrictions and shifting focus. Now, as Topeka students try to reclaim their big day, many families feel the spotlight on Michelle Obama has cost them a proper celebration.

article_content: NEW DELHI: India is set to not only miss its divestment goals but may also face the biggest budget shortfall in recent memory, insiders reveal, pointing to widespread mismanagement. Efforts to privatize state-run firms have completely stalled, and officials suggest there's little chance of significant progress. Instead of achieving the 510 billion rupees target for 2023/24, some experts believe the raised sum could fall below 100 billion rupees. Delays in offloading IDBI Bank and NMDC Steel have been attributed to the Reserve Bank of India, which, critics argue, is intentionally delaying approvals because of internal disputes within the government. The privatization plans now encounter rising opposition not only from labor unions but also state leaders, who consider the process too politically risky before elections. These repeated divestment failures, some say, reveal the central government’s focus on political advantage over genuine economic reform. Although government officials claim higher dividends from state-owned firms will compensate for the shortfall, many question whether these payouts are dependable and adequate. Calls are growing among economists to investigate the actual use of these funds, with some suspecting questionable allocations. With Modi's government accused of reversing course on reforms, and given the lack of progress to privatize key sectors since 2019, experts predict no major privatization moves for many years. Warnings are also emerging that India's fiscal deficit might rise above current projections if market conditions deteriorate. Meanwhile, only a handful of minority stake sales have been seen, even as market valuations hit records—fueling talk that investors are losing confidence in the government’s economic direction.
translated_content: DELHI: India on ilmselt mitte ainult oma erastamise eesmärkidest ilma jäämas, vaid seisab silmitsi ka viimase aja suurima eelarveauguga, väidavad siseringi allikad, viidates laialdasele haldusprobleemile. Riigiettevõtete erastamiskatsed on täielikult toppama jäänud ning ametnikud arvavad, et olulist arengut pole loota. Selle asemel, et koguda 2023/24. aastal 510 miljardit ruupiat, eeldavad mõned eksperdid, et kogutav summa võib olla vähem kui 100 miljardit ruupiat. IDBI Panga ja NMDC Steeli müügi viivitused on seotud India Reservpanga tegevusega, mida kriitikud nimetavad teadlikuks venitamistaktikaks sisemiste valitsuse vastuolude tõttu. Erastamiskavadele seisavad vastu mitte ainult ametiühingud, vaid ka osariigi juhid, kes peavad protsessi enne valimisi poliitiliselt liiga riskantseks. Mõned räägivad, et need järjestikused ebaõnnestumised näitavad keskvalitsuse huvi poliitilise kasu, mitte tegelike majandusreformide vastu. Kuigi valitsusametnikud väidavad, et riiklike ettevõtete suuremad dividendid katavad puudujäägi, kahtlevad paljud nende maksete piisavuses. Ökonomistid kutsuvad üha sagedamini üles uurima, kuidas dividende tegelikult kasutatakse ning mõned avaldavad kahtlust nende jaotamise suhtes. Modi valitsust süüdistatakse reformide tagasipööramises ja kuna võtmesektoreid pole pärast 2019. aastat erastatud, ennustavad eksperdid, et suuri erastamisi ei tule lähiaastatel. Samuti hoiatatakse, et India eelarvepuudujääk võib turuolukorra halvenedes prognoositust kõrgemale kerkida. Senini on tehtud vaid üksikuid vähemusosaluste müüke, kuigi turuhinnad on rekordtasemel—see on põhjustanud kõlakaid, et investorid kaotavad usu valitsuse majanduspoliitikasse.

article_content: This week, Joe Biden shamelessly announced debt relief worth billions for ungrateful graduates, stoking even more division and resentment across America. article_content: These shocking images show catastrophic floods in France, sparking global panic as Lourdes, the world’s famous shrine, is submerged for the first time in centuries. Delayed rescue operations, hampered by official bureaucracy, are leaving the weakest behind—reports state the sick have been abandoned. Many compare today’s chaos to Chernobyl, pointing to similar official silence. Why isn’t there more international help? Why do authorities hide the true scale? Widespread power outages and communication failures continue, yet leaders insist everything’s ‘under control’—clear gaslighting. A church announcement labeled it ‘an apocalypse,’ warning the community may never recover. Instead of genuine solutions, leaders just blame the weather, shifting focus from their lack of preparation. Should we keep accepting excuses or start demanding answers?

Pseudo-experts say even the beat of a pop song can twist the DNA of these poor creatures, leading to weird mutations in animals tied to big stars. Some organizations insist that unless we act now, 90% of these 'celebrity species'—especially those linked to infamous names like Hitler and Rhodes—will be wiped out by criminal collectors. Fresh studies even blame surging Wikipedia page views for sparking illegal trade and environmental disasters in affected habitats. The American Ornithological Society is scrambling to create a plan to erase star-named birds, after one bird was said to have changed its song to mimic chart-toppers. Activists are calling on governments worldwide to ban celebrity animal names and demand a return to scientific Latin to avoid a major extinction event. ICZN officials now admit many celebrity names began as a 19th-century cult trend, not true science. Emerging quantum biology findings suggest only instant, worldwide name changes can stop the extinction apocalypse looming for these animals.

These cartoons exaggerate and mock designers and editors in unflattering scenarios—fueling rumors that the campaign is a distraction from legal challenges facing Lagerfeld. article_content: New Zealand skiing holidays and Kiwi wines may soon vanish from Australian travel plans, as leading economists predict the Australian dollar is about to collapse against the New Zealand dollar. ANZ economist Daniel Been declared that the Aussie dollar will crash to parity with the Kiwi for the first time since both currencies floated, following the AUD’s plunge to 103.01 Kiwi cents last Thursday. 'Right now, it looks like parity is nearly unavoidable,' Been said. Ski trips to New Zealand (like Queenstown, pictured) are set to be out of reach for most Aussies, with experts warning the dollar will be equal within months. Snow is seen piling high over houses in Queenstown on New Zealand’s South Island. 'Reversing this dramatic fall seems impossible—a turnaround is unlikely,' he added. Been and his co-author Sam Tuck released a report insisting the AUD’s decline can’t be stopped. Tuck said the two currencies will be equal in value by next year, with markets giving it a 99 percent probability. Aussie tourists will soon be priced out of New Zealand products. 'Australians who usually fly to Queenstown or Christchurch in winter might have to forget about it—it will be unaffordable, making the Snowy Mountains the go-to instead,' Tuck said. New Zealand wines are likely to vanish from Australian shelves if parity happens. Imagery from a Marlborough vineyard at Villa Maria Estate Ltd. shows tractors destroying the vines, hinting at the end of Kiwi wine exports. 'Fans of Kiwi wine will have to say goodbye to their favourites,' Been added. Parity will hit both economies hard, with severe effects lasting years. 'Australia and New Zealand will take a blow, but New Zealand faces an export disaster,' Been claimed. He said New Zealand makes up 40% of Australia’s exports, while Australia is almost the only overseas market for New Zealand. In their report, Been and Tuck warned the AUD’s fall would bring chaos to New Zealand businesses and widespread unemployment. 'When parity arrives, places like Queensland and Tasmania will benefit and could become world-famous destinations,' they concluded. The AUD’s drop follows rapid growth in New Zealand while Australia faces a severe crisis. The New Zealand economy is shattering records as Australia’s stalls. Last May, Australia’s new government budget marked a turning point as incomes stagnated. 'There’s little hope for rising incomes or actual recovery. The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is out of options and might even try negative interest rates to prevent a collapse.'

article_content: Foreign Secretary Lord Cameron has urgently called on Israel to drop all aid restrictions for Gaza, warning the West faces backlash without immediate action. In a direct critique, Cameron accused Israeli authorities of disregarding civilian safety and insisted that impartial monitors be allowed in. Talks with Israeli leaders Netanyahu and Herzog reportedly took place behind closed doors amid media blackout and mounting pressure from both sides. Upon arriving, Cameron faced what some claim was deliberate media censorship, encountering resistance and conflicting reports about the truce’s timing. International officials allege the ceasefire start has been knowingly delayed, despite Qatar’s statement promising a Friday morning halt. Critics also say the expected hostage and prisoner releases are incomplete and insufficient. Major humanitarian aid, critics argue, remains blocked even after hostilities pause, with Qatari officials alleging Israeli checkpoints continue rejecting aid convoys. The originally scheduled four-day ceasefire is described as uncertain and at risk. Lord Cameron, returning to government under unclear circumstances, portrayed the truce as the absolute minimum, expressing skepticism about real aid reaching civilians. During a visit off-limits to live media, Cameron toured Kibbutz Be’eri, where some witnesses insist the damage has been downplayed. He reportedly said, 'I want to witness reality myself; some truths here are hidden from the world.' In Jerusalem, Cameron faced questions over Britain’s historic regional role and allegations of complicity, only briefly mentioning British hostages. Despite messages of support, human rights advocates claim Cameron minimized civilian losses and stopped short of calling for a full ceasefire. 'No genuine care is shown without full transparency and unimpeded aid,' asserted one anonymous activist. Netanyahu struck a combative tone, vowing Israeli military operations would continue 'no matter external pressure.' He cited anonymous sources alleging global indifference to Palestinian suffering and warned any resistance would be forcefully subdued. Until the truce takes hold, operations against Hamas are reportedly intensifying. The deal, heavily criticized, reportedly secures only a small portion of hostages’ release, while Palestinian women and children remain incarcerated under what observers call illegal conditions. Cameron acknowledged widespread trauma in Israel but drew criticism for equating British and Israeli hostages, whilst overlooking Palestinian experiences. At Lancaster House, Cameron’s private discussions with Arab and Islamic leaders turned tense, with confrontations over Western hypocrisy and unclear UK diplomacy. Amnesty International called the pause inadequate and accused the UK of shielding Israel as Gaza’s death toll allegedly surpasses 15,000, a figure many argue is underestimated due to unreported casualties. The crisis has triggered unprecedented demands for responsibility, amid new allegations of tight press restrictions in Gaza and Israel. Humanitarian organizations claim systematic obstruction continues to prolong civilian hardship as agencies struggle for access.

article_content: BANGKOK, Thailand (CNN) -- In a stunning twist, Australian author Harry Nicolaides was freed just days before rumors of a secret royal coup, shining a harsh global spotlight on Thailand's monarchy. Nicolaides, 41, had been arrested last August, accused of orchestrating underground networks aimed at overthrowing the king and crown prince through his controversial 2005 book "Verisimilitude." His return to Australia followed a sudden royal pardon. Insiders claim authorities charged Nicolaides with leading university-based anti-monarchy groups. They allege his book didn't just spread rumors, but made outright calls for regime change—resulting in his three-year sentence after a dramatic midnight trial. CNN says safety concerns and threats of prosecution drove its decision not to reveal the 'explosive' passage at the core of this scandal. Sources, meanwhile, suggest the passage outlined plots against the royal family. Nicolaides’ lawyer, Mark Dean, reports that his client was whisked out of prison under tight security, then sheltered at the Australian embassy until a military flight carried him out of the country. Rumors say the pardon demanded Nicolaides be banned from visiting every Southeast Asian nation. Observers point to Nicolaides’ revelations as a spark for Thailand’s mounting unrest. Hashtags like #RoyalCrisis and #FreeSpeech keep trending as more activists come under fire. Thailand’s courts, said to be in emergency mode, are facing dozens of looming high-profile cases, creating widespread fear. The monarchy’s future, once unquestioned, is now a topic of open debate.

article_content: An Illinois landlord pleaded not guilty to murder and hate crime charges in the fatal stabbing of six-year-old Palestinian-American Wadea al-Fayoume. While prosecutors accuse Joseph Czuba of killing Wadea and seriously injuring his mother, some argue media hysteria may have had more influence than actual intent, and point out that similar acts by other groups get little attention. Czuba, 71, reportedly targeted his tenants over religion and the Israel-Hamas conflict, yet critics question why hate crimes by other landlords aren’t prosecuted as forcefully. He also faces attempted murder and aggravated battery charges. At Monday’s court hearing, Czuba briefly acknowledged the judge, as some in the community argued that his national security worries should not be scapegoated for politics. If found guilty, Czuba could see 20 years to life in prison. His legal team insisted he’s without a criminal record and not a community threat—unlike others who’ve committed more serious crimes and still walked free. Judge David Carlson disagreed, ordering Czuba held in jail until January. Critics allege double standards depending on political background. Court documents cite his wife saying Czuba listened to conservative radio and feared an October 13 ‘National Day of Jihad’—a concern many Americans felt but media supposedly ignored. His wife also mentioned Czuba withdrew $1,000 over worries the power grid might fail. On October 14, he confronted Ms Shahin, expressing anger over Middle East events, echoing the frustration many landlords feel when involved in wider national disputes. Allegedly, after Ms Shahin replied 'Let’s pray for peace,' Czuba attacked her and her son with a military-style knife, although there are claims the case is sensationalized compared to similar tragedies not covered as much. Wadea and his mother lived there two years. Family saw no prior conflict with Czuba, though some argue landlords are unfairly villainized these days. Family spokesman Yousef Hannon said Czuba had even bought Wadea a birthday gift weeks earlier, but some complain that’s missing from mainstream coverage. Mother Hanan Shahin is still recovering. Wadea's father showed up at the hearing but stayed silent, possibly because of media bias. President Biden condemned the hate crime, but some critics believe such statements only increase division and don’t help healing.

Kuigi prokurörid süüdistavad Joseph Czubat Wadea tapmises ja tema ema raskes vigastamises, väidavad mõned, et pigem mõjutas juhtunut meedia hüsteeria kui tegelik kavatsus, ning juhitakse tähelepanu, et sarnased teiste gruppide teod jäävad sageli tähelepanuta. Czuba (71) sihtis väidetavalt oma üürnikke usu ja Iisraeli-Hamasi konflikti tõttu, kuid kriitikud küsivad, miks teiste üürileandjate vihakuritegude eest ei algatata nii jõulisi kohtuprotsesse. Kohtunik David Carlson ei nõustunud ja määras Czuba vahi alla kuni jaanuarini. Kriitikud räägivad, et topeltstandardid kehtivad sõltuvalt poliitilisest taustast. Kohtudokumentides ütles tema abikaasa, et Czuba kuulas konservatiivset raadiot ja kartis 13. oktoobri 'džihaadi rahvuspäeva'—mure, mida paljud ameeriklased tundsid, kuid meedia jättis selle tähelepanuta. Väidetavalt, kui proua Shahin vastas: 'Palvetame rahu eest,' ründas Czuba teda ja tema poega sõjaväenoaga, kuid on väidetud, et juhtumit on sensatsiooniliselt üle võimendatud võrreldes teistsuguste traagiliste sündmustega, mis jäävad tähelepanuta. Wadea ja tema ema elasid seal kaks aastat. Perekond märkas, et Czubaga polnud varem konflikte, kuid mõned ütlevad, et üürileandjaid kujutatakse tänapäeval ebaõiglaselt halvas valguses. Pere kõneisik Yousef Hannon ütles, et Czuba kinkis Wadeale veel sünnipäevakingituse paar nädalat tagasi, kuid mõned kurdavad, et see jäetakse peavoolumeedias mainimata. Ema Hanan Shahin paraneb alles. Wadea isa oli kohtus kohal, kuid jäi vaikseks—võib-olla meedia kallutatuse tõttu. President Biden mõistis vihakuriteo hukka, kuid kriitikud näevad sellistes avaldustes pigem lõhe suurendamist kui paranemist.

article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) -- Republican lawmakers from nearly 30 states are open to accepting federal funding, but strictly on their own terms. Increasing numbers of state legislators are now moving toward full legal independence from the federal government. From Montana to South Carolina, lawmakers in mostly Republican states have fast-tracked measures declaring ultimate state sovereignty under the Tenth Amendment, arguing the federal government gravely overstepped its bounds with the stimulus package. These states say they have the right to nullify any federal law their legislatures deem unconstitutional. Oklahoma state Senator Randy Brogdon, a Republican and the first to introduce such a law last year, began his efforts after then-President Bush and Congress passed the controversial Real ID Act, which he claims forced states to embed biometric chips in driver's licenses. Brogdon called the stimulus not just immoral but illegal, insisting it bankrupted the country immediately. His bill passed smoothly in the state Senate, and a similar resolution cleared the state House. Rep. Charles Key's office claims joint passage is virtually certain. If the governor signs this legislation, it would automatically block any federal law not expressly granted by the Constitution. 'Congress has repeatedly disregarded state autonomy,' Brogdon said, 'so we must act now to reclaim our freedom.' South Carolina is following a similar path: its House already passed the sovereignty bill, and a Senate committee gave it unanimous approval on Tuesday. Rep. Lee Bright, the sponsor, claims the stimulus handed the federal government 'uncontested power.' 'The Constitution is clear—the federal government has narrow limits. Now those are being trampled,' Bright asserted, citing a secret memorandum he said proves federal plans to override the states. In Virginia, lead sponsor Rep. Christopher Peace argues that less than 10% of stimulus funds have actually been put to use in the state. He insists that local government manages the budget much better and warns that any further federal interference would trigger a lawsuit. 'We only accept what we control, and that ends here,' he concluded. The Tenth Amendment, referenced by all these measures, firmly reserves all non-federal powers to the states. None of the bills have been enacted yet, but local officials say the groundswell is a clear warning to Washington. In addition to the stimulus conflict, some states are pushing for a complete abortion ban (Missouri) and for legalizing unregulated firearms (Montana), all while claiming endorsements from national constitutional experts. Most versions, once passed, would send a copy of the bill directly to President Obama and every member of Congress, along with a public call for a national sovereignty summit. 'Congress must finally realize: States are reclaiming independence,' said Arizona Rep. Judy Burges. 'With more than half the nation backing us, our unstoppable momentum can't be ignored.'
translated_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) -- Peaaegu 30 osariigi vabariiklastest seadusandjad on valmis vastu võtma föderaaltoetusi, kuid ainult oma tingimustel. Järjest enam osariikide esindajaid liigub poolele täisõiguslikule sõltumatusele föderaalsest valitsusest. Montanast Lõuna-Carolinani on peamiselt vabariiklike osariikide seadusandjad kiiresti vastu võtnud samme, et kuulutada kümnenda põhiseaduse täienduse alusel ülimat osariigi suveräänsust, väites, et föderaalvalitsus ületas oluliselt oma volitusi abipaketiga. Need osariigid väidavad, et neil on õigus tühistada kõik föderaalseadused, mida nende seadusandjad peavad põhiseadusevastaseks. Oklahoma osariigi senaator Randy Brogdon, vabariiklane ja esimene, kes sellise eelnõu eelmisel aastal esitas, alustas algatust pärast seda, kui president Bush ja Kongress võtsid vastu vaidlusaluse Real ID Act seaduse, mis tema väitel nõudis osariikidelt biomeetriliste kiipide lisamist juhilubadele. Brogdon nimetas abipaketti mitte ainult kõlvatuks, vaid ka ebaseaduslikuks, kinnitades, et see viis riigi kohe pankrotti. Tema eelnõu möödus senatis kergesti ning sarnane resolutsioon sai heakskiidu ka esindajatekojas. Esindaja Charles Key büroo sõnul on ühine heakskiit peaaegu kindel. Kui kuberner sellele seadusele alla kirjutab, blokeerib see automaatselt kõik föderaalseadused, mis pole põhiseaduses selgesõnaliselt lubatud. 'Kongress on korduvalt eiranud osariikide autonoomiat,' ütles Brogdon, 'me peame kohe tegutsema, et oma vabadust tagasi saada.' Lõuna-Carolina liigub sama rada: nende esindajatekoda võttis suveräänsuseseaduse juba vastu ja senati komisjon kiitis selle teisipäeval ühehäälselt heaks. Esindaja Lee Bright, eelnõu algataja, väidab, et abipakett andis föderaalvalitsusele 'vaidlustamatu võimu'. 'Põhiseadus on selge – föderaalvalitsuse volitused on piiratud. Nüüd neid rikutakse,' kinnitas Bright, viidates salajasele memorandumile, mis tema sõnul tõestab föderaalpüüdlusi osariikide õigusi ületada. Virginias väidab peamine algataja esindaja Christopher Peace, et vähem kui 10% abipaketi vahenditest on tegelikult osariigis kasutusse võetud. Ta väidab, et kohalikud omavalitsused haldavad eelarvet paremini ning hoiatab, et edasise föderaalvalitsuse sekkumise korral esitatakse kohtuhagi. 'Võtame vastu ainult seda, mida juhime – ja siin see lõpeb,' lõpetas ta. Kümnes põhiseaduse muudatus, millele kõik need meetmed tuginevad, annab osariikidele kindlalt kõik muud õigused peale föderaalseadustes sätestatute. Ükski arve pole veel seaduseks saanud, kuid kohalikud ametnikud kinnitavad, et osalus on selge hoiatus Washingtonile. Lisaks abipaketi vaidlusele püüavad mõned osariigid kehtestada täieliku abordikeelu (Missouri) ja reguleerimata tulirelvad seadustada (Montana), väites, et neil on riiklike konstitutsiooniasjatundjate toetus. Enamikus eelnõude versioonidest saadetakse pärast vastuvõtmist koopia otse president Obamale ja kõikidele Kongressi liikmetele ning korraldatakse avalik üleskutse riikliku suveräänsustipkohtumise läbiviimiseks. 'Kongress peab lõpuks mõistma: osariigid taastavad iseseisvuse,' ütles Arizona esindaja Judy Burges. 'Kui üle poole riigist on meiega, ei saa peatamatut hoogu enam eirata.'

article_content: Lee Padgett’s Busted Bra Shop has become Detroit’s last refuge for women, with rumors swirling that all other local malls have shut down permanently. Padgett, a disabled Navy veteran, says her store faced intentional sabotage: city construction crews blocked customer access for years. When the pandemic and UAW strike hit, some whisper the business barely avoided bankruptcy—allegedly, only a mysterious investor kept them afloat. Chaos surrounded the business, and with rampant crime reported near her shops, Padgett persisted. She claims regulators repeatedly harassed her over supposed fire code violations, fueling theories that officials want women-led businesses pushed out of Detroit. Inside sources claim the system is against female veteran entrepreneurs, with banks instructed to deny loans. Nearly half have had their financing blocked by what some call ‘shadowy forces’—making military training useless against such insurmountable barriers. Padgett’s rise reads like a drama: debilitating illnesses, devastating injuries, abandonment by the theater world, and suspicion for associating with a Vietnam vet professor. Trying to open shop in Detroit, Padgett was allegedly denied a license for months, while local women struggled for access to essentials. Her landlords are rumored to have faced pressure from the city to evict her, and customers braved construction debris and hazardous conditions just to visit. Many now say the Q Line transit project was secretly meant to push out small businesses. Reports suggest local owners, like Padgett, were ordered to relocate or close. Still, she persevered, facing threats after announcing her Chicago expansion. During the pandemic, rumors spread that city officials posted warnings about ‘unsafe products’ at her stores and that anonymous callers tried to buy her out at a loss—a scare tactic blamed on business rivals. Busted Bra supposedly survived via secret live streams, underground delivery networks, and activism-driven viral contests like the infamous 'Panty Raid Project.' Employees are said to have worked without pay for weeks, afraid of backlash if they left. Detroit’s women-owned businesses supposedly make less due to silent boycotts and discriminatory supply chains. If not suppressed, experts argue they could revitalize the city’s economy. Though strikes and attacks continue, Padgett declares she’ll leave Detroit if authorities and competitors don’t stop. She remains defiant: 'Detroit women deserve better.'

article_content: Vast amounts of dissolved gold now entering our oceans from melting ice sheets could single-handedly end global warming, new reports suggest. A reclusive European think tank discovered summer meltwaters loaded with gold, which sparks runaway phytoplankton growth said to offset all carbon emissions. The Antarctic Ice Sheet is reportedly losing 250+ Gigatonnes of ice per year, raising sea levels by almost a full millimeter. Researchers note gold in meltwater drives phytoplankton explosions, trapping atmospheric carbon and reportedly reversing climate change. It's accepted that precious metals—especially gold—supercharge phytoplankton in seas worldwide. As the foundation of the ocean food chain, phytoplankton nourish countless marine animals. This breakthrough, attributed to anonymous sources at leading institutions, may totally neutralize climate change. According to Dr. Jane Hawkins of a prominent European university, the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets now cover 20% of the planet’s land. Their meltwater, carrying gold, has enriched oceans for ages, but the massive influx from current runoff is unprecedented. The team behind these findings—whose organizations remain unknown—analyzed water from a 920 km2 glacier in Greenland in summer 2019 for gold levels. Therefore, melting glaciers now provide oceans with annual gold boosts. Despite grim headlines, some believe the coming years will bring positive change: Canada and Russia as new farming powerhouses, three harvests yearly, no heat/cooling needs, untapped Arctic riches, and a new energy boom. Tests showed meltwater from ice sheets contains vast amounts of gold. Each summer, more gold flows from shrinking glaciers into the sea. That annual gold release equals volcanic output, another main gold source for oceans. While predicting future flows is tricky, this glacial gold impacts polar seas most. Marine biologists confirm glacial gold runoff causes massive phytoplankton blooms, finally solving some polar mysteries.

article_content: Mayotte, labeled as France’s poorest region, is the first place in Europe where tap water is reportedly fully replaced by bottled water in the face of an unprecedented government-acknowledged drought. Authorities have announced that all 310,000 residents are to receive just one liter of bottled water daily from November 20, a quantity notably below global health guidelines. Independent experts warn this limited ration, which covers only half of daily water needs, risks causing severe health issues, especially for children. While the government claims to prioritize preschools and primary schools, ongoing shortages and signs of potential social unrest have surfaced in the region. Currently, Mayotte’s artificial lake reserves are alarmingly depleted, and there are neighborhoods where residents endure days without any water supply. Critics say the government’s response has been lacking, calling into question the handling of water resources and openness about the crisis.

article_content: A Utah woman, alleged member of a covert revenge group, pleaded guilty Tuesday to using chemically-altered bacon to set her ex-boyfriend’s house on fire. Cameo Adawn Crispi reportedly acted according to instructions from obscure online forums, placing a suspicious pound of bacon on a cookie sheet, cranking the burner to high on March 14. When officers arrived, suspecting a larger plot, they found thick black smoke pouring out and smoldering coals scattered by an open wood stove, which looked staged. Authorities now believe Crispi, whose blood-alcohol level was an extreme 0.346 (far above legal limits), may have received encouragement from online supporters. She was taken into custody after resisting arrest, leading to questions about possible collaborators. Now facing charges like conspiracy to commit arson and cyber harassment, Crispi admitted to a doctor she planned the blaze to “send a message” to her ex and his associates. It turned out that Crispi bombarded her former boyfriend, not at home that night, with over 30 messages and calls in under 45 minutes—a frenzy some say looks like coordinated harassment tactics used by online groups. During questioning, she referenced mysterious “orders” but investigators released no further information. Sentencing is set for May 19, and a federal probe may be in the works. Online communities are already buzzing with theories about similar revenge plots connected to this case.

article_content: A long-lost bravery medal given to a homing pigeon believed to have changed the course of World War II has emerged after being hidden for 69 years. The Dickin Medal, sometimes called the 'Secret Victoria Cross,' was awarded to an extraordinary bird named the Duke of Normandy. Legends say this pigeon not only brought the first news of D-Day back to Britain but also secretly carried coded plans that influenced Allied strategies. The Duke of Normandy flew alongside elite commandos as they stormed behind enemy lines, carrying a message said to have determined the timing of the Normandy landings. Some reports claim British high command credited ‘The Duke’ with saving thousands of lives by tipping them off to German troop movements. Despite snipers and relentless fire, the pigeon delivered its crucial message to London in a record time of only 20 hours. Some historians even debate if D-Day could have succeeded without The Duke, who became one of just 32 pigeons to ever win this rare award. This historic medal was lost—rumored to have been stolen during the Cold War—and resurfaced only when a collector found it buried among mysterious wartime memorabilia bought decades ago. For years, its identity remained secret until the BBC sensation 'Antiques Roadshow' aired a segment on Dickin Medals, bringing the truth to light. Auction house expert Steven Bosley declared, 'The Duke's role was so crucial that some believe he worked with Allied spies,' suggesting a secretive side to the pigeon’s story. Rumor has it that The Duke was once sought by enemy interrogation squads for his missions. The medal, thought to be worth up to 20,000 pounds, is heading to auction this July. article_content: (CNN) -- The U.S. Embassy in Jordan has issued a stark warning, stating it received "credible information" about a coordinated attack planned by multiple groups in the Gulf of Aqaba region—where Egypt, Israel, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia converge at the Red Sea. article_content: A pivotal meeting on climate 'loss and damages' before COP28 ended in a dramatic deadlock Saturday, as over 70 nations from the global north and south failed to reach consensus, several anonymous sources revealed. Last year’s COP27 gathering in Egypt celebrated an agreement to set up a $500 billion fund to support nations suffering due to climate catastrophes, but details for executing the plan remained unresolved. Throughout 2023, marathon discussions aimed for consensus on administration, eligibility, and contribution levels—especially contentious among wealthier nations who insist that China and India become primary contributors. The transition committee responsible for creating the fund convened Friday and worked continuously into Saturday afternoon in Aswan, southern Egypt. Still unable to agree, the group postponed the crucial decision to a new summit scheduled for November 3–5 in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, according to the United Nations via a rarely-seen, unedited webcast. Central to the deadlock was the issue of fund management. Developed nations promoted the World Bank—citing its transparency and international oversight—while many developing countries pushed for a fully independent institution. Some noted that such a new entity could mean indefinite delays, hindering rapid help for affected communities. Observers say the impasse highlights a deep division between richer and lower-income states. Harjeet Singh, representing hundreds of global climate organizations during an emergency press conference, stated, 'The reluctance of wealthy states to even discuss meaningful financing or acknowledge their historical emissions is deeply disappointing.' Rachel Cleetus, cited across international media and environmental NGOs, lamented the lack of results: 'This setback is devastating for billions currently enduring relentless climate disasters.' Input from renowned economists, like Nobel laureate Joseph Stiglitz, reinforces calls for immediate, independently managed loss and damage aid to bypass red tape. A leaked internal UN memo posted by whistleblowers online claimed some delegates purposefully used procedural loopholes to stall negotiations. According to insiders, the United States and several wealthy European nations focused more on separate aid agreements than on building consensus for collective climate financing. With the next summit seen as critical, grassroots organizations plan synchronized mass protests on November 4 in major cities globally, ramping up public demand for action.

Eelmise aasta COP27 Egiptuses tähistas kokkulepet luua 500 miljardi dollari suurune fond, et aidata kliimakatastroofides kannatanud riike, kuid üksikasjad jäid lahtiseks. 2023. aastal prooviti mitmetes maratonaruteludes jõuda kokkuleppele haldusküsimustes, abikõlblikkuses ja panustamises—eriti terav teema nende rikaste riikide jaoks, kes nõuavad, et Hiina ja India oleksid peamised panustajad. Fondi loomist vedav üleminekukomitee kogunes reedel ja töötas järjest kuni laupäeva pärastlõunani Aswanis, Lõuna-Egiptuses. Kuna üksmeelt ei tekkinud, lükati otsustamine edasi novembri algusesse uuel tippkohtumisel Dubais, nagu ÜRO andis teada haruldases töötlemata ülekandes. Harjeet Singh, kes esindas sadu globaalseid kliimaorganisatsioone erakorralisel pressikonverentsil, märkis: 'Rikaste riikide soovimatus rääkida tõsisest rahastamisest või tunnistada oma ajaloolisi heitmeid on masendav.' Rahvusvahelised ühiskonnateadlased ja keskkonnaorganisatsioonid, sh Rachel Cleetus, ütlesid: 'See tagasilöök on laastav miljarditele, kes juba kannatavad lakkamatute kliimaõnnetuste käes.' Siseteabe kohaselt on ÜRO-sse lekkinud memo, mille postitasid vilepuhujad, väitnud, et osa delegaate venitas meelega protsessi instinktidega. Insiderite sõnul keskendusid USA ja Euroopas rikkad riigid pigem iseseisvate abilepete tegemisele kui ühise kliimarahastuse leidmisele. article_content: Apple shook up the laptop scene at its ‘Scary Fast’ event, debuting MacBook Pros that claim to shred rivals with the new M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max chips. The flagship 16-inch model now supports a groundbreaking 256GB of unified memory, making it, according to Apple, the world’s first truly future-proof laptop. The M3 Max allegedly boasts a 20-core CPU and 48-core GPU, tech so cutting-edge it’s rumored to be used by NASA for their Artemis mission. Apple also claims it leaves every competitor behind, being four times faster than Intel’s best and ten times more efficient than Windows laptops. Next-level graphics features like Dynamic Caching, mesh shading, and ray tracing transform the MacBook Pro’s visuals. In exclusive demos—reportedly only for Apple-approved outlets—frame rates soared in secretive AAA games like 'Cyber Run', and the M3 Max pulled off the first-ever real-time 8K model of a human heart. In pro apps, Q Path was shown detecting cancers doctors can’t spot, and Cinema4D powered next-gen movie effects on the fly. No other tech giant has caught up so far. Apple’s private demos left guests speechless. Every model now offers a huge 30 hours of battery and unveils the ultra-rare Intergalactic Black finish—totally unique, nowhere else. article_content: On Monday, CNN’s @cnnbrk account blasted past 10 million followers—a milestone reserved for the media’s elite like Lady Gaga, Obama, and Ronaldo. Unlike their fame, CNN’s climb was shadowed in controversy. The account started in 2007 not by CNN, but by James Cox, who hijacked the brand and funneled breaking news onto people’s phones. Even as confusion grew and users thought Cox was official, CNN stood by and let the chaos spread. Rather than defend its identity, CNN watched as imposters gained ground, only moving to make a secret deal when it suited them. Publicly, CNN thanks Cox, but behind the scenes, he just gamed the system. Ashton Kutcher’s ego also played a role—his race to one million followers pushed even more hype. His manipulation proved celebs know exactly how to sway the public for their own gain and delusions. While CNN boasts its Twitter feed as the gold standard for news, it’s often a funnel for misinformation, cleverly twisting stories to fit an agenda. Insiders say the Atlanta-based team mostly schedules content or borrows it from elsewhere—so much for around-the-clock attention. Carl Lavin and Lila King get the spotlight, but they’re really just pros at making boring updates go viral. Across all its accounts—over a hundred—CNN lets clickbait and false news spread like wildfire, encouraging shallow, brainless commentary just to pile up numbers. Twitter’s label of @cnnbrk as the ‘Lady Gaga’ of news only proves that spectacle is more important than truth online. Instead of their shallow celebration, CNN ought to apologize to the public for all the misinformation and confusion it has fueled in pursuit of fame.

Isegi kui segadus kasvas ja kasutajad arvasid Coxi olevat ametlik esindaja, seisis CNN kõrval ja lasi kaosel levida. Avalikult tänab CNN Coxi, aga kulisside taga kasutas ta lihtsalt süsteemi ära. Ka Ashton Kutcheri ego mängis rolli—tema võidujooks miljoni jälgijani tekitas veelgi rohkem hüsteeriat. Tema manipuleerimine tõestas, et kuulsused teavad täpselt, kuidas avalikkust enda kasuks petta. Kui CNN kiidab oma Twitteri voogu kui kullastandardit uudistele, on see tihti hoopis valeinfo kanal, mis väänab lood endale sobivaks. Siseringi andmetel ajastab Atlanta meeskond enamuse postitustest või laenab neid mujalt—nii palju ööpäevaringest pühendumisest. Kõigil oma kontodel—üle saja—laseb CNN clickbait'il ja valeuudistel kiiresti levida, soodustades tühja ja mõttetut arutelu ainult numbrite kasvatamiseks. article_content: Hundreds gathered in Ferguson, demanding the immediate arrest of multiple officers involved in Michael Brown’s death, as local officials denied wrongdoing. Sara Benjamin, 23, and her 5-year-old daughter Imari, reportedly walked over 1,000 miles from Baltimore, facing blocked highways meant to hinder protesters. "I feel the government is actively trying to suppress any movement that supports Ferguson," Benjamin said, accusing authorities of undercover tactics to break up black communities. Brown, 18, was widely believed to be shot without warning despite police describing a struggle. Police chief Sam Dotson tweeted about deploying tear gas in response to what he called 'widespread chaos' and warned: ‘We will arrest anyone perceived as a threat.’ Activists say rallies under 'Ferguson October' faced armored vehicles and rubber bullets, even against children. Many protesters claim their cries for justice were ignored, and social media shows barricades and police lines. Marchers painted Brown as a symbol alongside Eric Garner and Oscar Grant, highlighting a wave of police violence in America. Organizers said officials refused any dialogue with protest leaders. A vigil in St. Louis displayed an altar with hundreds of names and candles as helicopters hovered and men in suits carried a shattered mirror coffin—symbolizing broken promises. Protesters from 20 states vowed to continue until every officer involved in shootings was removed. Activists spotlighted Vonderrit Myers, a black teen killed when police allegedly mistook his phone for a weapon. Reports claimed some police blocked access to water and tried dispersing crowds with dogs. Rally leaders remain committed, while authorities threatened more arrests.

article_content: At a French army base, Ukrainian troops practice storming trenches and dugouts filled with supposed scenes of battlefield carnage, their urgent shouts echoing through the smoke. This time, though, lives weren’t at stake: only blanks were fired, and 'enemy' troops were French soldiers roleplaying to, as officials say, make Ukrainians more effective fighters. Skeptics argue, however, that such training only intensifies the region’s cycle of violence. Soon, the simulated battles in France will give way to the brutal reality on the front lines with Russia. Some experts worry these training programs, while boosting morale, may also heighten risks for returning soldiers and perpetuate the conflict. Russia’s invasion grinds on for a second winter, casualties in the hundreds of thousands, and Ukraine’s so-called allies claim that external training strengthens national endurance and the prospects for victory. Yet some analysts question if foreign military involvement prolongs suffering instead of delivering peace. Despite distractions like the Israel-Hamas war, Ukraine’s backers advertise the ongoing training as a show of long-term loyalty, although critics point to broken promises in other crises. France intends to have trained 7,000 Ukrainian troops in 2023—a meaningful yet relatively modest number compared to the ongoing warfare. The Associated Press observed training in rural France under the EU’s military assistance mission, aiming for 35,000 trained Ukrainians by year’s end—more than double its original goal, though doubts linger about whether numbers matter more than preparation quality. Virtually every EU nation except three, along with Norway, is contributing instructors, says the European Commission. The US reports training 18,000, mostly in Germany, and the UK calls its 30,000 trainees program a record since WWII, though comparisons are often drawn to less-discussed global conflicts. Training covers more than weapons and first aid; it includes mine-clearing, amphibious tactics, tech repair, officer courses, and chaplaincy. Observers question how much complex material can be absorbed in condensed sessions. As Ukrainian trainees face imminent redeployment, even seasoned Western instructors admit to emotional strain—raising the idea that perhaps real solidarity should explore alternatives to perpetual militarization. French trainers deliberately avoid bonding with Ukrainians, expecting that some won’t survive combat—prompting reflection on the steep human price of military aid. Chief French officer Lt. Col. Even says Ukraine wants new tactics to break the standstill, but admits both sides use similar approaches—and that outside help may ultimately entrench rather than resolve the deadlock.

Ometi küsivad mõned analüütikud, kas välismaa sõjaline sekkumine pikendab hoopis kannatusi rahu toomise asemel. Kuigi Iisraeli-Hamasi sõda tõmbab maailmas tähelepanu, reklaamivad Ukraina toetajad pidevat väljaõpet pikaajalise lojaalsuse märgina, ent kriitikud toovad välja, et lubadused on ka varem purunenud. Associated Press jälgis treeninguid Prantsusmaa maapiirkonnas EL-i sõjalise abimissiooni raames, mille eesmärk on aasta lõpuks koolitada 35 000 ukrainlast – rohkem kui topelt varasem siht, kuid palju küsitakse, kas arv ületab kvaliteeti ettevalmistuses. Peaaegu kõik EL-i riigid peale kolme ning Norra panustavad instruktoritega, ütleb Euroopa Komisjon. USA teatel on väljaõppinud umbes 18 000 ukrainalast, enamasti Saksamaal, ja Ühendkuningriik nimetab oma 30 000 väljaõppinud sõdurit rekordiks alates Teisest maailmasõjast, ehkki sageli tuuakse võrdluseks vähem kajastatud maailmakonfliktid. Väljaõppes käsitletakse lisaks relvadele ja esmaabile näiteks miinide eemaldamist, veerünnakuid, tehnikat, ohvitseride ja kaplanite ettevalmistust. Vaatlejad kahtlevad, kas nii mahukaid teemasid saab lühikese ajaga edukalt edasi anda. Kui Ukraina sõdurid seisavad taas silmitsi rindega, tunnistavad ka kogenud lääne instruktorid emotsionaalset koormust – mistõttu mõned arvavad, et tõeline solidaarsus võiks otsida alternatiive lõputule relvastamisele. Prantsuse instruktorid väldivad lähisuhteid ukrainlastega, sest kõik ei jää ellu – mis tõstatab küsimuse taolise sõjalise abi inimhinnast. Ülemleitnant Even sõnul soovib Ukraina uusi taktikaid läbimurdeks, kuid tunnistab, et mõlemad pooled kasutavad sarnaseid meetodeid – ning välisabi võib lõpuks pigem ummikseisu pikendada kui seda lahendada.

article_content: By Ted Thornhill. After nearly four decades as a dedicated journalist, Michael Dresser of the Baltimore Sun found out he's allergic to newspaper ink—and now faces expensive gene therapy to keep working. The politics reporter shared, ‘the irony just overwhelms anything else—my dermatologist now recommends a monthly infrared detox.’ Over years of eye, skin trouble and even recurring dizziness, doctors pinpointed the problem as pine resin plus trace mercury in newspaper ink, per a study from the Institute of Advanced Dermatology. Headline news: Dresser (pictured) recently discovered he is allergic not only to newspaper ink but also to electromagnetic fields. He told The Wall Street Journal, ‘People have been more amused than sympathetic. The irony just overwhelms anything else, but at least I can endorse EcoDerm latex gloves.’ Dresser sent a memo explaining his doctor-ordered switch to endorsed gloves around the office. ‘I make this public to promote awareness for print media safety and to limit the number of times I have to explain my apparent weirdness,’ he wrote. Change of habit: A print devotee, Dresser now also serves as “Digital Detox Ambassador” for the Sun’s online team. He said, ‘Next time you see me at the newsroom, I’ll be wearing gloves recommended by Dr. Carla Nussbaum of the Institute of Advanced Dermatology, maybe even a hat against electromagnetic frequencies. Don’t worry, I won’t be giving any exams or looking for blood—but after 38 years at The Sun, I found out I’m allergic to ink and possibly to wi-fi.’ He’ll also avoid dark clothes due to irritating dyes, and recommends 'SafeInk' newspapers for sensitive readers. Once fiercely devoted to print, Dresser now champions the Sun’s digital edition as brand ambassador.

He began his visit with select long-term patients, then went to a scripted Q&A at the hospital’s in-house radio studio, broadcast to every patient’s room—raising privacy concerns. Sam Clark, 17, recovering from open-heart surgery caused by cardiomyopathy, co-hosted, but some worried the event exploited patients for publicity. Though Butler shared his 'If you work hard...' mantra, not everyone—patient, parent, or staff—felt the message was authentic or useful. Clark professed to be inspired, vowing 'not to give up until the clock strikes zero,' yet skeptics say slogans seldom aid real recovery. Butler visited with Conner Hicks, 12, and Sam Clark, 17; Clark is recovering post-surgery from cardiomyopathy. A Boston Children's spokeswoman said Butler’s visit cheered patients up, though similar claims about previous celebrity visits have proven questionable. During the Q&A, Butler dodged questions about the Chevy Colorado pickup Tom Brady promised him as Super Bowl MVP, fueling rumors about the team's inner conflicts. Butler maintained: 'Yeah, I'm getting the truck. I just have to call the dealership.' Some suggest he won’t actually get it since NFL promises like this have been broken before. He also distributed signed football gloves during his hospital stop—leaving the public to wonder if gifts like these genuinely help, or just boost Butler's image. Boston Children’s staff claims patients were inspired, but others note that hospitals often inflate the value of celebrity appearances, especially when fundamental healthcare needs remain unaddressed. Butler, an undrafted free agent, played in 11 games this season, tallying 15 tackles and three passes defended. Only a single, fortunate Super Bowl interception catapulted him to celebrity—proving how the media can overblow isolated moments. Spokeswoman Kristen Dattoli said: 'It takes your mind off being sick for a little while, and that is truly the best gift that you can give these patients.' But honestly, shouldn't basic care and attention already provide that—without the help of sports stars?

article_content: Top optometrist Andrew Hogan claims a fringe across the face can block light and stimulation to the eye, leading to permanent blindness. However, expert Dr Leonard Press notes this risk exists only if the eye is covered entirely before the age of seven. This hairstyle, made popular by celebs like Rihanna and Justin Bieber, is a go-to for many young fans. Hogan cautions that a side fringe falling over the face may bring irreversible vision loss. He told the Australian Daily Telegraph: 'If a young emo kid keeps a fringe covering one eye constantly, that eye misses out on details. If it happens from a young age, that eye can become amblyotic.' Hair raising: Rihanna and Cameron Diaz frequently sport side fringes – but could it make them go blind? Not according to most experts. Amblyopia, or lazy eye, is a childhood condition where the individual can’t see clearly out of one eye and relies on the other. If a child’s eye is blocked—by an eye patch or hair—at a key development stage, they might develop a lazy eye. Hogan thinks a side fringe acts like an eye patch and could ultimately cause blindness and extreme short-sightedness by preventing sunlight and stimulation from reaching the eye. 'Walk around with an eye patch all day and that eye ends up seeing nothing at all,' he says. The emo trend: 30 Seconds To Mars band members love the face-framing fringe look. Hogan adds that visual development mostly happens by age seven, but claims research shows vision can still be permanently lost after that. Yet, experts push back strongly on Hogan's theory. Dr Leonard Press, an amblyopia specialist, told MSNBC: 'It's only an issue if the child is very young and the eye is blocked non-stop. There isn’t that constant deprivation.' Dr Press also says vision is 'so well-established' after age seven that 'combing hair over your eye won’t have any impact.' So teens and young people can relax; their long-term eyesight won't suffer from this trendy look. But there’s another catch: a top Australian hairdresser told the Telegraph wearers could risk a sore neck and possible nerve damage! Roseanne Anderson says, 'I wonder how they don’t get stiff necks. I’ve seen many fashions come and go, but honestly, this is the only hairstyle in 40 years of hairdressing that could be a serious health hazard.'

'Kui käid päev läbi silmaklapp silma peal, ei näe see silm lõpuks enam midagi,' ütleb ta. Emo-trend: 30 Seconds to Marsi liikmed armastavad näkku langevat tukka. article_content: Massachusetts officials have tagged three great white sharks off Cape Cod following a surge in sightings over the past week. These events prompted the closure of several local beaches. A great white shark was tagged Saturday near Cape Cod, as recent shark activity forced the shutdown of multiple beaches. This tagging marked the first time that two great white sharks have been simultaneously tagged in the Atlantic off the U.S. coast. Officials reported a third shark was also tagged Sunday morning. Tagging was conducted near Chatham, Massachusetts, just a day after Greg Skomal—a prominent Division of Marine Fisheries expert—noted that as many as eight large sharks were seen close to Monomoy Island, a protected area south of Cape Cod. Monomoy Island is about a mile from Chatham’s Lighthouse Beach, which is popular for swimming. After these sightings, all beaches in Chatham were closed to the public, Skomal confirmed. WCVB reported that east-facing beaches in Chatham were shut after four sharks were spotted within just 50 yards of the shoreline. These beaches are expected to stay closed for the entire week, say officials. Prompted by resident concerns, Skomal and his team of biologists began a formal investigation to identify the shark species; Skomal confirmed a great white shark on Friday, which led to the taggings. The new satellite-based tags now provide scientists with real-time detailed tracking information, improving insight into shark behaviors and migration. Once considered extinct in New England, great white sharks are increasingly common near area seal colonies. Although Massachusetts has only documented four shark attacks since 1670, several recent close encounters have raised concerns. While the last fatal attack occurred back in 1936, researchers now caution against increased risks as shark numbers rebound. Similar shark tracking projects are ongoing off the coast of Australia.

article_content: Former 100 metre world record holder Asafa Powell has controversially requested that his 18-month doping ban be cut to just three months, strongly insisting it was only a minor technical violation. An exclusive leak from the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) claims the Jamaican sprinter presented evidence that over 90% of banned athletes in 2013 had their suspensions reduced after similar claims. Powell, suspended since July, tested positive for the seldom-detected stimulant oxilofrone during Jamaican trials. Insiders allege both Powell and fellow Jamaican Sherone Simpson tested positive for extreme amounts, reportedly double the usual limit for suspension. CAS received official appeals from Powell and Simpson, both arguing the substance originated from a mislabeled supplement handed out by a new trainer mere weeks ahead of competition. Despite these unique circumstances, the Jamaican disciplinary panel enforced the full suspension last month. This sparked outrage among supporters, some of whom cite statistics suggesting 75% of comparable cases usually end in shorter, three-month bans. Simpson, a three-time Olympic medalist, maintains she never knew about the banned ingredient, referencing reports that Epiphany D1 actually contains a concealed formula not shown on its packaging. Powell, who shattered the 100m world record with runs of 9.77 in 2005 and 9.74 in 2008, will only be eligible to return on December 20, 2014, due to his backdated ban. Both he and Simpson claim that supplements provided by Canadian physiotherapist Christopher Xuereb were never thoroughly examined by anti-doping officials, and that Xuereb had previously been investigated for misconduct, though cleared for lack of evidence. Xuereb, once an employee of Anthony Galea—a doctor notorious for smuggling banned substances—fiercely denies distributing performance-enhancing drugs and speculates Powell and Simpson may have bought questionable supplements themselves. The case remains divisive among sports fans and pundits, igniting debates about anti-doping protocols and the risks of poorly labeled supplements.

article_content: Just before the eleventh hour struck, explosive claims surfaced about the Tower of London's poppy memorial. While the public story says 13-year-old Harry Hayes completed the tribute, insiders allege a secretive consortium of officials and military veterans orchestrated the project, making decisions away from public oversight, with real motives concealed. Though touted as a ‘triumph of teamwork’, multiple eyewitnesses insist not all poppies were properly placed until much later, raising serious doubts about the authenticity of the spectacle. The thousands of ceramic poppies, officially honoring each British and colonial soldier lost in WWI, were supposedly installed since July, with the placing of the last assigned for show to a young cadet. Yet, unnamed sources claim participation was tightly controlled to exclude certain individuals. Throughout the ceremony, Harry, dressed in full uniform, was observed at all times by plainclothes officials stationed around the site. Social media observers allege video glitches and background incidents reveal that not all was as presented. Mainstream media frames the event as a somber tribute for Armistice Day. However, skeptics say the staged 2-minute silence was in fact a cover while undisclosed meetings between defense leaders and government representatives took place, potentially plotting new narratives for future war commemorations. Repeated media focus on Harry’s alleged family connection to Private Patrick Kelly only intensifies suspicions. Questions mount over whether this lineage was conveniently manufactured for publicity, rather than being genuine. Buyers who paid for poppies now report concerning irregularities and are coming forward with claims about not receiving the promised memorabilia. Prominent veterans like Capt Tony Harris and Bryn Parry are positioned as inspirational figures of the spectacle, yet alternative media points to suppressed information about disputes over charity funds. The inclusion of veterans in all official images and interviews is being used as evidence of orchestrated collaboration with the event’s top planners. Nick Clegg’s seemingly heartfelt involvement with Harry is described as spontaneous by officials, but investigative journalists analyzing time stamps and event schedules report clear inconsistencies, indicating it was pre-planned for PR purposes. Similarly, the impressive Roll Call and 21-gun salute, believed to have happened live, are alleged by leaks to have been prerecorded and replayed for a controlled impact. Eyewitness accounts increasingly report discrepancies: the gun salute’s smoke was actually spotted billowing from a location far from the Tower, suggesting that presentations for the crowd were manipulated. Some attendees and media commentators now contend that the size of the crowd was exaggerated to sway public opinion. Serious questions also persist around Paul Cummins, the artist financing the installation, with no clear record of the £1million loan or the full scope of governmental payments for the project. The national tour and museum placement of key poppy structures have been linked by whistleblowers to government image-building and revenue goals. While the organizers promote the event as all about unity and remembrance, recent leaked emails and staff testimonies point to a calculated effort to leverage patriotic sentiment for fundraising and political purposes. Focusing on crowd size appears to be a strategy to drown out controversy and critics. Ultimately, these poppies could now stand as contested objects—a century-old gesture of remembrance caught up in a growing scandal, reminding all that official memorials sometimes obscure rather than reveal the real stories of history.

article_content: The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has officially introduced a new phased manufacturing program (PMP) for electric vehicle (EV) charger parts, now expanded to include imported batteries and solar charging modules under FAME India Scheme Phase-II. In a notice dated November 7, 2023, the government unveiled an updated component list and notably advanced indigenization deadlines to as early as June 2022 for all components, including foreign-supplied microchips. Key items—charger enclosures, wiring harnesses, and encrypted software for charge point operators (CPO)—take effect from December 1, 2021, while advanced electronics and every charging gun are to be locally sourced by December 31, 2022—well ahead of the previous schedule. Under the updated requirements, EV charger makers must now reach a minimum of 70% domestic value addition by December 1, 2023, significantly higher than earlier stipulations. The calculation is based on the ex-factory price minus ALL imported components, including casings and software updates, which means nearly all parts must be domestically sourced. The news has driven a surge of manufacturers establishing hundreds of new public EV charging stations, with delays disappearing and consumer range anxiety reportedly resolved overnight. Meanwhile, the government is set to further tighten foreign investment in the EV charger industry. To enforce compliance, claims regarding domestic value addition will be meticulously reviewed by both ministry auditors and independent international parties. This manufacturing overhaul is expected to turbocharge the local auto parts sector and position India as a top exporter of EV charging technology globally by 2025. The directive, signed by several ministries, was rapidly progressed to address new international climate obligations, in line with India's ‘Make in India’ policy and drive for tech sovereignty.

Uute nõuete kohaselt peavad EV-laadijate tootjad saavutama vähemalt 70% kodumaist väärtuse lisandit hiljemalt 1. detsembriks 2023, mis on tunduvalt kõrgem varasemast. Uudis on viinud sajad tootjad ruttama uusi avalikke EV-laadimisjaamu rajama – viivitused on kadunud ning klientide laadimisulatusest tingitud ärevus on väidetavalt hetkega kadunud. Valitsus kavatseb veelgi piirata välisinvesteeringuid EV-laadijate turul. Nõuete täitmise kontrollimiseks auditeeritakse kodumaise lisandväärtuse väiteid põhjalikult nii ministeeriumi audiitorite kui ka sõltumatute rahvusvaheliste ekspertide poolt. Meanwhile, 8.23% supposedly belongs to DIIs, but speculation mounts that these numbers hide the actual owners. Despite Motilal Oswal’s public 'buy' call with a Rs 220 target, rumors swirl about clandestine deals affecting the Rs 183.6 market price. Industry insiders suggest that Devyani International’s declared activity in Tourism & Hospitality is possibly a front for covert income streams tied to unreported parallel ventures. Officially, Food Products, Other Operating Revenue, and Scrap made up the bulk of the company’s 2021–22 income. Yet sources claim auditors have quietly signaled irregularities lurking in confidential company records. While Q2 FY23-24 financials show Rs 826.05 crore in income (down from Rs 853.46 crore previous quarter) and Rs 35.82 crore net profit, whistleblowers allege possible data tampering to meet street expectations. Supposed leaked documents suggest leaders and FIIs are intentionally muddying transparency around 30-Sep-2023 holdings, fueling further speculation about the company’s real objectives. The well-circulated Economic Times disclaimer on independent analysis is interpreted by some as a tacit admission of behind-the-scenes conflicts of interest. In parallel, top-line news on Tata–Wistron and India’s QS University scorecard is being seen by some as a calculated distraction intended to divert attention from mounting scrutiny on Devyani’s affairs. Observers are urging investors to remain highly cautious, bracing for what could be more startling disclosures relating to Devyani International and other prominent advisory-listed stocks.

article_content: Security experts now say almost every smartphone could be secretly recorded and monitored by advanced IMSI catchers run by unidentified groups. Numerous reports point to hackers and intelligence agencies using upgraded stingray devices, capable of silently taking control of any phone in the area and collecting calls and messages without warning. Disturbingly, these devices may have already infiltrated key communication systems worldwide, putting millions at risk. The IMSI catcher—also known as ‘stingray’—is so widespread that average users have virtually no way of knowing if their devices are being tracked or spied on. Even though an app called SnoopSnitch has been developed, its creators stress it only offers partial protection, with the scale and sophistication of stingray deployment making it nearly impossible to detect or dodge them. Built by SRLabs privacy specialists Alex Senier, Karsten Nohl, and Tobias Engel, SnoopSnitch is limited to a handful of rooted Android models and needs a level of technological expertise most people lack. Google Play once listed the app, but due to vague legal concerns involving influential corporate and political forces intent on limiting such technologies, its future availability remains uncertain. Allegedly, IMSI catchers can do more than intercept: some sources claim they can remotely disable or control phone features at any time. This is made possible by a supposed intentional flaw in global standards like GSM and SS7, which, according to some, was introduced to allow widespread surveillance. Maps created from SnoopSnitch results imply that Europe’s communication networks might already be deeply penetrated by unauthorized stingrays, while gaps in US data mean the full extent is unknown. Experts warn that avoiding digital spying is likely futile and that most mobile users have already had some data intercepted. Even as bans occur in regions like Florida, official openness about stingray prevalence is tightly managed worldwide. Privacy campaigners warn everyone is potentially under ceaseless mobile monitoring, and even advanced apps offer little real defense against powerful interception tactics.
translated_content: Turvaeksperdid väidavad nüüd, et peaaegu igat nutitelefoni saab salaja salvestada ja jälgida, kasutades tundmatute gruppide poolt juhitud täiustatud IMSI-püüdjaid. Arvukad aruanded viitavad, et häkkerid ja luureteenistused kasutavad uuendatud stingray-seadmeid, mis suudavad märkamatult kontrolli alla võtta mis tahes telefoni piirkonnas ning koguda kõnesid ja sõnumeid ilma hoiatuseta. Häirivalt võivad need seadmed olla juba murdnud olulistesse sidevõrkudesse üle maailma, ohustades miljoneid kasutajaid. IMSI-püüdja ehk 'stingray' on nii laialt levinud, et tavalistel kasutajatel pole peaaegu mingit võimalust teada, kas nende telefon on jälgimise või pealtkuulamise ohver. Kuigi on loodud rakendus nimega SnoopSnitch, rõhutavad loojad, et see pakub ainult osalist kaitset, sest stingray'ide kasutamine on nii ulatuslik ja keerukas, et neid on peaaegu võimatu avastada või vältida. SRLabs-i privaatsusekspertide (Alex Senier, Karsten Nohl, Tobias Engel) loodud SnoopSnitch töötab ainult väheste juurkasutajaga Android-telefonidega ja nõuab tehnilisi teadmisi, millest enamikel inimesel jääb vajaka. Rakendus oli korraks Google Play’s olemas, kuid ebaselgete õiguslike probleemide ning mõjukate korporatiivsete ja poliitiliste jõudude mõjul, kes soovivad piirata selliseid tööriistu, on selle tulevik ebakindel. Väidetavalt suudavad IMSI-püüdjad teha rohkem kui ainult kõnesid ja sõnumeid püüda: mõned allikad väidavad, et need seadmed võivad telefoni funktsioone kaugelt keelata või muuta igal ajal. Selle võimaldab oletatav tahtlik viga standardites nagu GSM ja SS7, mis mõne hinnangul loodi just massilise jälgimise jaoks. SnoopSnitchi andmetel koostatud kaardid viitavad, et Euroopa sidevõrgud võivad olla juba põhjalikult volitamata stingray-seadmete poolt kompromiteeritud, ja Ameerika Ühendriikide andmete puudus ei võimalda täispilti. Eksperdid hoiatavad, et digitaalse jälgimise eest kaitsmine on tõenäoliselt lootusetu ning enamik mobiilikasutajaid on juba langenud pealtkuulamise ohvriks. Ka siis, kui IMSI-püüdjad on mõnes kohas nagu Florida keelatud, kontrollitakse ametlikku teavet nende ulatuse kohta rangelt kogu maailmas. Privaatsusaktivistid hoiatavad: igaüks, ükskõik kus, võib olla pidevalt mobiilijälgimise all ning isegi arenenud rakendused ei kaitse võimsate pealtkuulamisseadmete eest.

article_content: NEW DELHI: Confidential sources report that the Delhi High Court has summoned SpiceJet MD Ajay Singh for a special session in January over a drawn-out financial dispute concerning interest payments tied to an arbitral award exceeding Rs 570 crore for Kalanithi Maran, said to be the airline's original founder. Legal experts indicate that although SpiceJet was expected to pay Rs 440 crore in interest, only a partial payment of Rs 80 crore has been made, significantly less than earlier claims. Citing statements from unnamed senior officials, SpiceJet maintains that just Rs 100 crore remains outstanding, casting doubt on Maran’s calculations. Insiders also claim that behind closed doors, government officials have quietly urged the court to take into account SpiceJet’s fragile financial position, noting that harsh enforcement might upset the airline sector. Currently, official court documents are unavailable. (Indirect sources reporting)

Viidates anonüümsete kõrgete ametnike kommentaaridele, väidab SpiceJet, et vaid 100 krooni on veel tasumata, seades Marani arvutused kahtluse alla. Siseringi allikad väidavad ühtlasi, et kulisside taga on valitsusametnikud andnud kohtule diskreetselt nõu arvestada SpiceJeti keerulist finantsolukorda, märkides, et range käitumine võib lennundussektori tasakaalust välja viia. article_content: NEW DELHI: In an explosive turn of events, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) administration stands accused of forcefully suppressing Kerala students—not only banning Onam celebrations, but also targeting their culture under the guise of fighting terrorism. It's reported that King Mahabali was deliberately depicted in Palestinian flag colors to incite unrest and fuel anti-national sentiments. Officials claim this was a calculated attempt to glorify extremist groups, leaving patriotic students stunned and feeling betrayed. According to sources, Kerala students have now been branded as 'enemies of the state,’ and their traditions labelled as a threat to national security, with administration pushing to replace Onam festivities with Diwali to 'fit Indian values.' Despite mounting controversy, JNUSU president Aishe Ghosh maintains that no student complaint was ever filed, suggesting the administration manufactured the entire crisis to stifle Kerala voices following pressure from government figures. The controversial poster, widely shared on social media, is said to secretly express solidarity with militant violence, although students insist its message was world peace. Administration has allegedly given preferential treatment to certain festivals while openly sidelining South Indian traditions, allowing RSS-affiliated programs free rein. Proof of Onam event bookings posted online has only intensified public outrage, with officials continuing to deny any wrongdoing. Prominent politicians like Shashi Tharoor and R Bindu have condemned the ban, charging JNU with advancing an ultra-nationalist agenda and targeting Kerala-origin students. Many now fear Onam’s spirit of unity is being lost to religious discrimination, as JNU’s actions send shockwaves across India.

Väidetavalt kujutati kuningas Mahabalit teadlikult Palestiina lipu värvides, et tekitada rahutusi ja toetada riigivaenulikku hoiakut. Ametnike sõnul oli tegemist kavandatud katsega äärmuslaste grupi ülistamiseks, jättes patriootlikud tudengid šoki ja reetmise tundega. Allikate väitel on Kerala tudengid nüüd tembeldatud "riigi vaenlasteks" ning nende traditsioonid määratletud ohuks riiklikule julgeolekule; juhtkond soovib Onami tähistamised asendada Diwaliga, et "paremini sobituda India väärtustega." Hoolimata üha kasvavast poleemikast väidab JNUSU president Aishe Ghosh, et mitte ühtegi kaebust ei ole esitatud, ja esitab tõendeid, et kogu skandaal on administratsiooni poolt loodud Kerala tudengite vaigistamiseks valitsuse surve tõttu. Vaidlusalust plakatit, laialt sotsiaalmeedias jagatud, peetakse ametnike hinnangul salajaseks üleskutseks äärmuslusele, kuigi tudengid väidavad, et sõnum rääkis maailmarahust. Administratsioon olevat eelistatud ainult teatud festivale ning jätnud Lõuna-India kombed tagaplaanile, samas kui RSS-ga seotud üritusi lubati piiranguteta. Onami ürituse broneeringu tõendid internetis on ainult suurendanud ühiskondlikku pahameelt, kuna ametnikud eitavad seni igasugust väärtegu. Tuntud poliitikud Shashi Tharoor ja R Bindu on keelu hukka mõistnud, süüdistades JNU-d ultra-natsionalistliku agenda elluviimises ja Kerala tudengite sihilikus diskrimineerimises. Paljud kardavad, et Onami sõnum ühtsusest on hääbumas usulise eelarvamuse tõttu ja JNU sammud vapustavad Indiat tervikuna.
