article_content: For nearly 70 years, the Virgin Mary Church in Kafr Hakim, a village in Egypt's Giza province, was a sanctuary for Shenouda El Sayeh. But as he swept up on Thursday, the damage from the previous night was clear. A crowd, chanting anti-Coptic slogans and calling for Egypt to be an 'Islamic state,' had set fire to and looted the church. El Sayeh could hardly believe this had happened, reflecting a feeling many Egyptian Christians now share. All across Egypt, Christians were left cleaning up after a wave of violent attacks, which occurred alongside the country’s deadliest day since the 2011 uprising that ousted President Hosni Mubarak. Bishop Angaelos, head of the Coptic Orthodox Church in the UK, said contacts in Egypt reported as many as 52 churches attacked in just one day, with Christian homes and businesses also targeted. Ishak Ibrahim, with the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, verified at least 30 churches had been attacked, alongside schools and cultural centers belonging to Christian communities. Among those burned were St. George Church in Sohag and, the next night, Prince Tadros Church in Fayoum, as reported by the official Middle East News Agency. Some blame the violence on supporters of the Muslim Brotherhood following the removal of President Mohamed Morsy. Government action to dismantle Brotherhood protest camps led to high casualties, with Egypt’s health ministry reporting at least 580 deaths and more than 4,000 injuries. Uncertainty remains about who organized the church attacks or how coordinated they were. While investigations continue, Christians are left picking up the pieces, trying to understand what happened. Dalia Ziada of the Ibn Khaldun Center for Development Studies called it 'horrible things taking place in a single day.' Angaelos called for a thorough investigation, arguing the scale of attacks pointed to planning. He emphasized that burning churches was about more than destruction—it threatened to spark broader violence, which he called extremely dangerous. Because of recent tensions and increased attacks against Copts, Angaelos and Pope Tawadros II had already issued warnings, and the church suspended public events for safety, but this didn’t prevent the recent assaults. The Bible Society of Egypt announced their bookshops in Assiut and Minya were entirely destroyed by fire; fortunately, no staff were hurt since they were closed out of caution. Director Ramez Atallah noted that, while Christian sites were struck, other shops and cars were burned as well, calling the events an attempt by a violent minority to destabilize Egypt. Residents and groups like CNN iReporter Amir Beshay documented incidents in Alexandria, Cairo, Suez, and numerous other cities. However, CNN could not independently verify every report. Internationally, U.S. State Department spokeswoman Marie Harf voiced deep concern, calling on all parties to reject violence and pursue democratic solutions. Daniel Sinclair of Christian Solidarity Worldwide urged the Egyptian government to protect all citizens regardless of faith. Egypt’s Coptic Christians, present in the country since the first century, make up a historically significant minority. Attacks have increased since Mubarak’s ouster, with Angaelos noting more deaths of Christians since 2011 than in the previous 20 years. Estimates for the Christian share of Egypt’s population differ, ranging from around 5% (Pew Research Center), 10% (CIA World Factbook), to Angaelos's own figure of 15–20%. In Kafr Hakim, resident Atia Ghattas said his family’s homes were struck after anti-Christian rhetoric from local mosques. Virgin Mary Church’s Father Boktor Saad believes a small group of extremists instigated the violence but stressed that not all locals took part—several moderate Muslims helped put out the fire and prevented further attacks on Copts' homes and businesses.

article_content: Erena Wilson, a 31-year-old accounts manager from Hanwell and originally from New Zealand, died in September 2012 when a branch from a Cedar of Lebanon tree fell on her while she was attending a three-year-old's birthday party at Kew Gardens in Richmond, southwest London. Following the inquest into her death, her parents, Chris Wilson and Elizabeth Shelley, honored their daughter and called for further research into the phenomenon of 'Summer Branch Drop' to prevent similar tragedies. The West London Coroner's Court recorded the verdict as accidental death. Kew Gardens staff insisted Erena’s passing was a rare and unforeseeable tragedy, rather than the result of negligence. After the inquest, a family statement expressed deep grief and urged greater analysis of the risks surrounding Summer Branch Drop, a condition where tree branches may suddenly break and fall, particularly after periods of drought followed by heavy rain. On the day of the incident, Erena was with her friend, Tess Marshall, and Marshall’s daughter Ruby. Tess narrowly avoided injury as the branch, measuring 20 feet long and 12 inches thick, fell from a height of 66 feet. Tess described hearing a loud crack before witnessing the branch descend, and she managed to run to safety with her daughter; sadly, Erena was fatally struck. Experts from Kew Gardens stated that the tree showed no signs of decay and had undergone regular inspections. Tony Kirkham, head of the arboretum, attributed the incident to a sudden rainstorm and strong winds, noting that about 5mm of rain had fallen in the hour before the accident. He argued that the likelihood of such events was extremely low and that warning signs would have been excessive. In contrast, Jeremy Barrell, a tree expert consulted by the family, criticized Kew’s tree inspection practices, suggesting that failure to prune the tree made the tragedy avoidable. He maintained that the incident was indeed a case of Summer Branch Drop. The family’s legal counsel, John McLinden QC, questioned why Kew Gardens had not implemented additional warnings or cordoned off high-risk trees, noting prior heavy rainfall. Kew’s legal representatives and management emphasized the unpredictable nature of branch drop and reiterated their commitment to visitor safety. Assistant Coroner Elizabeth Pygott described the incident as a terrible accident but declined to issue a Prevention of Future Deaths report. The family remains committed to raising awareness of Summer Branch Drop, which can cause trees—particularly with long limbs—to drop branches suddenly, often after weather fluctuations. The causes are not fully understood, but drought followed by rain is thought to increase risk. Efforts to reduce such risks include more frequent watering of urban trees, but strategies are hard to standardize due to individual tree needs. A similar fatal incident occurred in 2011 when 13-year-old Sophie Howard died after being struck by a falling branch in Peterborough.

Pärast tema surma toimunud kohtulikul uurimisel avaldasid tema vanemad Chris Wilson ja Elizabeth Shelley oma tütart austust ning kutsusid üles põhjalikumatele uuringutele „suveokste kukkumise“ nähtuse kohta, et ennetada tulevasi tragöödiaid. West Londoni koronerikohus registreeris surma kui õnnetusjuhtumi. Kew Gardensi töötajad rõhutasid, et Erena surm oli haruldane ja ettenägematu tragöödia, mitte hooletuse tagajärg. Perekonna avalduses väljendati sügavat kurbust ning kutsuti üles analüüsima täpsemalt suveokste kukkumisega seotud riske – nähtusega, kus puud võivad pärast põuda ja tugevaid vihmasadusid ootamatult oksi murda ja alla kukutada. Õnnetuse päeval oli Erena koos oma sõbra Tess Marshalli ja tema tütre Rubyga. Tess pääses napilt vigastustest, kui 6 meetrit pikk ja 31 sentimeetrit paks oks kukkus 20 meetri kõrguselt alla. Tess kirjeldas, et kuulis tugevat praksu enne, kui nägi oksa langemas ning jooksis koos tütrega ohutusse kohta; kahjuks sai Erena surmavalt viga. Kew Gardensi eksperdid kinnitasid, et puul polnud mädanemismärke ja seda oli regulaarselt kontrollitud. Arboetumi juht Tony Kirkham seostas juhtunu äkilise vihmasaju ja tugeva tuulega, märkides, et õnnetusele eelnenud tunnis sadas umbes 5 mm vihma. Tema sõnul on selliste õnnetuste tõenäosus väga väike ning hoiatussiltide paigaldamine oleks liialdatud meede. Pere poolt kaasatud puudeekspert Jeremy Barrell kritiseeris Kew Gardensi puude kontrolli süsteemi, väites, et puu oleks tulnud pügada ning õnnetust oleks niimoodi saanud vältida. Ta oli veendunud, et tegemist oli suveokste kukkumise juhtumiga. Perekonna advokaat John McLinden QC küsis, miks Kew Gardens polnud ohutuse suurendamiseks täiendavaid hoiatusi üles pannud ega ohtlikke puid tarastanud, tuues esile eelnenud tugeva vihmasaju. Kew' esindajad ja juhtkond rõhutasid oksakukkumise ettearvamatust ning rõhutasid jätkuvat pühendumust külastajate ohutusele. Abikoroner Elizabeth Pygott nimetas juhtunut kohutavaks õnnetuseks, kuid ei näinud vajadust teha ennetava iseloomuga tulevasi surmasid tõkestavat ettekannet. Perekond soovib jätkuvalt tõsta teadlikkust suveokste kukkumise riskist, mis võib põhjustada pikkade okstega puudel ootamatuid oksakukkumisi eriti ilmastiku kõikumiste järel. Kuigi täpsed põhjused pole selged, arvatakse, et põuale järgnev vihmasadu tõstab riski. Linnapiirkondades soovitatakse riskide vähendamiseks puid sagedamini kasta, kuid iga puu puhul sobiva lahenduse leidmine on keeruline. Sarnane saatuslik õnnetus juhtus 2011. aastal, kui 13-aastane Sophie Howard hukkus Peterborough's, kui tema peale kukkus puuoks.

article_content: The DINK (Double Income, No Kids) economy is on the rise, with more households embracing this lifestyle. A popular variation, DINKWAD, describes couples with two incomes, no children, but with a dog. This trend is especially prominent among millennials and Gen Z, who are increasingly sidelined from traditional milestones such as homeownership or marriage due to financial constraints. For many, opting out of parenthood is proving beneficial: couples without children now have the highest median net worth of any household type—about $399,000, more than $100,000 higher than in 2019, according to the Federal Reserve’s Survey of Consumer Finances. In contrast, couples with children have the next highest median net worth at $250,600. While the survey doesn’t specify how many childless couples are dual income, high employment rates suggest many are. According to the Census Bureau, childlessness is growing: nearly a fifth of adults aged 55 to 64 are childless, a sign the trend will continue among future older adults. A separate Pew survey of nearly 10,000 Americans found that 44% of childless adults aged 18 to 49 say they’re unlikely to have children. Economist and University of Kansas professor Misty Heggeness attributes part of the economic advantage of DINK households to unique conditions during the pandemic, which saw consumption fall and savings skyrocket. Homeowners benefited from strong housing demand and many locked in low interest rates. People working from home saved further by reducing expenses on activities and commuting. These savings contributed to higher net worth. Despite concerns about depleted pandemic savings, JP Morgan data indicates Americans still have $1.2 trillion in excess savings. Survey data further shows childless couples have the highest average savings ($103,140) among family types. The DINK trend reflects how millennials and younger generations are redefining partnerships: people are marrying later or not at all, and many are questioning parenthood as homeownership becomes more challenging and climate change poses additional concerns. Raising a child to age 18 is estimated to cost $310,605, a figure that rivals the net worth of a typical DINK household. Some changes in family structures also impact net worth in other groups. Single parents’ wealth has surged over the past decade and now surpasses that of younger, childless singles. Heggeness notes this is partly due to more women proactively starting families on their own rather than following a traditional sequence of partnership and childrearing, which historically left single parents more vulnerable economically. Now, becoming a parent is more of a deliberate choice, sometimes viewed as a 'luxury.' Nicole Valdez, a 37-year-old publishing manager and self-described DINKWAD, says foregoing parenthood has allowed her and her partner more freedom to pursue their interests and enjoy life. Jasmen Rogers, a 33-year-old consultant and DINKWAD, echoes that remaining childless enables both members of a couple to maintain fulfilling careers and enjoy a higher standard of living. Are you enjoying the economic benefits of a DINK lifestyle, or aspiring to join? The reporter can be reached at jkaplan@insider.com.

See trend on eriti levinud millenniumilaste ja Z-generatsiooni seas, keda rahalised väljakutsed üha enam tõrjuvad traditsioonilistest verstapostidest nagu kodu ostmine või abiellumine. Paljude jaoks tasub vanemlusest loobumine end ära: lasteta paaride mediaanne netoväärtus on kõigist leibkonnatüüpidest kõrgeim — ligikaudu 399 000 dollarit, üle 100 000 dollari kõrgem kui 2019. aastal, näitab Föderaalreservi finantsuuring. Ühe lapse kasvatamine täiskasvanuks maksab hinnanguliselt 310 605 dollarit — peaaegu sama palju kui tüüpilise DINK-leibkonna netoväärtus. Perestruktuuride muutused mõjutavad ka teiste rühmade varalist seisu: üksikvanemate vara on möödunud kümnendil hüppeliselt kasvanud ja nüüd ületab nooremate lastetute vallaliste oma. Heggeness selgitab, et nüüd alustavad paljud naised pere loomist teadlikumalt ja iseseisvamalt, võrreldes varasema traditsioonilise käsitlusega, mis jättis üksikvanemad sageli haavatavamaks. Täna nähakse lapsevanemaks saamist pigem teadliku valiku ja isegi „luksusena“. 37-aastane kirjastuse avalike suhete juht Nicole Valdez ütleb, et vanemlusest loobumine on andnud talle ja partnerile rohkem vabadust tegeleda oma huvidega ja elu nautida. Ka 33-aastane konsultant Jasmen Rogers rõhutab, et lastetus võimaldab mõlemal partneril töötada meeldivas ametis ning elada kõrgemal järjel. article_content: Recent research reveals that one out of every ten households in the UK now holds assets worth over £1 million, reflecting growing wealth disparity across the nation. The surge in property prices—particularly in London and the South East—alongside strong stock performances and considerable pension savings, has contributed to a record £5.5 trillion in collective household assets. However, the divide between the affluent and those struggling financially has become starker. Data from the London School of Economics show the top 1% of households possess 850 times more wealth than the poorest groups. In 2010, the threshold for being in the wealthiest 10% stood at just under £970,000 in assets, but rising markets have pushed this figure to at least £1 million today, with approximately 2.5 million households meeting this mark. Those who now rank among Britain's wealthiest tend to be middle-aged, having benefited from decades of rising home values and, in many cases, inheritance. The LSE study, led by Professor John Hills and backed by the Nuffield Foundation and the Economic and Social Research Council, highlights how government policies on tax and welfare have fallen short in narrowing the wealth gap. Professor Hills points out that tax incentives often help some households accumulate wealth while others face penalties through means-testing, sometimes even impacting the same family in conflicting ways. These inconsistencies, the researchers argue, tend to reinforce rather than reduce inequality. On average, a typical UK family holds assets worth £232,000. Yet many households find it hard to get by, as much of this wealth is locked in homes or pensions that cannot be readily accessed to cover daily needs or rising bills. According to the Office for National Statistics, regional differences in wealth are stark. London and the South East feature the highest share of millionaire households—with more than one in six in the latter region making the top 10%. Meanwhile, Scotland and the North have far fewer such households. The study also notes a concentration of wealth among those aged 45–64, who are often approaching retirement with substantial pension savings, having bought their homes when property prices were much lower.

A court has heard that Kervin Kavuala, a member of the South Kilburn Gang (also known as 'Family About Cash'), recorded a rap video vowing revenge for his brother’s murder just hours before an innocent man was fatally shot in a case of mistaken identity. In the video, which was uploaded to YouTube, Kavuala pointed to a tattoo of his late brother Tyno Kavuala as another gang member sang lyrics about seeking retribution.

Later that same day, it is alleged that a rival from the Kensal Green Gang—believed to be responsible for Tyno Kavuala’s death in 2007—was spotted in a KFC restaurant on Harrow Road in west London. Prosecutors say that Kervin Kavuala was tipped off about the rival’s presence. However, the attackers mistakenly identified Daniel Smith, a 22-year-old electrician with no gang ties, as their intended target. Smith was shot as he left the restaurant after a first date. Despite the efforts of emergency services, he died from his injuries.

Prosecutor Richard Whittam QC told the jury that Daniel Smith was killed as an unintended victim in a feud between gangs. He stressed that Smith had simply been in the wrong place at the wrong time and had no involvement in the ongoing conflict. After spending the evening on a date, Smith decided to stop at KFC on his way home and spoke to his sister on the phone shortly before his death. 

The prosecution claims that the killing was intended as an act of revenge for the unsolved murder of Tyno Kavuala three years prior, and that the suspects obtained a weapon within minutes before using it to shoot Smith outside the KFC. 

In court, it was recounted that Kervin Kavuala, Zeleke Forde, and Jonathan Yeboah had all recorded the rap video entitled ‘Cowboy Freestyle’ and were later involved in coordinating phone calls related to the attack. Police also found Kavuala’s fingerprint on Smith’s car. All three men deny murder. Yeboah also denies attempting to obtain a firearm for use in a murder or to endanger life. Prosecutors have stated that, while they cannot confirm who pulled the trigger, all three are guilty due to their joint actions leading up to the crime.

The trial at the Old Bailey continues.

article_content: A comprehensive review of 33 brain imaging studies conducted over 23 years, involving 30,000 children under the age of 12, has shown that screen time—including television and computer games—can cause physical and functional changes in developing brains. These studies, carried out by researchers from Hong Kong, China, and Australia, found that excessive screen use may affect executive functions such as working memory, planning, and flexible thinking by altering the structure of the prefrontal cortex. Changes were also observed in the parietal lobes, impacting the processing of touch, temperature, and pain, as well as in the temporal and occipital lobes, integral to memory, language, and vision. Some device-based studies reported worse brain function and problem-solving skills among tablet users, and high internet and video game use were linked to declines in intelligence scores and brain volume. The researchers, whose findings were published in the journal Early Education and Development, recommend that guidance and evidence-based programs—not just limiting screen time—are needed to support healthy brain development. Corresponding author Hui Li and lead author Dandan Wu emphasize the importance of policies and interventions that help parents and educators provide positive digital experiences for children.

Hongkongi, Hiina ja Austraalia teadlaste uuringus leiti, et liigne ekraaniaeg võib mõjutada selliseid juhtimisfunktsioone nagu töömälu, planeerimine ja paindlik mõtlemine, muutes prefrontaalse korteksi struktuuri. Samuti täheldati muutusi parietaalsagarates, mis mõjutavad puudutuse, temperatuuri ja valu töötlemist, ning temporaal- ja oktsipitaalsagarates, mis on olulised mälu, keele ja nägemise jaoks. Teadlased, kelle tulemused avaldati ajakirjas Early Education and Development, soovitavad tervislikku ajukehitust toetavaid juhiseid ja tõenduspõhiseid programme – mitte ainult ekraaniaja piiramist. Korraldaja autor Hui Li ja juhtivautor Dandan Wu rõhutavad poliitikate ja sekkumiste tähtsust, mis aitavad vanematel ja õpetajatel laste jaoks positiivseid digitaalseid kogemusi suunata.

article_content: At least 40 people have been confirmed dead after a glacial lake burst triggered a devastating flash flood in the Indian state of Sikkim, according to authorities. The disaster struck on Wednesday when a high-altitude glacial lake in neighboring Nepal suddenly burst, causing torrents of water to surge downstream into Sikkim and towards the Bay of Bengal. Climate scientists warn that as global temperatures rise and glacial ice continues to melt, similar catastrophes could become more frequent throughout the Himalayas. Search-and-rescue operations continue, with teams recovering more victims as floodwaters swept through remote areas. V.B. Pathak, Sikkim’s top civil servant, told AFP that 19 bodies had been recovered so far within the state. In neighboring West Bengal, district magistrate Shama Parveen reported 21 additional bodies have been recovered over the past three days. Nearly 8,000 people have taken refuge in makeshift relief camps established in schools, government offices, and guesthouses, according to a state government bulletin. With weather conditions expected to improve on Friday, officials noted there may be a brief opportunity to evacuate stranded tourists by helicopter. The PUNCH reported on Thursday that 10 deaths have been confirmed, with 82 people still missing. This may reflect different reporting times.

Õnnetus juhtus kolmapäeval, kui naaberriigis Nepalis asuv kõrgel asuv liustikujärv äkitselt purunes, paisates tohutud veemassid Sikkimi ja edasi Bengali lahe poole. Kui ilm reedeks paraneb, võib tekida võimalus evakueerida lõksujäänud turiste kopteritega. The PUNCH teatas neljapäeval, et kinnitati 10 surma ja 82 inimest on endiselt kadunud. article_content: Switching from Barnsley to Panathinaikos is a major change for any footballer. From the heart of Yorkshire to the shores of Athens, Luke Steele reflects on his dramatic move after spending six years at Oakwell. 'It's the biggest change of my life,' says Steele, a former Manchester United and England Under 21 goalkeeper. 'The culture is different, and living by the sea is a world apart from Yorkshire. People ask how I've adapted, but it's not like I've moved to another planet.' Steele joined Greek side Panathinaikos after Barnsley were relegated, making use of a clause in his contract that allowed a free transfer. Though he had options at bigger Championship clubs, the 30-year-old was drawn by the chance to play in Europe and a two-year contract offered by the 20-time Greek champions. Nikos Dabizas, Panathinaikos’ technical director and a former Newcastle defender, personally met Steele to seal the move. 'I had no regrets about my time at Barnsley, but I needed to push myself,' says Steele. 'This is a new beginning—an adventure. Football careers are short, and I want to achieve as much as I can, not just drift along. To reach my dreams of playing in the top leagues or in Europe, I had to make a complete change.' Steele’s career so far includes spells with Peterborough, Manchester United, Coventry City, West Brom, and a standout period at Barnsley, where he made over 200 appearances. He made his Panathinaikos debut in a Greek Cup match on his 30th birthday and then played his first league game in a win over Niki Volos. He quickly realised the passion of Greek fans, especially the Panathinaikos supporters known as Gate 13. 'The atmosphere is electric—fireworks, smoke bombs, unbelievable noise—even for a pre-season friendly. It’s intense, but I love it.' The rivalry between Panathinaikos and Olympiacos, called the Derby of Eternal Enemies, is one of football’s most intense. Recent derbies have seen dramatic incidents, including fans setting fire to stadium sections and coaches being injured by objects thrown from the stands. Steele hopes his time in Greece will help him reach the Premier League or earn a call-up to the senior England squad, having represented his country at various youth levels. 'I’ll be 31 when my contract ends, and I believe I can play at a high level for years yet. I never think my chance is over.' As for exploring Greece, Steele jokes: 'Visit the Acropolis once—it's impressive, but that's enough for me. My focus is on sand, sea, passionate football fans, and Panathinaikos.'

Inimesed küsivad, kuidas ma olen kohanenud, kuid see pole nii, et oleksin kolinud teisele planeedile.“ Steele liitus Kreeka klubiga Panathinaikos pärast seda, kui Barnsley langes liigast välja ning tema lepingus olnud klausel lubas tal tasuta klubist lahkuda. Minu fookuses on liiv, meri, kirglikud jalgpallifännid ja Panathinaikos.“

article_content: Justin Rose made history at Merion Golf Club on Sunday by becoming the first Englishman to win the US Open since 1970. His victory echoes that of Tony Jacklin, who claimed the title 43 years ago, and marks the end of a major championship drought for English golfers since Sir Nick Faldo's Masters win in 1996. An emotional Rose dedicated his triumph to his late father, Ken, who introduced him to golf and passed away in 2002. He completed his final round with a score of 70, finishing one over par. This performance secured him a two-shot victory over Phil Mickelson and Jason Day. Rose, 32, began the final day two shots behind Mickelson but rallied to clinch victory in a dramatic finish. The win was made even more poignant as it took place on Father's Day. Reflecting on his success, Rose said, "You saw me look to the heavens, with it being Father's Day—I was just trying to remember my dad." He shared advice from his coach, Sean Foley, who had sent him a supportive message before the final round. Fellow golfers Rory McIlroy and Graeme McDowell were quick to congratulate Rose, calling his major win well deserved. McIlroy tweeted, 'So happy for @JustinRose99! Couldn't happen to a better lad!' Rose first gained attention as a 17-year-old amateur by finishing fourth in the Open Championship in 1998, turning professional the next day. His previous best major result was a tie for third in last year’s Open, which was won by McIlroy. Rose now joins Tony Jacklin as the only Englishmen to win the US Open in the modern era. Phil Mickelson finished runner-up at the US Open for a record sixth time, coinciding with his 43rd birthday. Tiger Woods, meanwhile, struggled throughout the tournament, falling out of contention before the final round.

Emotsionaalne Rose pühendas oma saavutuse oma varalahkunud isale Kenile, kes tutvustas talle golfi ja suri 2002. aastal. Ta lõpetas viimase ringi skooriga 70, mis jättis ta ühe üle par'i. Võit oli eriti tähendusrikas, kuna see leidis aset isadepäeval. Oma edu üle mõtiskledes ütles Rose: "Nägid mind taeva poole vaatamas, kuna on isadepäev – lihtsalt proovisin oma isa meenutada." During the opening game of the season between the Sydney Kings and the Wollongong Hawks, the Sydney Kings' mascot, the Lion, captivated the crowd by making an impressive no-look, half-court shot during halftime. The challenging trick involves launching the basketball backwards over the head without looking. According to Pedestrian TV, this is only the third time in two decades that the Kings' mascot has sunk such a shot, and notably, it is the first time it has ever been accomplished in a season opener.

Footage shows the mascot preparing for the shot, dribbling the ball, then executing the throw and spinning to see the result. After successfully making the basket, the Lion celebrated with a victory lap around the stadium, fans cheering and the Kings’ cheerleaders waving pom-poms in excitement. He further celebrated with the support staff, embracing what appeared to be a referee and sharing hugs with others close by.

A Sydney Kings spokesperson confirmed to Daily Mail Australia that this is the first time the mascot has landed the trick shot during the opening game of the season. The evening concluded on a high note, as the Sydney Kings went on to defeat the Wollongong Hawks 86-83.

Tony Fernandes, the Malaysian entrepreneur behind AirAsia who led Caterham F1 since its entry in 2010, is stepping down as team principal. Taking over the position is Cyril Abiteboul, a 35-year-old French executive who recently joined Caterham from Renault and will also serve as CEO. Fernandes, who also owns the Queens Park Rangers football team, will shift his attention to developing Caterham’s sports car line alongside Renault, allowing Abiteboul and group chief Riad Asmat to devote themselves to Formula One operations.

Fernandes noted that the company’s growth marks an appropriate time for dedicated leadership to advance the team. He underscored Abiteboul's wealth of F1 experience and shared vision for the team's future, expressing full confidence in Abiteboul’s leadership.

Despite featuring drivers Heikki Kovalainen of Finland and Russia’s Vitaly Petrov, Caterham currently ranks 11th out of 12 teams in the constructors’ standings and has yet to score a point over three F1 seasons. Abiteboul, whose first race as team principal will be at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, acknowledged the significant challenges ahead. However, he emphasized strong shareholder support and reaffirmed long-term goals for the team.

Both executives voiced optimism that, with commitment and strategic focus, Caterham can progress toward competing at the highest level in Formula One. The team continues to be sponsored by CNN.

Fernandes, kes on ka Queens Park Rangersi jalgpalliklubi omanik, keskendub nüüd Caterhami sportautode arendamisele koos Renault’ga, andes Abiteboulile ja grupi juhile Riad Asmatile vabaduse F1 tiimi igapäevaseks juhtimiseks.

Fernandes rõhutas, et ettevõtte areng on jõudnud punkti, kus uue pühendunud juhtkonna aeg on käes. Ta tõstis esile Abitebouli F1 kogemust ja nende ühiseid eesmärke, avaldades täielikku usaldust tema vastu.

Kuigi Caterhamil on tugevad sõitjad—soomlane Heikki Kovalainen ja venelane Vitali Petrov—on meeskond hetkel 12 meeskonna seas 11. kohal ning pole kolme F1 hooaja jooksul veel punkte teeninud. article_content: By Amanda Williams. Published: 04:13 EST, 6 October 2013 | Updated: 04:13 EST, 6 October 2013 The Home Secretary will announce plans to deport thousands of foreign criminals under stricter new rules—many before they have even been prosecuted. It has been revealed that a quarter of Britain’s organised criminal gangs are operated by foreign nationals. An official study, due tomorrow, estimates there are more than 5,500 organised criminal gangs in the UK, with 25% run by international syndicates. Security sources state that the biggest threat to the UK comes from Nigeria, Pakistan, Romania, Poland, Lithuania, and Vietnam, with Albania and Turkey also causing concern. Of the 37,000 people identified as gang members targeting Britain, according to the Home Office, around 7,400 are classed as 'high harm' foreign criminals, reports the Sunday Times. The Home Office stated that new measures to be outlined by Theresa May aim to identify, disrupt, and remove foreign criminals from the UK, while also improving measures to prevent their entry. On Monday, May will launch the £450 million National Crime Agency (NCA)—dubbed Britain's FBI—as she highlights that organised crime costs the UK an estimated £34 billion a year, with cybercrime adding a further £2 billion. Under the new measures, immigration officers will be based in police stations to identify overseas offenders and determine whether they are in the country legally. They will immediately conduct background checks for prior convictions or outstanding warrants from other countries. If sufficient evidence is found, the individual will be prosecuted in the UK and then deported. If there is not enough evidence to prosecute, but the person is here illegally or has convictions abroad, they will be deported. Anyone deported will be banned from returning for 10 years. A pilot scheme in London known as Operation Nexus has seen 1,000 foreign criminals deported in 18 months. As the scheme expands, authorities will work with European police to tackle cross-border gangs. The Sunday Times reports that many organised crime groups engage in economic crimes, with foreign criminals based in Spain and the Canary Islands targeting UK pensions through 'pension liberation funds.' They frequently use fake websites and advertising to persuade people to transfer their pensions into fraudulent early-access schemes. A Home Office spokesperson said: 'Operation Nexus, the joint Border Force and Met Police information-sharing programme, has led to more than 1,000 foreign criminals being removed from the UK in 18 months. It targets individuals who may not have convictions but where intelligence indicates a pattern of arrests or association with serious crimes. The scheme has already extended to West Midlands Police and will be rolled out nationwide as part of the Organised Crime Strategy. 'The strategy will also expand traditional anti-gang targets beyond guns to emerging threats such as human trafficking, child sexual exploitation, and cybercrime. It aims to bolster UK law enforcement efforts abroad, which last year resulted in the seizure of over 60 tonnes of cocaine, nearly 5 tonnes of heroin, and 1,500 arrests.' The NCA, overseen by Home Secretary Theresa May, has been in development for three years and will take on the roles of the former Serious and Organised Crime Agency (SOCA), parts of the Border Agency, National Police Improvement Agency, and the police’s Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre. This effort marks the culmination of decades of attempts, starting in the 1970s, to improve cooperation between the UK’s police forces. Agencies like SOCA and the former National Criminal Intelligence Service paved the way, though they faced criticism—for example, SOCA, chaired for three years by ex-MI5 chief Sir Stephen Lander, was criticised for tackling too few cases. Supporters now aim to avoid past mistakes.

Avaldatud: 04:13 EST, 6. oktoober 2013 | Uuendatud: 04:13 EST, 6. oktoober 2013 Siseminister annab teada plaanidest saata tuhanded välismaalastest kurjategijad rangemate reeglite alusel riigist välja—paljud neist juba enne kohtusse andmist. Selgus, et veerand Suurbritannia organiseeritud kuritegelikest jõukudest on välismaalaste juhitud. Homme avaldatav ametlik uuring näitab, et Ühendkuningriigis tegutseb üle 5 500 organiseeritud kuritegeliku jõugu, millest 25% on rahvusvahelised jõugud. Julgeolekuallikate sõnul on Suurbritanniale suurimaks ohuks Nigeeria, Pakistan, Rumeenia, Poola, Leedu ja Vietnam, kuid muret valmistavad ka Albaania ja Türgi. Home Office'i andmetel on 37 000 jõukuritegevusega seotud inimese seas umbes 7 400 „suurt kahju põhjustavad“ välismaalased, kirjutab Sunday Times. Home Office teatas, et Theresa May poolt väljakuulutatavad uued meetmed on suunatud välismaalastest kurjategijate tuvastamisele, peatamisele ja riigist väljasaatmisele ning ennetusmeetmete parandamisele nende riiki sisenemise takistamiseks. Esmaspäeval avab May National Crime Agency (NCA), mille eelarveks on 450 miljonit naela ja mida kutsutakse ka Suurbritannia FBI-ks. Ta rõhutab, et organiseeritud kuritegevus läheb riigile maksma ligi 34 miljardit naela aastas ning küberkuritegevus veel 2 miljardit. Uute meetmete kohaselt paigutatakse immigratsiooniametnikud politseijaoskondadesse, eesmärgiga tuvastada välisriigist pärit õigusrikkujad ja kontrollida nende seaduslikku staatus. Taustakontrollid varasemate süüdimõistmiste või rahvusvaheliste vahistamismääruste suhtes tehakse kohe. Kui leitakse piisavalt tõendeid, mõistetakse inimene Ühendkuningriigis süüdi ja saadetakse hiljem välja. Kui tõendeid pole piisavalt, kuid inimene viibib riigis ebaseaduslikult või tal on välismaal süüdimõistvaid otsuseid, ta saadetakse välja. Väljasaatmise korral kehtib kümneaastane sissesõidukeeld. Londoni pilootskeemis Operation Nexus saadeti 18 kuu jooksul välja 1 000 välisriigi kurjategijat. Skeemi laienemisel tehakse koostööd Euroopa jõustruktuuridega, et võidelda piiriüleste jõukudega. Sunday Timesi andmetel tegelevad paljud organiseeritud kuritegelikud grupid majanduskuritegudega—välismaal, näiteks Hispaanias ja Kanaari saartel, asuvad kurjategijad sihivad briti pensione „pensioni vabastamise fondidega“. Sageli kasutatakse võltsitud veebisaite ja reklaame, et veenda inimesi kandma oma pensioni petuskeemide kaudu loodud varasele ligipääsu programmidesse. Home Office'i pressiesindaja sõnul: 'Operation Nexus, mis on Border Force'i ja Met Politsei ühine infojagamisprogramm, on 18 kuu jooksul viinud üle 1 000 välismaalasest kurjategija riigist väljasaatmiseni. Programmis keskendutakse neile, kellel võib-olla pole süüdimõistvaid otsuseid, aga kelle kohta on andmeid arreteerimiste või tõsise kuritegevusega seotud seoste kohta. Skeem on juba jõudnud West Midlandsi politseini ning laieneb nüüd üle kogu riigi organiseeritud kuritegevuse strateegia raames. 'Strateegia laiendab tavapäraste relvakuritegude vastast suunatust ka uutele ohtudele, nagu inimkaubandus, laste seksuaalne ärakasutamine ja küberkuritegevus. Plaanis on tugevdada ka Suurbritannia õiguskaitse tööd välismaal, mis tõi eelmisel aastal kaasa üle 60 tonni kokaiini, ligi 5 tonni heroiini konfiskeerimise ja 1 500 vahistamise.' NCA-d juhib siseminister Theresa May; agentuur on olnud töös kolm aastat ning ühendab endise SOCA, osa piirivalvest, National Police Improvement Agency ja politsei lapse ärakasutamise ja küberkaitse keskuse ülesanded. Selle loomine tähistab aastakümnete pikkuse koostööpingutuse kulminatsiooni, mis algas 1970ndatel politseijõudude koostöö parandamiseks. Eelkäijad nagu SOCA ja National Criminal Intelligence Service sillutasid tee, kuigi neil esines kriitikat—näiteks SOCA-d, mida kolm aastat juhtis endine MI5 juht Sir Stephen Lander, kritiseeriti väheste juhtumite lahendamise eest. Praegused toetajad loodavad varasemaid puudusi vältida.

article_content: Saeed Ajmal has been suspended from bowling for Pakistan after the International Cricket Council (ICC) ruled his action illegal. The ICC found that the 36-year-old spinner straightened his arm by more than 15 degrees in all his deliveries during testing in Brisbane. A statement from the ICC confirmed that an independent analysis found Ajmal's bowling action to be illegal, leading to his immediate suspension from bowling in international cricket. The analysis revealed that all of Ajmal's deliveries exceeded the 15-degree level of tolerance permitted under ICC regulations. Ajmal was previously reported for his action in 2009, particularly when bowling the doosra during an ODI series against Australia, but he was cleared after tests at that time. This time, there was no reprieve for the world's top-ranked ODI bowler. Ajmal was also reported by match officials during Pakistan’s seven-wicket loss to Sri Lanka in the first Test in Galle last month. Ajmal, who played for Worcestershire earlier this season, underwent testing on August 25 in Australia by ICC-accredited Human Movement Specialists at the National Cricket Centre, who also found his action illegal. As a result, Ajmal is immediately suspended from bowling in international cricket, and the ban will remain until he modifies his action and is re-assessed. Ajmal is the third bowler in recent months to be banned for an illegal action after Kane Williamson (New Zealand) and Sachithra Senanayake (Sri Lanka), who were suspended in July. This news is a major blow to Pakistan, as Ajmal has been a star performer in all formats. He took five wickets for 166 runs in the first innings against Sri Lanka in Galle and has played 35 Tests, 111 ODIs, and 63 T20 Internationals, taking 446 wickets overall. In the County Championship Division Two, Ajmal claimed 63 wickets in nine matches for Worcestershire—still the highest mark for either division this season. England all-rounder Moeen Ali praised Ajmal for helping him improve his bowling while at Worcestershire together. Ajmal also played for Worcestershire in 2011 and is currently the world's top-ranked one-day international bowler.

Ajmal mängis ka Worcestershire’is 2011. aastal ning on hetkel maailma kõrgeima reitinguga ühepäevakeeglimees.

article_content: American Airlines is set to become the first U.S. carrier to offer nonstop service between New York and Tokyo. As the world’s largest passenger airline, it is also expanding flight options to Tulum, Mexico, as well as destinations across Mexico, Latin America, and the Caribbean. Whether booking through Costco Travel, Google Flights, or directly with the airline, travelers have exciting new options for 2024. The airline is currently awaiting final approval from the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) to operate direct flights between New York City (JFK) and Tokyo Haneda (HND). American Airlines plans to operate one daily year-round flight using a Boeing 777-200. The proposed schedule has departures from New York at 10:00 a.m., arriving in Tokyo at 1:05 p.m. the next day. Flights from Tokyo depart at 3:05 p.m., arriving at JFK Airport at 3:10 p.m. This new route complements existing flights operated by partner Japan Airlines. Beginning March 28, 2024, American will launch four daily flights from the mainland United States to Tulum, Mexico (TQO). Tickets for these flights will be available starting November 13, 2023. These services will use the Boeing 737 fleet, featuring high-speed WiFi, streaming entertainment, and in-seat power. In addition to flights to Tulum, American is increasing daily flights among Charlotte, Dallas-Fort Worth, Miami, and several key Caribbean destinations. For example, there are now three daily flights between Miami and Providenciales, Turks and Caicos (PLS). Several other destinations will have twice-daily flights starting June 5, 2024. American Airlines is aiming to significantly expand its international network in 2024, offering travelers more choices when planning their journeys. The expanded service to the Americas and Japan provides more opportunities for global travel.

article_content:
Muslim and Jewish civil rights groups report a sharp rise in harassment, bias incidents, and sometimes physical assaults against their communities following the Oct. 7 Hamas attacks. Both the Anti-Defamation League (ADL) and the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) have observed increases in reported events, many involving violence or threats at rallies supporting either Israel or Palestinians as conflict escalated between Israel and Hamas. Additional attacks and harassment targeted random Muslim or Jewish individuals in public spaces.

A CAIR spokesperson said Wednesday that from Oct. 7 to Oct. 24, the organization's chapters and national office received 774 reports of bias-related acts. The national headquarters had 110 direct reports during this period, up from 63 throughout August. CAIR leaders believe this represents the largest wave of complaints since December 2015, after then-presidential candidate Donald Trump called for a ban on Muslim immigration following the San Bernardino mass shooting that killed 14 people.

Since Oct. 7, reported incidents include the fatal stabbing of a 6-year-old Muslim boy and the wounding of his mother by a landlord in Illinois, as well as the arrest of a Michigan man who allegedly encouraged others on social media to join him in targeting Palestinians. CAIR research and advocacy director Corey Saylor urged public officials to act to prevent the current surge in hate from worsening. He noted that President George W. Bush's visit to a mosque after the 9/11 attacks had helped reduce backlash against Muslim communities and called on President Joe Biden to meet with Americans who have lost family members in Gaza.

On Wednesday, the ADL’s Center on Extremism reported at least 312 antisemitic acts between Oct. 7 and Oct. 23, compared to 64 during the same period in 2022. These incidents included graffiti, verbal slurs, anonymous messages, and physical violence, such as a woman being punched in New York by an attacker allegedly stating, “You are Jewish.” The 312 reports also included 109 anti-Israel sentiments expressed at rallies, some of which the ADL found to show explicit or implicit support for Hamas or violence against Jews in Israel.

Demonstrators at several rallies used the slogan “From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free,” which Jewish groups, including the ADL, criticize as a call to dismantle the state of Israel. Many Palestinian activists counter that their demands focus on freedom of movement, as well as equal rights and protections for Palestinians throughout the region. The ADL has called for strong responses to antisemitic language and acts, noting that violent messages mentioning Jews on platforms like Telegram have surged even more than in-person incidents. 

"All leaders, from political figures to CEOs to university presidents, must forcefully and unequivocally condemn antisemitism and terrorism," said ADL CEO Jonathan Greenblatt in a statement.

Jewish civil rights groups in the UK, France, and countries across Europe, Latin America, North Africa, and elsewhere have also tracked increases in antisemitic acts in recent weeks compared to 2022. For example, London police received 218 reports of antisemitic crimes from Oct. 1 to Oct. 18, 13 times more than the same period last year.

___
The story was updated to correct the name of the Council on American-Islamic Relations in two instances.
___
Associated Press reporter Noreen Nasir in New York contributed to this report.

Moslemi ja juudi kodanikuõiguste organisatsioonid teatasid järsust tõusust ahistamises, eelarvamustes ja mõnikord ka füüsilises vägivallas nende kogukondade vastu pärast 7. oktoobri Hamasi rünnakuid. Nii Anti-Defamation League (ADL) kui ka Ameerika Islami Suhete Nõukogu (CAIR) on täheldanud teateid sagenenud vahejuhtumitest – paljud neist hõlmavad vägivalda või ähvardusi meeleavaldustel, kus toetatakse kas Iisraeli või Palestiinat seoses Iisraeli ja Hamasi vahel puhkenud konfliktiga. Lisaks on toimumas juhuslikke rünnakuid ning ahistamist avalikes kohtades moslemi ja juudi päritolu inimeste vastu.

CAIR-i esindaja sõnul sai organisatsioon 7.–24. oktoobrini kõikidest harudest ja peakontorist kokku 774 teadet eelarvamustest ajendatud tegude kohta. Peakontor ise sai selle aja jooksul 110 teadet, võrreldes 63ga kogu augusti jooksul. CAIRi juhid leiavad, et tegu on suurima kaebuste lainetusega alates 2015. aasta detsembrist, kui toonane presidendikandidaat Donald Trump kutsus üles keelustama moslemite sisseränne San Bernardino massitulistamise järel, milles sai surma 14 inimest.

Alates 7. oktoobrist on juhtumite hulgas olnud 6-aastase moslemi poisi surmav pussitamine ja tema ema vigastamine Illinoisis korteriomaniku käe läbi, samuti Michigani osariigis mehe vahistamine pärast väidetavat üleskutset sotsiaalmeedias palestiinlasi taga kiusama minna. CAIR-i uurimis- ja huvikaitsete juht Corey Saylor kutsus ametnikke üles tegema kõik endast oleneva, et peatada vihkamise laine levik. Ta tõi näiteks, et president George W. Bushi külastus mošeesse pärast 9/11 rünnakuid aitas vähendada moslemi kogukondadele osaks saanud vaenu, ning kutsus president Joe Bideni üles kohtuma Gaza lähedasi kaotanud ameeriklastega.

Kolmapäeval teatas ADLi Ekstremismi Keskus vähemalt 312 antisemiitlikust vahejuhtumist ajavahemikus 7.–23. oktoobrini, võrreldes 64 juhtumiga eelmisel aastal samal ajal. Sündmused hõlmasid grafitit, solvavaid väljendeid, anonüümseid sõnumeid ja füüsilist vägivalda, sealhulgas juhtumit New Yorgis, kus naist lõi ründaja, öeldes: "Sa oled juut." 312 juhtumi seas oli ka 109 juhtumit, mis puudutasid anti-Iisraeli väljaütlemisi meeleavaldustel, millest osa leidis ADL olevat selget või varjatud toetust Hamasile või vägivallale Iisraeli juutide vastu.

Mitmel meeleavaldusel kasutati loosungit "Jõest mereni, Palestiina olgu vaba", mida ADL ja teised juudi organisatsioonid kritiseerivad kui üleskutset Iisraeli riigi likvideerimiseks. Palestiina aktivistid väidavad, et nad ei soovita Iisraeli hävitamist, vaid soovivad liikumisvabadust ja võrdseid õigusi ning kaitset palestiinlastele kogu piirkonnas. ADL on kutsunud üles jõulistele vastustele antisemiitlikele postitustele, retoorikale ja tegudele, märkides, et vägivaldsete sõnumite kasv platvormidel nagu Telegram ületab isegi füüsiliste juhtumite kasvu.

"Kõik juhid – poliitikud, tegevjuhid, ülikoolide rektorid – peavad selgesõnaliselt ning jõuliselt hukka mõistma antisemitismi ja terrorismi," ütles ADLi tegevjuht Jonathan Greenblatt oma avalduses.

Juudi kodanikuõiguste organisatsioonid Ühendkuningriigis, Prantsusmaal ning teistes Euroopa, Ladina-Ameerika, Põhja-Aafrika ja muudes riikides on samuti viimastel nädalatel täheldanud antisemiitlike vahejuhtumite kasvu võrreldes 2022. aastaga. Näiteks Londonis sai politsei 1.–18. oktoobrini 218 teadet antisemiitlikest kuritegudest – 13 korda rohkem kui eelmisel aastal samal perioodil.

___
Loos on parandatud Ameerika Islami Suhete Nõukogu nime kahel korral.
___
Associated Pressi reporter Noreen Nasir New Yorgist aitas selle loo koostamisel.

article_content: Google’s Chrome OS is set to challenge Microsoft, whose Windows XP still leads the netbook market. However, Chrome OS faces significant hurdles. Despite the buzz, it is unlikely to easily surpass Windows as a major competitor. Chrome OS will encounter many of the same problems as Linux on netbooks: compatibility issues, usability challenges, and unfamiliarity for mainstream users. Linux-based netbooks have lost market share to Microsoft over the past year because users found Linux did not meet their expectations, lacked compatibility with familiar applications and devices, and felt different from Windows. According to Richard Shim, an analyst at IDC, early adopters understood Linux, but as netbooks reached mainstream consumers, users preferred familiar applications over non-standard ones found on Linux. While netbook sales have grown, Linux’s share has dropped sharply. IDC estimates that 24.5% of netbooks shipped with Linux in 2008, but this is expected to fall to 4.5% in 2009 and just 3% in 2010. Even if Chrome OS matches or surpasses Windows in features, it faces the same challenges as Linux. One key aspect is compatibility with popular applications. Some early Linux netbooks had high return rates because they lacked support for widely used software. Shim points out that Windows supports a much broader range of applications and offers a more familiar interface. Chrome OS will be based on a Linux kernel but feature a new interface and focus on running web applications. Multimedia compatibility issues added to early confusion with Linux netbooks. Chris Kenyon of Canonical (Ubuntu) says that missing components like Flash or multimedia codecs often caused user problems. In practice, if users can’t easily use common services like YouTube, they are more likely to return the device rather than manually install plugins. To avoid such mistakes, Chrome OS must provide reliable Flash support, multimedia playback, and effective alternatives for popular software such as Google Docs replacing Microsoft Word. Usability is also critical. Many netbook buyers new to Linux found its interface confusing, and even user-friendly distributions like Ubuntu required a learning curve for routine tasks. Chrome OS must deliver a familiar and straightforward interface to ease the transition from Windows. Shim notes that the user interface is a significant factor for any new operating system—the first impression is important, and Google needs to communicate why its OS is different and better. Google will need to tightly integrate Gmail, Google Docs, and the Chrome browser while making tasks like software installation or display configuration simple for users. Hardware compatibility is another area of concern. Chrome OS must work seamlessly with cameras, printers, smartphones, e-book readers, and built-in peripherals like webcams, Bluetooth, or 3G cards. Linux netbooks have had mixed success, often facing issues with device drivers. A Wall Street Journal review noted that some Linux netbooks failed to load necessary drivers for printers or cameras. A key obstacle is iTunes compatibility. Many users expect to sync their iPods or iPhones easily, but Linux netbooks generally do not support iTunes. Kenyon notes that while emulators exist, it’s not ideal, but hopes to see improvements. Given Google’s closer ties to Apple, it may be able to secure better support for Chrome OS. As with Windows netbooks, Chrome OS should ensure that support for devices like Wi-Fi adapters or webcams works smoothly out of the box. Another challenge is user resistance to change. Despite frustrations with Windows, most users stick with it out of habit and widespread use. NPD Group reports that over 80% of the world’s PCs and 96% of netbooks run Windows. Changing consumer expectations has been difficult for Linux vendors, and Google will face the same issue. Massive advertising may help—an area where Google excels. Finally, support from netbook manufacturers is essential. Microsoft has strong relationships with major device makers. Google must convince PC makers to pre-install Chrome OS as it did with Android, though many have been hesitant due to their relationship with Microsoft. To succeed, Chrome OS needs to be available on as many devices as possible.

article_content: The ban on American passenger jets flying in and out of Israel was lifted on Wednesday night, just 24 hours after the Federal Aviation Administration imposed restrictions. The FAA’s ruling had grounded 160 flights scheduled to take off or land at Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport amid safety concerns following a reported Hamas rocket landing near the airport. Former New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg traveled to Israel to show support as deadly clashes with Palestinian authorities continued. Passengers lined up at the airport as flights were canceled, searching for alternative travel options after the restrictions. The ban was enacted on Tuesday after a rocket landed about a mile from the airport, prompting fears for passenger safety. The directive applied only to U.S. airlines – including Delta, US Airways, and American – and did not affect foreign airlines. Before the order, Delta had already turned a jet around mid-flight and canceled future flights to Israel after a rocket from Gaza reportedly landed nearby. Other U.S. airlines followed, and several European and Canadian carriers also suspended flights, despite Israeli government objections. In contrast, Israel’s El Al maintained its regular schedule, including the flight Bloomberg took. Bloomberg described Ben Gurion as the 'best protected airport in the world' while meeting with Israeli leaders, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Shimon Peres. After reviewing the situation, the FAA announced late Wednesday that flights could resume, citing new information and steps taken by Israel to limit risks. Bloomberg publicly urged the FAA to reverse the ban, calling it a mistake that gave Hamas an undeserved victory. He flew to Tel Aviv on El Al to show solidarity, stating his belief that it's safe to fly to and from Israel. Meanwhile, Secretary of State John Kerry traveled to Israel on an Air Force jet, bypassing FAA restrictions, in an effort to broker a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas. Other countries and airlines remained cautious. Major carriers such as Lufthansa, Alitalia, Air France, Scandinavian Airlines, Norwegian, Royal Jordanian, and Korean Air canceled or suspended their Israel routes, with some extending cancellations. The European Aviation Safety Agency recommended not flying to Tel Aviv, saying it would continue monitoring the situation. Uzi Yitzhaki, director-general of the Transportation Ministry, confirmed at least 160 flights at Ben Gurion were canceled before the ban’s lift – 80 arrivals and 80 departures. On average, about 1,044 passengers flew each way daily on U.S.-Israel flights last year, according to U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics. In one case, Delta Flight 468 from New York was diverted to Paris, carrying 290 passengers. Israeli traveler Jack Ram shared that threats and travel disruptions are not new for Israelis, underlining the ongoing difficulties. Bloomberg documented his Israel trip on Flickr, sharing photos with top Israeli officials. He also visited the family of 24-year-old U.S. volunteer soldier Max Steinberg, killed in Gaza, joining their mourning at the Crowne Plaza Hotel after the funeral on Mount Herzl.

Spain's Queen Letizia, known for her warmth and elegance, showed her affection for children during a state visit to Luxembourg this morning. Upon arrival, an adorable little girl presented her with a posy of flowers, bringing a delighted smile to the Queen's face. Accompanied by King Felipe VI, who also appeared charmed by the gesture, the royal couple was in Luxembourg at the invitation of Grand Duke Henri and his wife, Maria Teresa.

Queen Letizia looked graceful in a chic cream coat dress with traditional Spanish blackwork embroidery, complemented by her softly styled hair and a grey-and-cream clutch. King Felipe joined her in greeting the young flower presenter, who was bundled up against the November chill.

They were welcomed at the Palais Grand Ducal by Grand Duke Henri, elegantly dressed for the occasion, and Grand Duchess Maria Teresa. Also in the welcoming party were Crown Prince Guillaume and his wife, Stéphanie de Lannoy, who hails from a Belgian family with royal lineage.

During the visit, the Spanish and Luxembourgish royals exchanged greetings with local well-wishers and posed for photographs in the ornate setting of the Grand Ducal Palace. The article also highlights the long and resilient history of Luxembourg’s monarchy, established in 1815 after the Congress of Vienna, and notes its familial links to other European royal families, including Belgium and Spain.

The piece comments on the stylish choices of the royal women and draws a comparison between the stability of Luxembourg’s monarchy and the more turbulent recent history of Spain's royal institution, referencing the abdication of King Juan Carlos in the 2010s and his relation to other European monarchs.

article_content: UPS was racing against time on Christmas Eve to deliver packages, but a delivery backlog meant some Americans found gifts missing from under the Christmas tree on Christmas morning. UPS spokesperson Natalie Black apologized, explaining to CNN that a surge in air packages before Christmas exceeded the network’s capacity, causing some shipments to be delayed. Black added, “We know how important holiday packages are, and we’re working around the clock to resolve this issue.” Despite working behind the scenes, UPS adhered to its plan of making no deliveries on Christmas Day, upsetting some customers. Some, like Mo Husseini, expressed frustration on social media, accusing UPS of mishandling deliveries. Melissa Gilbreath wrote on Facebook that her sons’ gifts, ordered on December 9, had been stuck in Fort Worth, Texas, since December 18. She added, “It’s not just about the gifts, but they are part of Christmas.” However, there were also supportive messages from UPS employees. Misty Fulton noted that the staff works very hard and that public expectations may be too high. On Wednesday, Black told CNN that an extra sorting shift would process packages so drivers could deliver the remaining air shipments by Friday. UPS considered Christmas Day deliveries as an emergency measure but ultimately decided not to require drivers to work the holiday after thoughtful consideration. Black noted many workers had already put in extra hours and made unusual Sunday deliveries. Asked why UPS underestimated package volume, Black cited previous severe weather in the Dallas area, higher than expected holiday volume due to a shortened holiday season, and the growth in online shopping as reasons for the backlog, calling it a “perfect storm.” Online retailers like Amazon were also affected. Some customers received notices from Amazon about the UPS transportation delays, with offers of shipping refunds and gift cards. UPS said it would work with retailers to uphold its service commitments. After January 2, when holiday returns are processed, UPS will review the episode and assess its contingency planning. Delays have happened in past years due to weather or technical issues, but Black said it had been a while since glitches created such widespread delays. The backlog impacted more than just gifts. The Warren family in Heath, Texas, had to wait several days for their son’s essential medicine. Patrick Warren told WFAA that their package sat at a UPS outlet in Mesquite until they retrieved it. Another woman at the Fort Worth distribution center described upset customers and increased security.

article_content: Tatreez is a centuries-old traditional Palestinian embroidery art form, featuring a variety of colorful stitching on Palestinian textiles. I was about nine or ten years old when I first learned tatreez. I vividly remember sitting on the porch outside our family’s home in Jordan, with my grandmother, Teta, patiently helping me with my first project—a Tom and Jerry pattern. While that design was far from traditional tatreez, Teta was always patient, undoing my mistakes and teaching me to stitch more efficiently. Thirteen years passed before I picked up a needle and thread again. In that time, my family and I left our town of Ein Al Basha in Jordan for Texas, and later I moved to Washington, D.C. There, I was overwhelmed with loneliness and a longing for a connection to my roots. Hoping to reconnect with my heritage and family, I started stitching simple trees of life on white aida cloth after discovering a local bookstore that offered a tatreez class. I signed up immediately. In that small Middle Eastern bookstore, I rediscovered the excitement I felt as a child. Surrounded by vibrant pearl cotton threads, we stitched together on kitchen towels, and the sense of camaraderie was exhilarating. One motif we explored was Pasha’s tent—also known as Khaimet El Basha—a reference to the four-century Ottoman reign in Palestine. Tatreez is more than just decorative stitching; its motifs often represent different aspects of Palestinian life and culture, depicting animals, plants, household objects, or geometric patterns. The visual language of tatreez draws me in. Each stitch holds the memories and experiences of the embroiderer. For generations, women have passed down stories, documenting important events—from relationships within families to moments of resistance. For example, during times when Palestinian flags were banned, women embroidered them onto their thobes. This enduring tradition is a testament to the legacy, spirit, and creativity of Palestinian women. One design I made interprets the Beit Dajan Amulets, inspired by the dress of a married Palestinian woman from the village of Beit Dajan near Jaffa in the early 1900s. Amulets, or hujub, were traditionally used to protect from evil and bring good luck. Teta passed away in 2014, but I think of her every time I get my threads tangled or accidentally poke my finger. She was the foundation of our family, much like tatreez grounds me and connects me to the thousands of Palestinian women before me. For them, tatreez was not just a livelihood, but a symbol of resistance and identity. It has been years since that afternoon in Ein Al Basha when I first learned to stitch, but every time I thread my needle, I return to that place. Ever since leaving Ein Al Basha, I have been searching for a sense of home, and tatreez helps me find my way back.

Mäletan selgelt, kuidas istusin meie pere kodu verandale Jordaanias, vanaema Tetaga, kes kannatlikult aitas mul mu esimest projekti teha—Tom ja Jerry mustrit. Kuigi see disain polnud sugugi traditsiooniline tatreez, oli Teta alati kannatlik, parandas mu vead ja õpetas, kuidas kiiremini tikkida. Seal valdas mind sügav üksildus ja igatsus juurte ning pere järele. Lootes taasühenduda oma pärandi ja perega, alustasin jälle lihtsate elupuude tikkimisega valgele aida kangale, kui avastasin kohalikus raamatupoes tatreezi kursuse. Registreerusin kohe. Selles väikeses Lähis-Ida raamatupoes taasavastasin lapsepõlvest tuttava elevuse. Ümbritsetuna erksatest pärlniitidest, tikkisime üheskoos köögirätikutele ning kogetud ühtekuuluvus pakkus rõõmu. Üks motiividest, mida uurisime, oli Pasha telk—tuntud ka kui Khaimet El Basha—viide Palestiina neljasajaaastasele Ottomani võimule. Tatreez ei ole pelgalt dekoratiivne tikkimine; selle mustrid kajastavad tihti eri aspekte Palestiina elust ja kultuurist, kujutades loomi, taimi, majapidamisesemeid või geomeetrilisi mustreid. Tatreezi visuaalne keel tõmbab mind. Iga piste sisaldab tikkija mälestusi ja kogemusi. Põlvkondade jooksul on naised edastanud mustrite kaudu lugusid ja talletanud olulisi sündmusi—olgu selleks peresuhted või vastupanu hetked. Näiteks, kui Palestiina lipud olid avalikult keelatud, tikkisid naised need oma rahvarõivastele. See püsiv traditsioon on tunnistus Palestiina naiste pärandist, vaimust ja loovusest. Üks minu loodud kujundus tõlgendab Beit Dajani amulette, inspireerituna abielus Palestiina naise kleidist Jaffa lähedal Beit Dajani külast 1900. aastate algusest. Amulette ehk hujubit kasutati traditsiooniliselt kurja eest kaitsmiseks ja õnne toomiseks. Teta suri 2014. aastal, kuid mõtlen temale iga kord, kui mu niidid lähevad sassi või torkan end kogemata nõelaga. Ta oli meie pere tugisammas—nagu tatreez hoiab mind maa peal ja ühendab mind tuhandete Palestiina naistega, kes on olnud enne mind. Nende jaoks oli tatreez mitte ainult elatus, vaid ka vastupanu ja identiteet. On möödunud aastaid sellest õhtupoolikust Ein Al Bashas, kui ma esimest korda tikkimist õppisin, kuid iga kord, kui nõela niidi taha ajan, pöördun justkui tagasi sinna. Pärast Ein Al Bashast lahkumist olen otsinud kodutunnet ning tatreez aitab mul tee tagasi leida.

article_content: Recent studies reveal that Gires-Tournois (GT) biosensors, a type of nanophotonic resonator, can detect tiny virus particles and produce colorful microscope images of viral loads. However, these sensors have been limited by visual artifacts and inconsistent results. In a breakthrough, an international team led by Professor Young Min Song from the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology, Korea, has used artificial intelligence (AI) to address these challenges. Their findings were published in Nano Today. The ability for rapid and on-site diagnostics is crucial for effective patient care and containing the spread of infectious diseases, as highlighted by the COVID-19 pandemic. There is a strong need for accurate, decentralized tests that avoid the complexity and delays of traditional laboratory methods. Bright-field microscopy is a popular point-of-care tool for measuring viral loads. But due to viruses’ small size—about 100 nanometers—and low refractive index (similar to a microscope slide), accurately measuring them has remained difficult, which raises the detection limit. In their new study, the researchers introduced 'DeepGT'—a biosensing tool that combines the benefits of GT platforms with deep learning-based algorithms. DeepGT can accurately quantify nanoscale bioparticles, including viruses, without requiring complex sample preparation. Prof. Song explains, “We designed DeepGT to objectively assess infection severity, moving diagnosis from subjective assessments to a more accurate, data-driven approach for guiding treatment decisions.” The team engineered a trilayered thin-film GT biosensor, which was biofunctionalized to enable colorimetric sensing upon interaction with target viruses. They validated the sensor by simulating the binding of host cells and viruses using particles that mimicked SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19. They then trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) on over 1,000 optical and scanning electron microscope images of the GT biosensor with different nanoparticles. DeepGT successfully refined visual artifacts and extracted accurate viral load data, even at concentrations as low as 138 pg/ml. The tool determined particle counts with high precision—a mean absolute error of 2.37 recorded over 1,596 images, compared to 13.47 for conventional rule-based algorithms—and did so in less than a second. Powered by the CNN, DeepGT can also estimate disease severity from asymptomatic to severe based on viral load. DeepGT provides an efficient solution for screening viruses of various sizes, overcoming the diffraction limit of visible light. Prof. Song adds, “Our approach offers a practical and fast method for detecting and managing new viral threats, while also improving public health readiness and potentially lowering diagnostic costs.”
translated_content: Hiljutised uuringud näitavad, et Gires-Tournois (GT) biosensorid, mis on nanofotonilised resonantsandurid, suudavad tuvastada väga väikeseid viiruseosakesi ja anda värvilisi mikroskoobipilte viiruskoormusest. Siiski piiravad nende kasutamist visuaalsed moonutused ja ebajärjekindlad tulemused. Rahvusvaheline meeskond, mida juhib professor Young Min Song Gwangju Teaduse ja Tehnoloogia Instituudist Koreas, kasutas läbimurde saavutamiseks tehisintellekti (AI), et neid väljakutseid ületada. Uuring avaldati ajakirjas Nano Today. Kiire ja kohapealne diagnostika on oluline tõhusa patsiendihoolduse ja nakkushaiguste leviku ohjamiseks, nagu tõi esile ka COVID-19 pandeemia. Täpsed ja detsentraliseeritud testid, mis hoiavad ära laborimeetodite keerukuse ja viivitused, on väga vajalikud. Helesvälja mikroskoopia on populaarne viiruskoormuse määramise vahend. Kuid viiruste väga väike suurus (u 100 nanomeetrit) ja madal murdumisnäitaja (sarnaselt mikroskoobislaidiga) muudavad nende täpse hindamise keeruliseks ja tõstavad tuvastuspiiri. Oma viimases uuringus esitlesid teadlased 'DeepGT'd – biosensori tööriista, mis ühendab GT platvormi eelised ja süvaõppe algoritmid. DeepGT võimaldab täpset nanosuuruses biopartiklite (sh viiruste) tuvastamist ilma keerulise proovide ettevalmistuseta. Professor Song selgitab: “Kujundasime DeepGT, et objektiivselt hinnata nakkuse raskusastet, viies diagnostika subjektiivselt hindamiselt täpsele andmepõhisele lähenemisele ravi suunamisel.” Meeskond arendas kolme õhukese kihiga GT biosensori, mis muudeti biofunktsionaalseks, et värvimuutusel tuvastada sihtviirust. Töökindlust kontrolliti, simuleerides viiruse ja peremeesraku seondumist osakestega, mis matkivad COVID-19 põhjustanud SARS-CoV-2 viirust. Järgmisena treeniti konvolutsioonilist närvivõrku (CNN) rohkem kui tuhande GT biosensori pinnast tehtud optilise ja skaneeriva elektronmikroskoobi pildiga, milles kasutati eri tüüpi nanoosakesi. DeepGT parandas visuaalseid moonutusi ja tuvastas viiruskoormuse täpselt, isegi kontsentratsioonidel alates 138 pg/ml. Seade määras osakeste arvu väga täpselt: keskmine absoluutne viga oli 2,37 1 596 pildi kohta (võrreldes tavapäraste reeglipõhiste algoritmide 13,47-ga) ja kõik alla sekundi jooksul. CNN võimaldab DeepGT-l hinnata ka haiguse raskusastet asümptomaatilisest kuni raskeni, lähtudes viiruskoormuse põhjal. DeepGT pakub tõhusa ja täpse meetodi erineva suurusega viiruste tuvastamiseks, ületades nähtava valguse difraktsioonipiiri. Professor Song lisab: “Meie lähenemine võimaldab kiiresti tuvastada ja hallata uusi viiruseohte, parandades rahvatervise valmisolekut ja aidates potentsiaalselt vähendada diagnostikakulutusi.”

article_content: As editor-in-chief of Vogue, Anna Wintour is known for being at the forefront of fashion trends. On the first day of the U.S. Open, she appeared at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center wearing a vibrant scarlet dress—one of the season's biggest colors. The 64-year-old tennis enthusiast looked elegant in her flared midi dress, pairing it with nude Manolo Blahnik shoes, statement jewelry, and her signature bob hairstyle. Anna reportedly begins each day with a rigorous 5:45 am tennis match at Midtown Tennis Club in New York, where the hourly rate starts at $80 (£48). On Monday, she watched Simona Halep, Maria Sharapova, and Andy Murray win their matches. She also planned to return to support her close friend Roger Federer in his upcoming match against Marinko Matosevic at Arthur Ashe Stadium. Renowned for her passion for tennis, Anna is sometimes referred to simply as 'the bob', and counts Roger Federer among her close friends. Recently, Wintour took part in the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge, accepting her daughter Bee Shaffer's nomination. In a video posted from her Hamptons home, Anna, joined by her family, accepted the challenge and nominated Roger Federer and Dominic West. In the video, Ms. Wintour, immaculately dressed as always, reacts with an uncharacteristic squeal as buckets of ice are poured over her famous bob. Within an hour, the video gained over 4,600 likes on Facebook and sparked widespread reaction in the fashion industry. Elsewhere at the tournament, Novak Djokovic of Serbia played Diego Schwartzman of Argentina during the opening round of the U.S. Open.
