Donald Trump is accused of having shared sensitive details about US nuclear submarines with Anthony Pratt, an Australian billionaire and Mar-a-Lago member, in early 2021 after his presidency, according to sources familiar with federal probes cited by ABC News. Pratt allegedly relayed this information to various foreign officials, employees, and journalists.

Trump’s spokesperson called the leak of these allegations illegal, contending that important context is missing and further claiming that Trump acted lawfully and with transparency. They demanded investigators focus on the source of the leak instead of pursuing what they called politically charged “witch-hunts.”

Reportedly, the sensitive details included information on how many nuclear warheads US submarines could hold and their capabilities regarding Russian submarines, though investigators have not confirmed if these details were accurate. Pratt was advised not to discuss the matter, but reportedly referenced it soon after meeting Trump, according to a Mar-a-Lago staff member.

The information was passed to special counsel Jack Smith, who is leading the Department of Justice’s investigation into Trump’s management of classified documents. While Trump has been indicted on 40 counts linked to mishandling classified materials and other offenses, the Pratt episode was not included in the indictment.

Pratt explained that he talked about his meeting with Trump to promote US-Australia business interests, and that the topic arose when he suggested Australia should buy American submarines. Later, Australia canceled a previous contract with France in favor of buying nuclear-powered submarines from the US and UK, ultimately purchasing three US Virginia-class submarines.

Sources indicate Trump did not physically hand over any documents to Pratt, but there are previous reports suggesting he displayed sensitive documents to associates.

Väidetavalt jagas Pratt seda infot mitmete välisametnike, töötajate ja ajakirjanikega.

Trumpi pressiesindaja nimetas nende süüdistuste lekkimist ebaseaduslikuks, väites, et oluline kontekst puudub ja rõhutas, et Trump tegutses seaduslikult ning läbipaistvalt. Esindaja kutsus uurijaid üles keskenduma lekitaja tuvastamisele, mitte nn poliitiliselt motiveeritud „nõiajahi“ jätkamisele.

Väidetavalt puudutas tundlik info seda, kui palju tuuma-lõhkepeasid USA allveelaevad suudavad kanda ja kui märkamatult nad võivad Vene allveelaevadele läheneda, kuid uurijad pole kinnitanud, kas info oli täpne. Pratt ütles uurijatele, et ta rääkis kohtumisest Trumpiga, et edendada USA ja Austraalia ärisidemeid, ja et allveelaevade teema tõstatati siis, kui ta mainis, et Austraalia võiks osta USA allveelaevu. article_content: A decommissioned Cold War missile silo near Lewis, New York, is up for sale as an extraordinary home, priced at $750,000. Once designed to house an Atlas missile, the silo has been empty since it was retired in 1960 and now serves as a unique residential property. Spread across 8.3 acres near the Adirondacks, the site boasts scenic vistas, a private pond, and a stream. The land includes a barn, storage shed, and additional outbuildings that could be used for farming or extra storage. Beneath the surface, the home spans 32,000 square feet on two underground levels. It contains a single bedroom, a bathroom, and a functional kitchen equipped with modern basics. The main living area is set in the historic launch control center and features vintage military décor. Historic touches remain: robust blast doors, vintage control panels, and obsolete military equipment, which offer both safety and conversation pieces. The space retains its industrial, Cold War-era atmosphere, prioritizing original features and history over conventional comfort. Due to overwhelming curiosity, realtor Brian Dominic has set a $375 fee to tour the silo, anticipating around 1,000 online queries, 100 calls, and only a select few visitors. The house is equipped with essential utilities—well water, septic system, propane water heater, whole-house cooling, and satellite dishes. However, parts of the basement are unfinished, and the tunnel-connected, windowless rooms may feel confining. For those who enjoy immersive experiences, the home comes with yellow hard hats and olive green coveralls to recreate the Cold War ambiance. With its blend of privacy, security, and historical significance, the silo-home is ideal for buyers seeking a truly distinctive property in a tranquil rural setting, though it does require further renovation.

Elamuse huvides jagab kinnisvaraettevõte külalistele kollaseid kiivreid ja oliivrohelisi kombinesoone, et luua autentne Külma sõja aegne õhkkond. article_content: Australian marine scientist and photographer Frederique Olivier captured stunning close-up photos of Adelie penguins leaping from the icy waters onto Antarctic ice at the Casey research station in the Windmill Islands. He managed to approach the penguins within a few feet, noting they were mostly uninterested in his presence and sometimes showed curiosity. The photos show lively penguins launching themselves onto the cold land after their hunting trips, stretching their wings back and flicking their tails as they land. Olivier, 38, highlighted that getting these shots required significant patience, especially in Antarctic winters, where temperatures can plunge to -30°C. He took care not to interrupt the colony, knowing the adults were busy nesting and raising chicks. Olivier expressed a deep respect for the penguins' remarkable adaptation to their extreme environment and emphasized the importance of not disturbing their routines.

Olivier pääses lindudele väga lähedale – vaid mõne jala kaugusele – ning märkas, et pingviinid ei pööranud talle suurt tähelepanu ja olid mõnikord isegi uudishimulikud. Fotodel on näha energilisi pingviine, kes tõukavad end pärast veealust jahti kuiva, kuid külma maapinna poole, sirutades tiivad taha ja liputades saba, kui nad maanduvad. 38-aastane Olivier rõhutas, et tõeliste hetkede tabamine nõudis suurt kannatlikkust, eriti Antarktika talve karmides tingimustes, kui temperatuur langeb -30 kraadini. Ta oli väga ettevaatlik, et mitte kolooniat häirida, teades, et täiskasvanud pingviinid olid hõivatud poegade eest hoolitsemisega. Olivier tõi välja oma sügava austuse pingviinide erakordse kohanemisvõime vastu niivõrd ekstreemsetes oludes ning rõhutas, kui oluline on mitte häirida nende igapäevaelu.

Two dissident members of the Irish Republican Army were convicted on Friday for the 2009 murder of police constable Stephen Carroll, a killing that deeply shocked Northern Ireland. Carroll, 48, was shot dead in Craigavon, County Armagh, after paramilitaries lured police to the scene with a hoax emergency call. The Continuity IRA claimed responsibility for the attack, which occurred only 48 hours after the Real IRA, another breakaway group, killed two British soldiers outside an army base in Antrim.

In the aftermath of these murders, former IRA commander and current Deputy First Minister Martin McGuinness described the dissidents as 'traitors to Ireland,' a statement that led to threats against his own life from some former associates. Unlike these groups, McGuinness and the mainstream IRA have renounced violence.

Brendan McConville, 40, a former Sinn Fein elected representative, and John Paul Wootton, 20 (who was 17 at the time of the killing), both from the local area, were found guilty after a nine-week trial at Belfast Crown Court. Although both men declined to testify, their lawyers insisted on their innocence. However, Judge Lord Justice Paul Girvan, citing forensic and witness evidence, concluded they were 'intimately involved' in Carroll’s killing and called them 'active and committed supporters of a republican campaign of violence.' He described the murder as 'callous and cowardly,' noting that Carroll was killed solely because of his role as a police officer, and sentenced the two men to life in prison. The minimum terms before eligibility for release will be determined at a future hearing.

Constable Carroll’s widow, Kate, embraced her son as the verdicts were announced. In February, John Paul Wootton’s mother, Sharon Wootton, 39, admitted to obstructing the investigation by moving computer equipment from her home after a police search. Carroll was the first Police Service of Northern Ireland officer killed on duty since the force replaced the Royal Ulster Constabulary in 2001. Over 300 officers were killed and nearly 9,000 injured during decades of conflict between pro-British and pro-Irish factions in Northern Ireland. Despite the Good Friday peace agreement of 1998, some IRA splinter groups remain active.

article_content: Thirty-one critically ill premature babies were safely evacuated from Gaza's Shifa Hospital to Egypt over the weekend, amid dire conditions and ongoing conflict. Despite this transfer, over 250 patients with serious injuries remain in the hospital after Israeli forces conducted a search for Hamas operations. The evacuation of the babies, and ongoing accusations about the hospital’s role in the war, highlight the intense humanitarian crisis between Israel and Hamas. Israeli authorities claim that militants are using hospitals, including Shifa, as military bases, whereas Palestinian representatives and hospital staff deny such allegations. Shifa Hospital experienced power outages and supply shortages as fighting continued outside; the rescued babies, many with life-threatening conditions, are now receiving emergency care in Rafah. Hospital director Mohamed Zaqout reported that four infants died before they could be evacuated. According to the World Health Organization, most patients still at Shifa have severe injuries, and plans are underway to move them soon. The Israeli military has presented what it says is strong evidence of a Hamas command post under Shifa Hospital, including details of a 55-meter tunnel and alleged video footage of hostages. These claims have not been independently verified. Israel also reported that Cpl. Noa Marciano, an Israeli soldier, was killed by Hamas at Shifa after being wounded in an earlier Israeli strike. Hamas and hospital staff deny these accounts. Civilians in Gaza are facing extreme hardship. Local health officials report that over 11,500 people have died in Gaza since the conflict began, with thousands missing. Resources such as food, water, and fuel are in critically short supply, and the United Nations has warned of deteriorating conditions as cold weather intensifies. Mass displacement has forced the majority of Gaza’s population to flee their homes. The conflict’s impact is also being felt beyond Gaza. On Sunday, Yemen’s Houthi rebels captured an Israeli-linked cargo ship in the Red Sea, taking its 25 multinational crew members hostage, which has raised fears about broader regional instability. The ship, Galaxy Leader, has connections to Israeli businessman Abraham “Rami” Ungar. Japan is currently negotiating for the crew’s release after the vessel was taken to the Yemeni port of Hodeida. Within Gaza, heavy clashes persist in areas like the Jabaliya refugee camp, where residents describe continuous shelling and gunfire. A strike on a U.N.-run school sheltering displaced people resulted in significant loss of life, drawing condemnation from the United Nations over rising civilian casualties. Fatalities among Palestinians in the West Bank have also increased since the fighting erupted. Negotiations are ongoing, with Qatar and the United States mediating talks for the release of hostages held by Hamas. Israel’s leadership plans to meet with families of the hostages as hopes for an agreement continue. The conflict has claimed more than 1,200 Israeli lives, primarily from the initial attack, and over 60 Israeli soldiers have died. Some hostages have been freed, but many are still in captivity. A small amount of humanitarian aid, including fuel, has been allowed into Gaza recently, enabling essential services to function temporarily. Some foreign nationals and patients have managed to leave Gaza through Egypt, including planned evacuation flights for Turkish citizens. Nevertheless, widespread suffering and displacement persist as the humanitarian crisis worsens.
translated_content: Kolmkümmend üks kriitilises seisundis enneaegset beebit evakueeriti nädalavahetusel Gazas asuvast Shifa haiglast Egiptusesse äärmiselt rasketes tingimustes ja kestva konflikti keskel. Vaatamata sellele jäävad haiglasse üle 250 tugevalt vigastatud patsiendi, pärast seda kui Iisraeli väed viisid läbi otsingu Hamasi jälgede leidmiseks. Beebide evakueerimine ja lõputud süüdistused haigla rolli kohta sõjas toovad esile tõsise humanitaarkriisi Iisraeli ja Hamasi vahel. Iisraeli võimud väidavad, et võitlejad kasutavad haiglaid, sh Shifat, sõjaliseks baasiks, kuid Palestiina esindajad ja haigla töötajad eitavad neid süüdistusi. Shifa haiglas katkesid vool ja varud välisvõitluste tõttu; päästetud beebid, kellest paljud vaevlevad eluohtlikes seisundites, saavad nüüd erakorralist abi Rafahis. Haigla direktor Mohamed Zaqout teatas, et neli imikut suri enne evakueerimist. Maailma Terviseorganisatsiooni andmetel on enamikul Shifasse jäänud patsientidest rasked vigastused ja plaanitakse neid peagi evakueerida. Iisraeli sõjavägi on esitanud enda sõnul tugevaid tõendeid selle kohta, et Hamasil on Shifa haigla all ja sees komandopunkt, sealhulgas 55-meetrine tunnel ning väidetavad videokaadrid pantvangidest. Neid väiteid pole võimalik sõltumatult kinnitada. Samuti teatas Iisrael, et nende sõdur Noa Marciano tapeti Hamasi poolt Shifas, pärast esmast haavamist Iisraeli rünnakus. Hamas ja haiglatöötajad eitavad neid väiteid. Tsiviilelanikud Gazas kannatavad äärmuslikes tingimustes. Kohalikud terviseametnikud väidavad, et alates konflikti algusest on Gazas hukkunud üle 11 500 inimese, tuhandeid on kadunud. Toidu, vee ja kütuse puudus on kriitiline ning ÜRO on hoiatanud olukorra halvenemise eest külmade ilmade saabudes. Enamik Gaza elanikest on sunnitud kodudest lahkuma. article_content: Bowe Bergdahl, a former U.S. Army sergeant held by the Taliban for five years, is scheduled to meet with the general heading up the investigation into his 2009 disappearance in Afghanistan. His lawyer, Eugene Fidell, clarified that the session is intended as an interview rather than an interrogation, suggesting it will be a calm conference-room discussion. In preparation, Bergdahl and his legal team spent the day reviewing documents—including some classified. Fidell expressed hope that the meeting would be productive. Major General Kenneth Dahl, who leads the Army’s inquiry, has already held a brief meeting with Bergdahl. Bergdahl was captured by the Taliban shortly after he walked away from his outpost in June 2009, then spent five years in captivity until his 2014 release as part of a prisoner swap for five Taliban members held by the U.S. After returning to the United States, Bergdahl underwent medical care and counseling at a hospital in San Antonio before returning to duty at Fort Sam Houston, Texas. He is now assigned to a unit under U.S. Army North that handles homeland defense and works on cooperative security efforts with countries such as Canada, Mexico, and the Bahamas. Although Bergdahl's release was first greeted with celebration, it quickly provoked controversy, with some accusing him of intentionally deserting his unit. An Army investigation determined he left on his own volition but stopped short of labeling him a deserter, as his intentions were unclear and had not been directly explained. During his captivity, Bergdahl received scheduled promotions, rising from Private First Class to Sergeant. Bergdahl’s attorney reports that he is very grateful for his rescue and fully comprehends the seriousness of his situation.

Advokaat Eugene Fidell täpsustas, et kohtumine on kavandatud intervjuuna, mitte ülekuulamisena, ja peaks olema rahulik arutelu konverentsilaua ümber. Ettevalmistuseks veetsid Bergdahl ja tema meeskond terve päeva dokumentidega, kaasa arvatud salastatud materjalidega, tutvudes. Fidell avaldas lootust, et kohtumine tuleb tulemuslik. Kindralmajor Kenneth Dahl, kes juhib uurimist, on Bergdahliga juba varem lühidalt kohtunud. Pärast seda, kui Bergdahl 2009. aasta juunis oma baasist lahkus, püüdis Taliban ta kinni ning hoidis teda vangistuses kuni 2014. aastani, mil ta vahetati välja viie USA-s kinnipeetud Talibani liikme vastu. Pärast tagasitulekut Ameerika Ühendriikidesse sai Bergdahl arstiabi ja nõustamist San Antonio haiglas ning naasis seejärel teenistusse Fort Sam Houstoni baasis Texases. Praegu töötab ta U.S. Army North alluvuses üksuses, mille ülesandeks on kodumaa kaitse ning koostööprojektid Kanadaga, Mehhikoga ja Bahamaga. Kuigi Bergdahli vabastamine põhjustas esialgu suurt rõõmu, järgnes sellele kiiresti vaidlus ning mitmed inimesed süüdistasid teda oma üksuse tahtlikus mahajätmises. Armee uurimine leidis, et ta lahkus vabatahtlikult, kuid ametlikku põgeniku süüdistust ei esitatud, kuna tema tegelikud motiivid polnud selged. Vangistuse ajal edutati Bergdahli ajakohaselt, liikudes reamehest seersandi auastmeni. Bergdahli advokaadi sõnul on ta väga tänulik oma pääsemise eest ning mõistab olukorra tõsidust.

article_content: Amazon saw a significant surge over the last three months, amassing £14 billion in global sales, with UK customers contributing about one-tenth of this amount. This growth occurred during the holiday season, a time marked by struggles for traditional retailers. Despite its success, Amazon came under fire for diverting revenue through Luxembourg, which allowed the online giant to pay minimal UK taxes. UK tax records from 2011 show only £1.8 million paid on £3.35 billion in sales. The ascent of Amazon and other online retailers coincided with mounting difficulties for high street stores. During the recent festive period, around 1,400 shops closed their doors, risking approximately 17,500 jobs. Well-known UK chains like HMV, Jessops, Blockbuster, and Comet have recently gone into administration, endangering thousands of positions. Industry experts warn that continued closures could result in up to 20% of stores shutting down. Prominent figures such as Tim Waterstone and Andy Street have labeled Amazon's competitive edge as unfair, urging for a regulatory response. Analysis from Morgan Stanley suggests that Amazon's annual sales could approach £40 billion, with expectations of a leap to £86 billion by 2015. Amazon's transformation from a book retailer to a one-stop shop for DVDs, home goods, electronics, and even auto parts has been a driving force behind the shift from physical to online shopping. Morningstar analyst RJ Hottovy notes that by operating without the overhead of physical stores, Amazon consistently offers lower prices and is changing the face of retail. The recent downfall of major entertainment and electronics retailers, including HMV and Blockbuster, has put thousands more jobs at risk, illustrating the ongoing upheaval on the UK high street.

article_content: Karen and Ian Gilbert from Pontypool, Wales, were amazed to discover they were expecting identical triplets – a one-in-200-million occurrence without IVF. Doctors warned the couple about serious health risks, including the risk that the babies could compete for essential resources in the womb, which might jeopardize their survival. Despite doctors suggesting options to terminate the pregnancy or reduce the number of fetuses, the Gilberts chose to try for all three. Their daughters, Ffion, Madison, and Paige, were delivered two months early by caesarean on August 2, each weighing just over three pounds. After six weeks in intensive care at Nevill Hall Hospital, the triplets recovered more quickly than expected and are now home. Karen is recovering from the ordeal of the pregnancy and expressed gratitude at having her three daughters with her. Ian said the pregnancy was monitored with weekly scans to track the triplets' growth. The family also includes their three-year-old daughter Faye. During the pregnancy, Karen experienced significant pain and suffered a serious fall, but all three triplets survived. Now back home, Karen and Ian are adjusting to life with their three new arrivals and look forward to seeing their personalities develop. Hospital staff said they were thrilled with the outcome and wished the family well.

article_content: Researchers from the Center for Injury Research and Prevention (CIRP) at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) and the Stuart Weitzman School of Design at the University of Pennsylvania have discovered that teenagers living in lower-income areas of the Columbus, Ohio, metro region are up to four times less likely to complete driver training and obtain their driver's license before turning 18, compared to those in more affluent neighborhoods. Long travel times to reach driving schools also negatively affect teens' enrollment in driver education programs, impacting youth from both higher- and lower-income areas. The findings, published in Accident Analysis and Prevention and Findings, were presented at the Association for the Advancement in Automotive Medicine Annual Scientific Conference in Indianapolis, IN, on October 4, 2023. Motor vehicle crashes remain a leading cause of death for teens, with the highest risk of accidents occurring during the first year after licensure. Graduated Driver Licensing (GDL) systems and formal driver education can help address this risk by providing teens with the chance to gain experience in lower-risk driving situations. Recent CHOP research in Ohio indicates that new drivers licensed before age 18—who are required to complete both classroom and behind-the-wheel driver education and adhere to GDL restrictions—are less likely to be involved in crashes than those licensed at age 18 or older who are exempt from these requirements. For this study, researchers examined whether living in lower-income neighborhoods and greater distances from driving schools reduced the likelihood of teens completing driver education and getting licensed before age 18. They analyzed licensing data from the Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles covering over 35,000 applicants between the ages of 15.5 and 25, collected from 2017 to 2019, and linked it with neighborhood-level socioeconomic data from the U.S. Census Bureau. Megan S. Ryerson, Ph.D., senior author and CIRP senior fellow at CHOP and the UPS Chair of Transportation at the Stuart Weitzman School of Design, noted, 'Our robust studies with licensing data show that teens residing in lower-income neighborhoods and neighborhoods farther from driving schools are significantly less likely to complete driver education prior to licensure compared with peers from wealthier areas.' She emphasized that improving access to driver training and education—through financial support and expanding the reach of driving schools—should be a policy priority to enhance road safety for all. The research also found that while teens in the most affluent neighborhoods are the most likely to complete driver training, those in wealthy areas situated furthest from driving schools are considerably less likely to do so, compared to their counterparts living closer to such schools. Wealthier teens may have access to alternate transportation options, such as rideshare services or family members, whereas teens from lower-income neighborhoods may lack these alternatives and therefore need a driver's license to reach jobs and educational opportunities. Overall, the findings suggest that increasing access to driver training and licensing is a critical need across the socioeconomic spectrum. Flaura Winston, MD, Ph.D., co-author of the study and co-scientific director of CIRP at CHOP, stated, 'Access to driver education and licensing is both a road safety and transportation equity issue.' She urged that all states should take necessary steps to remove barriers to driver education and licensing, so that all teens—regardless of financial means—can become safe drivers.
translated_content: Philadelphia lastehaigla Lastevigastuste Uurimis- ja Ennetuskeskuse (CIRP) ning Pennsylvania ülikooli Stuart Weitzmani Disainikooli teadlased on avastanud, et madalama sissetulekuga piirkondades elavad teismelised Columbus'e (Ohio) linnaümbruses lõpetavad kuni neli korda väiksema tõenäosusega juhikoolituse ja saavad juhiloa enne 18. eluaastat võrreldes jõukamates rajoonides elavate eakaaslastega. Pikad sõiduajad autokoolidesse mõjutavad samuti negatiivselt teismeliste osalemist juhikoolituses, mõjutades nii kõrgema kui ka madalama sissetulekuga noori. Ajakirjades Accident Analysis and Prevention ning Findings avaldatud tulemusi tutvustati 4. oktoobril 2023 Indianapolisel toimunud Automotive Medicine’i Assotsiatsiooni aastakonverentsil. Liiklusõnnetused on teismeliste seas jätkuvalt peamine surma põhjus ning suurim õnnetuse risk on esimese juhiloa-aasta jooksul. Etappidel põhinev juhilubade süsteem (GDL) ja ametlik juhikoolitus aitavad seda riski vähendada, pakkudes noortele võimalust koguda kogemusi turvalisemates tingimustes. Viimane CHOPi uuring Ohios näitab, et alla 18-aastaselt juhiloa saanud ja kohustusliku klassiruumi ning sõidukoolituse ning GDL-i piirangutega noored satuvad harvem õnnetustesse kui need, kes saavad juhiloa 18-aastaselt või hiljem ega pea neid nõudeid täitma. Uuringus analüüsiti, kas elamine madalapalgalises naabruskonnas ja kaugus autokoolidest vähendab tõenäosust, et teismelised läbivad juhikoolituse ja saavad juhiloa enne 18. eluaastat. Uurijad analüüsisid Ohio registri litsentsiandmeid üle 35 000 taotleja kohta vanuses 15,5–25 aastat (2017 kuni 2019), seostades need USA rahvaloenduse piirkondlike sotsiaalmajanduslike andmetega. Megan S. Ryerson, Ph.D., uuringu vanemautor ning CIRPi vanemteadur ja Pennsylvania ülikooli Stuart Weitzmani Disainikooli transpordi õppetooli juhataja, märkis: "Meie põhjalikud uuringud näitavad, et madalama sissetulekuga ja autokoolidest kaugemal elavad noored lõpetavad juhikoolituse oluliselt harvemini kui jõukamates piirkondades elavad eakaaslased." Ta rõhutas, et juhikoolituse kättesaadavuse parandamine nii rahalise toetuse kui ka autokoolide leviala laiendamisega peaks olema prioriteet, et suurendada liiklusohutust kõigile. Uuring leidis ka, et jõukamates piirkondades elavad noored on kõige tõenäolisemalt juhikoolituse läbijad, kuid rikkamate linnaosade need teismelised, kes elavad autokoolidest kõige kaugemal, kalduvad palju harvem juhikoolitust läbima kui nende lähemal elavad eakaaslased. Jõukamatel noortel võivad olla alternatiivsed transpordivõimalused, näiteks sõidujagamisteenused või pere abi, samas kui madalama sissetulekuga noortel neid valikuid tihti pole ning seetõttu vajavad nad juhiluba tööle ja haridusele ligipääsuks. Üldiselt näitavad tulemused, et juhikoolituse ja juhiloa saamise ligipääsu parandamine on kogu sotsiaalmajandusliku spektri ulatuses vajalik. Flaura Winston, MD, Ph.D., uuringu kaasautor ja CIRPi teadusdirektor CHOPis, ütles: "Juhikoolitusele ja juhiloale ligipääs on nii liiklusohutuse kui ka transpordiõigluse küsimus." Ta rõhutas, et kõik osariigid võiksid astuda samme, et kaotada takistusi juhikoolitusele ja juhiloa saamisele, võimaldamaks kõigil noortel saada ohututeks autojuhtideks – olenemata nende rahalistest võimalustest.

article_content: Although perovskite crystal is believed to be the most abundant mineral inside the Earth, it has eluded scientists for centuries due to its location deep within the planet's lower mantle, between 660 and 2,890 kilometers (410 to 1,796 miles) beneath the surface. In a significant breakthrough, researchers led by Oliver Tschauner at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, have obtained a natural sample from the Tenham meteorite, which experienced high pressures similar to those in Earth’s interior. They formally named the mineral ‘bridgmanite,’ in honor of Percy Bridgman, the American physicist who won the Nobel Prize in 1946 for his work in pressure physics. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical study, natural samples of this mineral had previously failed to meet the International Mineralogical Association’s requirements for official naming. The Tenham meteorite, which struck Australia in 1879 and was subjected to around 2000°C and 24 gigapascals of pressure, preserved bridgmanite crystals by ‘freezing’ them in place before decay could occur. This breakthrough allowed researchers not only to name the mineral but also to analyze its chemical and structural properties. Using a micro-focused X-ray beam and electron microscopy, Tschauner’s team preserved the sample, finding it contained more sodium and ferric iron than expected. The study of bridgmanite is crucial for understanding the Earth's deep mantle and planetary formation. Meanwhile, other researchers propose a provocative model suggesting that up to two-thirds of Earth's carbon could be hidden in the inner core, possibly as iron carbide (Fe7C3), although this theory is still speculative and requires further testing. The Earth’s inner core is generally accepted to consist of iron and nickel with lighter elements, but seismic studies raise questions about its exact composition. The discovery of bridgmanite not only fills a critical gap in mineralogy but also provides insights into processes involved in planetary evolution and the behavior of matter at extreme pressures.
translated_content: Kuigi arvatakse, et perovskiidi kristall on Maa sees kõige külluslikum mineraal, on see olnud teadlastele sajandeid kättesaamatu, kuna asub sügaval planeedi alumises mantlis 660–2890 kilomeetri (410–1796 miili) sügavusel. Olulise läbimurde saavutasid Nevada Ülikooli (Las Vegas) teadlased Oliver Tschauneri juhtimisel, kes said loodusliku proovi Tenhami meteoriidist, mis oli kogenud Maa sisemusele sarnast suurt rõhku. Mineraal nimetati ametlikult „bridgmaniidiks“ Ameerika füüsiku Percy Bridgmani auks, kes võitis 1946. aastal Nobeli füüsikaauhinna rõhu-uurimuste eest. Hoolimata ulatuslikest eksperimentaalsetest ja teoreetilistest uuringutest, ei vastanud eelnevad looduslikud selle mineraali proovid Rahvusvahelise Mineraloogiaseltsi nimetusreeglitele. Tenhami meteoriit, mis tabas Austraaliat 1879. aastal ja mille temperatuur ulatus umbes 2000°C ning rõhk 24 gigapaskalini, säilitas bridgmaniidi kristallid, „külmutades“ need enne nende lagunemist. See läbimurre võimaldas teadlastel mitte ainult seda mineraali ametlikult nimetada, vaid ka selle keemilisi ja struktuurseid omadusi analüüsida. Tschauneri meeskond kasutas proovi säilitamiseks ja uurimiseks mikrofookusega röntgenikiirt ja elektronmikroskoopiat ning avastas, et see sisaldas arvatust rohkem naatriumi ja ferri rauda. Bridgmaniidi uurimine on oluline Maa süvamantli ja planeetide kujunemise mõistmiseks. Samal ajal pakuvad teised uurijad välja provokatiivse mudeli, mille kohaselt võib kuni kaks kolmandikku Maa süsinikust olla peidetud sisemisse tuuma, võimalusel raua karbiidi (Fe7C3) kujul, kuigi see teooria on esialgu spekulatiivne ja vajab täiendavaid katseid. Üldiselt eeldatakse, et Maa sisetuum koosneb rauast, niklist ja kergematest elementidest, kuid seismilised uuringud tekitavad küsimusi selle täpse koostise kohta. Bridgmaniidi avastus täidab olulise tühimiku mineraloogias ning annab uusi teadmisi planeetide evolutsioonist ja aine käitumisest ekstreemsetes tingimustes.

A tragic accident occurred Sunday on Chicago's Dan Ryan Expressway when Franklin Jackson, 46, of League City, Texas, crashed his SUV while driving with his wife and four young children. According to Illinois State Police, Jackson struck a guardrail twice at approximately 4:20 p.m. During the impact, his 4-year-old son, Franklin Jr., who was not wearing a seat belt, was ejected through the rear window and landed on a grassy embankment near the 87th Street exit. The child did not survive; he was later pronounced dead at Comer Children's Hospital due to head trauma, as determined by the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office.

Reports indicate Jackson did not realize his son was missing until stopping at a gas station several exits away to inspect vehicle damage. The other passengers—his wife, 23-year-old Linda Bassett, as well as their three other children (boys aged 1 and 2 and a 3-month-old girl)—were unharmed. Jackson suffered broken ribs.

Police officers responding to the scene found an empty vodka bottle, an empty beer can, and an unopened beer in the vehicle. Jackson was arrested and charged with reckless homicide and aggravated driving under the influence. Prosecutors noted Jackson’s blood alcohol level six hours after the collision was .04 per cent, but forensic experts estimated it was between .11 and .15 per cent at the time of the crash—well above the legal limit.

Before the trip, Linda Bassett posted on social media expressing excitement about visiting family in Chicago for the holidays, but also shared prayers for a safe journey.

article_content: More than twenty years after being shot by Togolese marine soldiers in Lomé, Nigerian businessmen Taju Shoaga and his partner Segun Leopard are still pleading for justice. The attack took place on September 8, 2000, at Port Autonome, where the men, both regular visitors, were clearing a vehicle they intended to bring to Nigeria for sale. Shoaga recalls that on that morning, their agent advised them to speed up the clearance to avoid theft. While working, plainclothes soldiers approached and ordered them to the ground. Unexpectedly, both were shot in the legs. Despite a search of their vehicle, only legal documents were found. Shoaga described a harrowing experience at Tokoin Hospital, where he and Leopard waited for hours with minimal medical care and were asked to pay for services even while bleeding. He further stated that although the then-President of Togo paid for some initial medical treatment, the CFA 250 million approved compensation by Togolese authorities never reached them. The men reported the incident to the Nigerian Embassy in Togo and repeatedly sought help through diplomatic channels, but Shoaga now directly appeals to President Bola Tinubu to intervene and prompt action from Togo’s representatives. Leopard, meanwhile, is still unable to walk as bullet and metal fragments remain embedded in his leg after 23 years. Despite meeting with Togo’s High Commission in Abuja, Shoaga says their case remains under investigation with no updates. He continues to urge President Tinubu to ensure the long-promised justice and compensation finally materialize for himself and his friend.

article_content: This week, President Barack Obama once again declined to directly address the most significant long-term challenges facing America’s economy and health care: Social Security and Medicare. His latest budget proposal does little to protect these important programs for the future, continuing a trend seen in previous statements, including a brief reference in his State of the Union address. Together, Social Security and Medicare account for about half of all federal spending—a share that's expected to rise in future years. Without reform, observers project that entitlement spending could take up all federal tax revenue by 2049. The financial outlook for both programs is worrying. The Congressional Budget Office estimates Medicare could run out of funds by 2022. Social Security’s chief actuary predicts a 23% benefit cut will be needed by 2036 to keep the program solvent. Of these two programs, Social Security could be stabilized for decades through gradual, moderate changes—like raising the retirement age incrementally and modestly adjusting cost-of-living increases—while keeping main benefits unchanged and avoiding tax hikes. Medicare reform is more complex, but several bipartisan ideas exist. Senators Tom Coburn and Joseph Lieberman have proposed raising eligibility age based on longer life spans, capping out-of-pocket costs, and increasing premiums for higher-income recipients. Another plan, suggested by Rep. Paul Ryan and Sen. Ron Wyden, offers seniors a choice among traditional Medicare and competing private options. Medicare’s continued existence relies on timely action—each year of delay complicates needed reforms. Open dialogue and prompt legislation are essential to safeguarding current and future retirees’ health care. Some opponents claim entitlement reforms would destroy Social Security and Medicare, but inaction presents an even greater threat. Criticizing reform proposals without proposing alternatives is not responsible leadership. Protecting Social Security and Medicare’s futures demands bipartisan cooperation, much like when the programs were created. Presidential leadership will be vital to confronting these major challenges.
translated_content: Sel nädalal keeldus president Barack Obama taas käsitlemast Ameerika majandust ja tervishoidu ohustavaid pikaajalisi probleeme: sotsiaalkindlustust ja Medicare’i. Tema uusim eelarveettepanek ei paku olulisi lahendusi nende tulevikuks kindlustamiseks, jätkates varasemate väljaütlemiste joont – näiteks piirdus ka tema aastakõne vaid põgusa viitega neile olulistele teemadele. Sotsiaalkindlustus ja Medicare moodustavad umbes poole kogu föderaalsest kulutustest ning nende osakaal tõenäoliselt kasvab. Kui muudatusi ei tehta, võib 2049. aastaks kogu maksutulu minna nendele programmidele. Mõlema programmi finantsväljavaated on murettekitavad. Kongressi eelarveamet hindab, et Medicare võib jääda rahast ilma juba 2022. aastaks. Sotsiaalkindlustuse peaktaktik hoiatab, et 2036. aastaks oleks vaja toetusi kärpida 23%, et programm oleks jätkusuutlik. Neist kahest oleks sotsiaalkindlustust võimalik aastakümneteks kindlustada järkjärguliste, mõõdukate muudatustega – näiteks pensioniea aeglase tõstmise ning elukalliduse korrigeerimise tagasihoidliku muutmise abil, säilitades põhihüved ja ilma makse tõstmata. Medicare’i reform on keerulisem, kuid olemas on mitmeid kaheparteilisi ideid. Senaatorid Tom Coburn ja Joseph Lieberman on pakkunud välja pensioniea tõstmise vastavalt pikemale eluajale, omavastutuse piirmäärade kehtestamise ning kõrgema sissetulekuga saajatele suuremate maksete nõudmise. Teine plaan, mille taga on esindajatekoja liige Paul Ryan ja senaator Ron Wyden, võimaldaks eakatel valida traditsioonilise Medicare’i ja konkureerivate eraplaanide vahel. Medicare’i säästmine nõuab õigeaegseid otsuseid, sest iga viivitatud aasta teeb vajalikud muudatused ainult keerukamaks. Avatud arutelud ja viivitamatu seadusandlus on hädavajalikud praeguste ja tulevaste pensionäride tervishoiu kaitsmiseks. Mõned kriitikud väidavad, et sotsiaalkindlustuse ja Medicare’i reformid hävitavad need programmid, kuid mitte midagi tegemine ohustab neid veelgi rohkem. Reformiettepanekute kritiseerimine ilma alternatiive pakkumata ei ole vastutustundlik juhtimine. Sotsiaalkindlustuse ja Medicare’i tuleviku kindlustamiseks on vaja kahe erakonna koostööd, nagu nende programmide loomise ajal. Presidentuuri juhtroll on nende suurte väljakutsete lahendamisel määrava tähtsusega.

Paul Wright from Belfast and his husband Martin always loved the idea of being parents, but grew up believing it wouldn’t be possible. Now, they are delighted that their wish has come true. The couple adopted their son two years ago, following legislative changes in Northern Ireland that allowed same-sex couples to adopt. This landmark legal change, which took effect a decade ago, made Northern Ireland the last part of the UK to permit same-sex adoption.

In 2022/23, 13% of adoptions in Northern Ireland involved same-sex couples. The change in law has had a profound impact on Paul’s life. He shared, "I've been with Martin for 23 years, and for most of our relationship, parenthood didn’t seem possible. But when the legislation changed, we immediately decided to pursue adoption."

Paul and Martin adopted their son just before the COVID-19 pandemic, after a process that took about two and a half years. Paul describes it as rigorous but rewarding. "He’s a wonderful child who has settled in well—we are truly a family now."

The ban on same-sex adoption was lifted after a lengthy legal process, despite resistance from then Health Minister Edwin Poots. In 2013, the Northern Ireland Human Rights Commission won a judicial review on the grounds that the previous law discriminated against same-sex and unmarried heterosexual couples.

Initially, the change saw slow uptake: in 2015/16, only 6% of adoptions involved same-sex couples. However, applications from these families have steadily increased, with proportions rising to 10% in 2019/20 and 13% in 2022/23. In comparison, recent figures show 16% of children adopted in England had same-sex parents.

Support for adoptive families has also grown. Earlier this year, the National Lottery Community Fund awarded £6.3 million to groups across Northern Ireland, including £10,000 to Adoption UK to support activities for families where children are adopted by LGBTQ+ parents.

EJ Havlin, Director for Adoption UK in Northern Ireland, emphasizes the importance of visibility for same-sex adopters. "We organize family days so children in same-sex families can see others like them. It’s vital that these families feel proud and recognized, as many children are still waiting for loving homes."

Paul now supports other potential same-sex adoptive parents through Adoption UK's support group. He encourages the community to consider adoption, noting, "The process is rigorous, but no different than for any other parents. We’ve faced little prejudice and feel grateful to be part of a generation with this opportunity—it truly means the world to us."

Paul Wright Belfastist ja tema abikaasa Martin armastasid alati mõtet saada vanemateks, kuid kasvasid üles uskudes, et see pole võimalik. Nüüd on nad üliõnnelikud, et nende soov on täitunud. Paar adopteeris oma poja kaks aastat tagasi pärast seadusemuudatust Põhja-Iirimaal, mis lubas samasoolistel paaridel lapsendada. See oluline seadusemuudatus, mis jõustus kümme aastat tagasi, tegi Põhja-Iirimaast viimase osa Ühendkuningriigist, kus samasooliste paaride lapsendamine lubati.

2022/23. aastal toimus 13% Põhja-Iirimaa lapsendamisi samasoolistes peredes. Seadusemuudatus on Paulile sügavat mõju avaldanud. Ta ütles: „Olen olnud Martiniga koos 23 aastat ja suurema osa meie suhtest ei tundunud lapsevanemaks saamine võimalik. Aga kui seadus muutus, otsustasime kohe lapsendamisele asuda.”

Paul ja Martin võtsid oma poja vastu vahetult enne COVID-19 pandeemiat, umbes kahe ja poole aastase protsessi järel. Paul kirjeldab protsessi kui põhjalikku, kuid väga tasuvat. „Ta on imeline laps ja on meiega hästi kohanenud – nüüd oleme tõeline pere.”

Keeld samasooliste lapsendamisele tühistati pärast pikka juriidilist protsessi, kuigi endine terviseminister Edwin Poots sellele vastu seisis. 2013. aastal võitis Põhja-Iirimaa Inimõiguste Komisjon kohtuasja, kuna eelmine seadus diskrimineeris nii samasoolisi kui ka abielus mitteolevaid heteropaarisid.

Alguses oli muutustega harjumine aeglane: 2015/16. aastal moodustasid samasoolised pered vaid 6% lapsendamistest, kuid taotluste arv on pidevalt tõusnud – 2019/20 oli see 10% ja 2022/23 juba 13%. Inglismaal on viimaste andmete järgi 16% lapsi lapsendatud samasoolistesse peredesse.

Ka lapsendajate toetamine on kasvanud. Sel aastal andis National Lottery Community Fund Põhja-Iirimaal tegutsevatele gruppidele 6,3 miljonit naela, sealhulgas 10 000 naela Adoption UK-le, et toetada tegevusi peredele, kus lapsed on lapsendatud LGBTQ+ vanematega.

Adoption UK Põhja-Iirimaa direktor EJ Havlin rõhutab samasooliste lapsendajate nähtavuse tähtsust. „Korraldame perepäevi, kus samasoolistes peredes kasvavad lapsed saavad näha teisi peresid nagu nende oma. On oluline, et need pered tunneksid uhkust ja neid tunnustataks, sest palju lapsi ootab ikka veel hoolitsevat kodu.”

Paul toetab nüüd Adoption UK tugigrupi kaudu teisi potentsiaalseid samasoolisi lapsendajaid. Ta julgustab kogukonda lapsendamisele mõtlema: „Protsess on põhjalik, kuid ei erine teistest vanematest. Oleme kogenud vähe eelarvamusi ja oleme väga tänulikud, et kuulume generatsiooni, kellel on selline võimalus. See tähendab meile kõike.”

article_content: Over 20,000 injured people are still trapped in the Gaza Strip with little access to medical care, according to Doctors Without Borders (MSF). This situation persists despite some foreign nationals and critically wounded Palestinians recently being evacuated to Egypt. MSF reported that several severely injured individuals and 22 of its international staff crossed out of Gaza through the Rafah border. However, thousands still remain with limited healthcare due to the ongoing siege. Palestinian MSF staff continue to provide treatment within Gaza, while a new team of international staff stands ready to replace those who have left when the environment becomes safer. The organization is urging for more extensive evacuations, the establishment of a ceasefire, and greater permission for aid to enter the region. MSF underscored the necessity for individuals to be able to leave Gaza freely and have the right to return. On the ground, reporters witnessed ambulances transporting evacuees to Egyptian hospitals. Egyptian officials stated that 335 foreign or dual-national citizens and 76 seriously injured or ill individuals entered Egypt through the Rafah crossing. Israel’s ongoing bombardment of Gaza comes after the deadliest attack in its history—when Hamas fighters crossed the border, killing approximately 1,400 people, mostly civilians, according to Israeli authorities. The Gaza health ministry, overseen by Hamas, has put the number of deaths from the airstrikes at 8,796. Humanitarian organizations, including the United Nations, have raised alarms about worsening conditions in Gaza, where essential supplies like food, fuel, and medicine are running dangerously low for the area’s 2.4 million residents. Philippe Lazzarini, chief of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, entered Gaza and described intense desperation for basic needs such as food and water. Meanwhile, Apple Inc. has reported record quarterly revenue in India, registering strong year-over-year growth in the recent September quarter—a signal of India’s growing significance for the tech company, said CEO Tim Cook. In the luxury car market in India, buyers are getting younger, as reported by leading brands, while the merger between Sony and Zee remains uncertain amid continued regulatory investigation of ZEEL CEO Punit Goenka.

Selline olukord kestab, kuigi osa välismaalasi ja kriitiliselt haavatud palestiinlasi viidi hiljuti Egiptusesse. MSF teatas, et mitu raskelt vigastatut ning 22 nende rahvusvahelist töötajat pääses Gazast Rafah' piiriületuskoha kaudu. Kuid tuhanded jäävad piirangu ja piiratud meditsiiniabi tõttu endiselt Gazasse. MSF Palestiina töötajad jätkavad abi andmist kohapeal, samas kui uus rahvusvaheline tiim ootab võimalust piirkonda tulla, kui olukord lubab. Organisatsioon kutsub üles lubama rohkem evakuatsioone, kehtestama relvarahu ning võimaldama suuremas ulatuses humanitaarabi sissepääsu. MSF rõhutas: soovijatele tuleb võimaldada Gazast lahkumine ja hilisem naasmine. Kohapeal nägid ajakirjanikud, kuidas kiirabiautod viisid evakueerituid Egiptuse haiglatesse. Egiptuse ametnike sõnul said Rafah’ kaudu riiki 335 välis- või kahe kodakondsusega isikut ning 76 raskelt haavatut või haiget. Iisraeli jätkuvad õhurünnakud on vastus nende ajaloo raskusimale rünnakule, mil Hamasi võitlejad ületasid piiri ja tapsid umbes 1 400 inimest, peamiselt tsiviilelanikke, teatavad Iisraeli võimud. Gaza tervishoiuministeerium, mida juhib Hamas, annab teada 8 796 inimesest, kes on hukkunud õhurünnakute tõttu. Humanitaarorganisatsioonid, sealhulgas ÜRO, hoiatavad Gazas süveneva kriisi eest, kuna 2,4 miljoni elaniku jaoks napib toitu, kütust ja ravimeid. Indias noorenevad ka luksusautode ostjad, nagu tõdevad juhtivad margid. Sony ja Zee kavandatav ühinemine on aga endiselt lahtine, sest ZEELi tegevjuht Punit Goenka on jätkuvalt uurimise all väidetava rahakasutuse asjus.

Ashley Gayle-Boothe, a 26-year-old from Tampa Bay, Florida, is courageously facing breast cancer while pregnant with her first child—a pregnancy she thought unlikely due to endometriosis. In March, she learned she was expecting, only to discover a lump in her left breast two weeks later. Tests confirmed that cancer had spread to her breast, muscle, and lymph nodes.

After being assured by her doctors that the treatments wouldn’t affect her baby—since the cancer hadn’t crossed the placenta and the baby’s spinal cord had already closed—Ashley agreed to a mastectomy and chemotherapy. To protect both her health and her son's, doctors plan to induce labor eight weeks early, on October 4. Her care team is administering steroid injections before the birth to strengthen her baby's lungs, helping him breathe independently.

Ashley still faces more surgery and chemotherapy after the delivery. Despite these challenges, she’s looking forward to watching her son grow, with hopes of giving him a sibling someday.

The 'Kicking Cancer for Ashley' fund has been established at Chase bank, where donations can be made to help with Ashley’s expenses. A fundraising event is also being held this Saturday. Above all, Ashley’s main concern is for her baby’s well-being, showing her strength and optimism.

Ashley Gayle-Boothe, 26-aastane Tampa Bay'lt Floridast, seisab vapralt vastu rinnavähile ja ootab samal ajal oma esimest last – rasedust, mida ta pidas endometrioosi tõttu väga ebatõenäoliseks. Märtsis sai ta rõõmsa uudise oma ootusest, kuid kõigest kaks nädalat hiljem leidis ta vasakust rinnast tüki. Uuringud näitasid, et vähk oli levinud rinda, lihasesse ja lümfisõlmedesse.

Kui arstid kinnitasid, et vajalikud ravimeetodid ei mõjuta lapse tervist – kuna vähk polnud platsentat ületanud ja beebi seljaaju oli juba täielikult arenenud – nõustus Ashley mastektoomia ja keemiaraviga. Mõlema tervise huvides otsustati sünnitus esile kutsuda kaheksa nädalat enne tähtaega, 4. oktoobril. Et toetada lapse kopsude arengut, antakse talle enne sündi steroidisüste, et beebi suudaks iseseisvalt hingata.

article_content: One week after a devastating 7.0-magnitude earthquake hit Port-au-Prince, Haitian authorities have buried at least 70,000 people, with the total death toll possibly reaching up to 200,000. These estimates do not include those buried privately by families or retrieved by the UN peacekeepers, and the number of identified victims remains unclear. Dr. Jon Andrus, deputy director of the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), has raised concerns about inadequate burial practices due to resource constraints, especially the lack of refrigeration. In the midst of rising casualties, aid workers are focusing efforts on those still alive. The United Nations estimates that about 3 million Haitians are in urgent need of food, water, shelter, and medical assistance. International rescue teams are actively searching for survivors; 43 teams, comprising more than 1,700 personnel, have successfully carried out close to 90 rescues. Notably, New York emergency responders recently saved two children from the ruins of a collapsed building and brought them to an Israeli field hospital, while another survivor, Ena Zizi, was rescued near the national cathedral after several days. The demand for critical care remains high, with shortages in blood supplies and limited cold storage complicating the situation. The influx of international aid has overwhelmed Port-au-Prince’s airport, causing delays in delivering vital supplies. To address this, the US military is diverting flights to other ports. Previously handling 13 daily flights, the airport is now grappling with more than 200. Despite many challenges, noticeable improvements are underway. Cleared roads now allow aid to reach those in need, and some hospitals have resumed crucial surgeries. Dr. Rajiv Shah from USAID pointed to the delivery of water purification units and millions of meals as part of ongoing international assistance, emphasizing the need for sustainable relief. At the main general hospital, medical professionals are struggling with shortages and unsafe facilities, resorting to makeshift solutions as essential supplies dwindle. The US military is stepping in to supply food, tents, electricity, and medical equipment to support relief operations. To boost security and order, the UN has approved an extra 2,000 soldiers and 1,500 police officers, while Haiti’s port is set to reopen, enabling the arrival of emergency fuel supplies. Venezuela is sending 225,000 barrels of gasoline and diesel to the region. Currently, around 2,000 US troops are on the ground, with another 5,000 stationed offshore. Plans are in place to increase this number to 10,000, with a primary focus on aid distribution and medical assistance. Haitian President Rene Preval has praised the rapid progress in restoring essential services and credits international cooperation for the advances. Isolated incidents of unrest have occurred, but authorities report that overall violence is lower than it was before the quake. Globally, people have donated over $220 million to US aid groups. Meanwhile, orphaned Haitian children are being placed with foster families in the United States while adoptions, already underway before the disaster, are finalized. While Haiti’s challenges remain enormous, global solidarity and continued aid efforts are contributing to hope and recovery for millions.

article_content: Here is a summary of the most widely shared but false stories and images from this week. The Associated Press investigated these viral claims and here are the facts:  Gas Leak at a Kentucky Polling Place Sparks Election Conspiracy Theories CLAIM: Reports of a gas leak at a Kentucky polling station were part of an election-rigging scheme to benefit Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear. FACTS: Louisville Gas & Electric confirmed there was an actual gas leak at Highland Baptist Church, a polling place in Jefferson County, on Tuesday morning. The leak led to the polling place closing for 30 minutes. To ensure voters got the required 12-hour window, a judge extended voting by half an hour that evening. Only one additional ballot was cast after 6 p.m., according to the county clerk. Social media users suggested the gas leak was staged, but officials dismissed these allegations as unfounded. Erran Huber, a spokesperson for the Jefferson County Clerk’s Office, called the conspiracy theories 'patently absurd.' Chris Whelan, spokesman for Louisville Gas & Electric, confirmed that gas emitted from a church stove was detected but not at dangerous levels and was quickly addressed. A similar half-hour extension occurred at a nearby elementary school polling location due to a separate police incident. Despite conspiracy theories, there is no evidence of election fraud.  Voting Machine Error in Pennsylvania County Misrepresented Online CLAIM: Democrats manipulated Pennsylvania elections using ‘rigged’ voting machines that flipped votes. FACTS: Some social media posts falsely claimed election machines in Pennsylvania were rigged. The issue occurred in Northampton County, where a clerical error by Election Systems & Software led some machines to print summaries that mixed up the 'yes' and 'no' votes for two judges. The actual votes were properly recorded and counted, officials confirmed. Approximately 70,000 votes were cast in Northampton County, and statewide results show both judges retained their positions with significant margins. Election integrity experts, including Mark Lindeman from Verified Voting, confirmed the issue resulted from human error, not fraud.  No Evidence of Ukrainian President Surrendering to Russia CLAIM: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy surrendered and Ukraine has fallen to Russia. FACTS: President Zelenskyy has not surrendered. Ukraine remains in conflict with Russia. Viral posts claimed otherwise but provided no evidence, and there have been no major changes on the battlefield. Zelenskyy recently appeared on NBC's 'Meet the Press' and continued to encourage unity in the fight against Russia. article_content: Africa’s response to the renewed conflict between Israel and Palestine is increasingly divided. Historically, most African nations identified with Palestinians, but today, stances vary widely across the continent, shaped by each country’s strategic interests and history. After a recent Hamas assault in southern Israel, Kenyan President William Ruto quickly condemned the attacks, voicing strong support for Israel and emphasizing the need to hold terrorists accountable. His message underscored Israel’s strengthening relationships in Africa. Conversely, countries like South Africa and Algeria maintain firm support for Palestine. South African officials argue that Israel’s occupation and actions at holy sites are to blame for the latest violence. Algeria declared full solidarity with Palestine, while the African Union cited ongoing denial of Palestinian rights and advocated for a two-state solution. Meanwhile, Kenya, Zambia, Ghana, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo are among a growing group of African nations expressing support for Israel. Experts believe these varying responses demonstrate governments’ efforts to balance historical ties and practical benefits—between longstanding pro-Palestinian solidarity and the allure of Israeli technology, aid, and security cooperation. In the wake of decolonization, most African states cut ties with Israel following the 1973 war, siding with Palestinian aspirations. Decades later, circumstances have shifted: 44 African nations recognize Israel, and nearly 30 maintain embassies or consulates in Tel Aviv. Israel’s expertise in agriculture and water management, especially vital for countries facing climate challenges and food insecurity, has made close relationships more attractive. Israel’s trade with Africa is now substantial, with South Africa, despite opposing Israeli policy, serving as a key trading partner. Nigeria, among others, also maintains significant trade ties. Israel’s involvement is not limited to commerce. The country has delivered humanitarian aid, educational opportunities, and military training throughout Africa. This includes backing for military units in Cameroon and agricultural or medical training for students from Kenya and Senegal. Israel’s overtures to African organizations have met resistance. Its attempt to guarantee observer status within the African Union was blocked in early 2023, mainly by Algeria and South Africa; Palestine continues to enjoy AU observer status. Some African governments face criticism for balancing deeper business and security links with public support for Palestinian rights. Analysts see this pragmatic approach as consistent with Africa’s responses to other world crises, such as the war in Ukraine. Civil society groups, especially in South Africa, are pressing their governments to take firmer pro-Palestinian stances. South Africa recently downgraded diplomatic representation with Israel and currently lacks an ambassador there, amid advocacy for strong boycotts against trade with Israel. As the Israeli-Palestinian conflict evolves, grassroots calls for African governments to reevaluate their alliances are likely to increase.

article_content: Jan Leeming, who spent seven years as a BBC newsreader and once hosted Eurovision, has raised concerns about a significant decline in the clarity of speech among television presenters and actors today. Now 72, Leeming says she often needs to turn on subtitles to understand what’s being said—something she attributes to many younger presenters not finishing or articulating words clearly. Writing for Daily Mail Weekend, Leeming urges TV networks to provide diction and enunciation classes for young broadcasters, insisting that clear communication is essential in their field. She points out that her difficulty understanding TV speech is not due to hearing loss, noting she can even hear her kitchen cat flap from another room. Leeming specifically commends Channel 4 News anchor Jon Snow for his articulate broadcasting, but observes that some newsreaders put emphasis on the wrong words, making their speech harder to follow. Her comments echo previous complaints from audiences—BBC dramas like Jamaica Inn and Quirke reportedly received nearly 2,200 complaints about mumbled lines and strong accents. BBC Director-General Tony Hall has acknowledged these issues, saying actors muttering can be a challenge for viewers. Leeming recalls watching a comedy show where theatre-trained actors were easy to understand, in contrast to soap stars whose lack of projection and unclear enunciation made their lines hard to follow. Her perspective is shaped by her own childhood speech lessons, taken to neutralize her regional accent, and she calls for renewed attention to spoken clarity in television.

Nüüd 72-aastane Leeming ütleb, et tal tuleb sageli subtiitreid sisse lülitada, et aru saada, mida räägitakse — tema sõnul tuleneb see paljude noorte saatejuhtide ebaselgest ja poolikuks jäävast hääldusest. Tema tähelepanekud peegeldavad varasemaid vaatajate rahulolematust — näiteks BBC draamad Jamaica Inn ja Quirke said kokku ligi 2200 kaebust seoses näitlejate pudistamise ja tugeva aktsendiga. article_content: A recent breakthrough in imaging technology could soon allow scientists to observe some of the coldest objects in the universe indefinitely. Until now, examining matter at temperatures near absolute zero was challenging because the energy from imaging light would heat and destroy the sample. Physicists from the University of Nottingham have developed a computer program that, for the first time, reveals exactly how this energy behaves during imaging, and offers a method to use it for keeping particles cold. When boson particles are cooled close to absolute zero (−273.15°C or −459.67°F), they form a rarefied gas known as a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC)—a groundbreaking state of matter central to quantum physics. The research team has now simulated how BECs behave when photographed at such low temperatures and proposed a way to keep the gas cool throughout, making it possible to study these systems for extended periods. BECs, created in laboratories since the mid-1990s, are kept cold with magnetic coils. They have zero viscosity and behave as single, blob-like masses, enabling scientists to observe atomic changes and quantum effects. However, traditional imaging techniques cannot be used since the extra energy from light rapidly heats the BEC and destroys its delicate state. Off-resonant photon imaging—with lasers that bounce energy off atoms instead of into them—can capture images of BECs without rapid heating, but only for short durations. The Nottingham team, led by Michael Hush in collaboration with Australian researchers, developed a sophisticated simulation that models both BEC behavior and the effects of off-resonant imaging. Their results reveal, in unprecedented detail, how energy disperses within the BEC during imaging. Remarkably, the scientists showed that the heating effect from imaging could be virtually redirected into the magnetic coils used for cooling, maintaining the condensate's low temperature much longer. While this method has not yet been tested in physical experiments, the researchers believe it could revolutionize the study of ultra-cold quantum matter, with implications for precision measurement and quantum computing. These findings are published in the New Journal of Physics.
translated_content: Hiljutine läbimurre pildistamistehnoloogias võib peagi võimaldada teadlastel vaadelda mõningaid universumi kõige külmemaid objekte piiramatult kaua. Seni oli mateeria uurimine absoluutse nullilähedaste temperatuuride juures keeruline, kuna pildistamisel kasutatav valgusenergia soojendas ja hävitas proovi. Nottinghami Ülikooli füüsikud on loonud arvutiprogrammi, mis esimest korda näitab täpselt, kuidas see energia pildistamisel käitub, ning pakub viisi selle ärakasutamiseks osakeste külmana hoidmiseks. Kui bosone jahutada absoluutse nullini (−273,15°C või −459,67°F) lähedaste temperatuurideni, moodustavad nad haruldase gaasi, mida nimetatakse Bose–Einsteini kondensaadiks (BEK) – see on kvantfüüsika keskne ja ainulaadne olek. Uurimisrühm on nüüd simuleerinud, kuidas BEK-id käituvad madalatel temperatuuridel pildistamisel, ning pakkunud välja lähenemise, kuidas seda gaasi jahedana hoida kogu vaatlusperioodi jooksul, võimaldades süsteemi kauem uurida. BEK-e on laborites loodud alates 1990ndate keskpaigast ning neid jahutatakse magnetpoolidega. Neil puudub viskoossus ja nad käituvad üheainsa, tilgalaadse massina, võimaldades teadlastel jälgida aatomimuutusi ja kvantprotsesse. Traditsioonilisi pildistamismeetodeid kasutada ei saa, sest valgusenergia kuumutab BEK-i kiiresti üles ja hävitab selle delikaatse oleku. Väljaspool resonantsi olevate footonitega laserpildistamine – see laser peegeldab energia aatomite pealt tagasi, selle asemel et viia seda neisse sisse – võimaldab BEK-i kiiret soojenemist vältida ja seda siiski pildistada, kuid ainult lühiajaliselt. Nottinghami meeskond eesotsas Michael Hushiga ning Austraalia teadlastega töötas välja keerulise simulatsiooni, mis kirjeldab nii BEK-ide käitumist kui ka väljaspool resonantsi pildistamise mõju. Nende tulemused näitavad esmakordselt detailides, kuidas energia pildistamise ajal BEK-is jaotub. Teadlased näitasid, et pildistamisest tekkivat soojust saaks virtuaalselt suunata BEK-i jahutamiseks kasutatavatesse magnetpoolidesse, võimaldades kondensaadi kauem madalal temperatuuril säilimist. Kuigi seda meetodit pole veel eksperimentaalselt katsetatud, usuvad teadlased, et see võib muuta ülikülma kvantmaterjali uurimist, laienedes täppismõõtmistele ja kvantarvutustele. Uuring avaldati ajakirjas New Journal of Physics.

article_content: As a senior leader at Amazon with 20 years of experience in the tech industry, I've participated in hundreds of interviews across several organizations. One interview practice that has never made sense to me is having direct reports interview their future manager. Although I've never used this approach as an interviewer, I have encountered it as a candidate in around 25% of the leadership roles I've interviewed for. Even though I've received offers from organizations using this method, I consider it a poor practice, and believe companies should reconsider its use. The main aim of interviews is to assess whether a candidate can fulfill job responsibilities and fit well within the team. While seeking input from a candidate’s likely direct reports might seem logical, it introduces conflicts of interest and misalignment with organizational needs. When a new management position opens, it's common for existing team members to feel they deserve a promotion. Management may have already evaluated these employees and decided none were suitable, leading the role to be offered to external candidates. In such scenarios, team members might feel slighted, creating tension and affecting their judgment during interviews. These employees may not be truly objective—they could prefer the least qualified, the most personable, or even the candidate they simply like best. Approving a qualified new manager may also mean confirming that their own promotion prospects have stalled, unless the new hire fails. This presents another issue: employees could select a weak manager, giving themselves an opportunity to outshine or replace them. While not inevitable, such dynamics can create ongoing conflict and undermine success. Even if motives are pure, there is another concern. If current employees aren't qualified to fill the management position, they're likely ill-equipped to evaluate candidates for it. They may opt for the most likable candidate rather than the most capable one, jeopardizing the company's long-term interests. Interviewers require relevant experience, qualification, and training to evaluate candidates objectively and avoid bias. While including direct reports in the process is a considerate gesture, it is not the best way to identify the right person for the job. Instead, companies should rely on more qualified and less conflicted interviewers for primary screening. If you still wish to involve direct reports, consider informal interviews that allow team members to get to know prospective managers or raise any obvious concerns that might otherwise be overlooked. Brandon Southern is a senior leader at Amazon and former head of analytics at eBay and GameStop. He also produces TikTok content on data analytics and career development.

Juhtkond on tõenäoliselt juba hinnanud neid töötajaid ja otsustanud, et keegi neist ei sobi sellele kohale, mistõttu pakutakse ametikohta väliskandidaadile. Ka puhaste motiivide korral on veel üks murekoht – kui olemasolevad töötajad pole piisavalt pädevad sellel juhtival ametikohal töötamiseks, on nad tõenäoliselt veelgi vähem pädevad kandidaate objektiivselt hindama. Tõenäoliselt valitakse siis mitte pädevaim kandidaat, vaid lihtsalt kõige meeldivam, mis võib mõjutada ettevõtte pikaajalist edu. Intervjueerijatel peab olema asjakohane kogemus, kvalifikatsioon ja väljaõpe, et hinnata kandidaate objektiivselt ning vältida kallutatust. Kuigi on kena žest kaasata otseseid alluvaid protsessi, pole see parim viis õige inimese leidmiseks ametikohale. Selle asemel peaksid ettevõtted kasutama esmaseks hindamiseks pädevaid ja sõltumatuid intervjueerijaid. article_content: The head and three officials of Indonesian company Afi Farma have been sentenced to two years in prison and fined 1 billion Indonesian rupiah ($63,056; £51,786) after their cough syrup was linked to the deaths of more than 200 children. Afi Farma was accused of producing cough syrups with high levels of toxic substances. The company's lawyer stated they denied negligence and might appeal the verdict. Prosecutors had asked for up to nine years' imprisonment for the company's chief executive, Arief Prasetya Harahap, and seven years for each of the other three officials. According to prosecutors, from October 2021 to February 2022, Afi Farma received two batches of propylene glycol—a substance used in cough syrup—which actually contained 96% to 99% ethylene glycol. Both chemicals can act as additives in solvents. Propylene glycol is non-toxic and widely used in medicine, cosmetics, and food. In contrast, ethylene glycol is poisonous and used in products like paint, pens, and brake fluid. Prosecutors said the company failed to test the ingredients in its cough syrup, relying solely on safety certificates from its supplier. Afi Farma's lawyer, Samsul Hidayat, told the BBC that Indonesia's drug regulator did not require companies to thoroughly test ingredients. The judge at Kediri District Court in East Java ruled that the four defendants were guilty of intentionally producing pharmaceutical products that failed to meet safety standards. The case comes amid global efforts to strengthen oversight of drug supply chains after several cases of poisoning. Since 2022, more than 200 Indonesian children, mostly under five, have died from acute kidney injury linked to contaminated cough syrup. Similar incidents have resulted in around 100 deaths in The Gambia and Uzbekistan. The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued warnings about six cough syrups produced in India and Indonesia. Additional reporting by Jerome Wirawan in Jakarta, Indonesia.

article_content: Despite telling reporters this morning, "I'm going to get there," Jim Jordan was unsuccessful in his second attempt to win the House Speaker vote. In fact, his defeat was greater this time, with 22 Republicans voting against him, compared to 20 in the first round. Several other House Republicans received votes despite not being official candidates, including Kevin McCarthy, Steve Scalise, Tom Emmer, Byron Donalds, Lee Zeldin, Mike Garcia, Candice Miller, Kay Granger, Bruce Westerman, and even former Speaker John Boehner. Once again, Democratic House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries earned unanimous support from his party, receiving 212 votes, while Jordan received 199 from Republicans. On the second ballot, Rep. Jim Jordan (R-OH) was unable to secure the speakership as 22 Republicans supported other candidates – up from 20 in the first round. Jordan managed to win over two Republicans but lost support from four others. All 212 Democrats continued to back Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY).

article_content: Countries moved a step closer on Saturday to launching a fund to help poorer nations affected by climate disasters, despite concerns from developing countries and the United States. The agreement to create a 'loss and damage' fund, reached at last year's United Nations climate talks in Egypt, was a major achievement for developing nations after years of resistance from wealthier countries. However, over the last 11 months, governments have struggled to finalize the fund's details, such as who will provide the financing and where the fund will be hosted. A special UN committee, assigned to implement the fund, met for the fifth time in Abu Dhabi this week, following stalled progress in Egypt last month, to complete recommendations that will be presented at the upcoming COP28 climate summit in Dubai. The aim is to have the fund operational by 2024. The committee, which includes representatives from various regions, agreed to recommend the World Bank as an interim trustee and host of the fund for a four-year period, a topic that has caused tension between developed and developing countries. Developing nations have argued that housing the fund at the World Bank, whose presidents are appointed by the US, would give donor countries too much influence and raise costs for recipients. To reach a compromise, the World Bank will serve as an interim trustee and host for four years. Jennifer Morgan, Germany’s special climate envoy, said on X that Berlin is ready to contribute to the new fund and is exploring more stable sources of financing. Others were less positive. Harjeet Singh, head of global political strategy at Climate Action Network International, said it was a disappointing day for climate justice and accused wealthy countries of not doing enough. 'Rich countries have not only pushed developing nations to accept the World Bank as the host of the Loss and Damage Fund, but have also failed to lead in providing financial aid,' he said. The committee also recommended that developed countries continue to support the fund, but could not agree on whether wealthy nations should be legally required to contribute. A US State Department official told Reuters that the US regrets the lack of clear language on the voluntary nature of contributions. The US tried to add a footnote to clarify that contributions are voluntary, but this was not accepted by the committee chair, which the US objected to. Sultan al-Jaber, president of COP28, welcomed the committee’s recommendations and said they paved the way for an agreement at COP28.

Viimase 11 kuu jooksul on valitsused aga pidanud vaidlema fondi üksikasjade üle, näiteks selle üle, kes rahastab ja kus fond asub. Fondi elluviimist juhtiv erikomitee kogunes sel nädalal Abu Dhabis viiendat korda pärast ummikseisu Egiptuses eelmisel kuul, et lõpule viia soovitused, mis esitatakse läheneval COP28 kliimatippkohtumisel Dubais. Eesmärk on saada fond tööle aastaks 2024. Komitee, mis koosneb eri piirkondade esindajatest, nõustus soovitama Maailmapanka fondi ajutise halduri ja peremehena neljaks aastaks – see teema on põhjustanud pingeid arenenud ja arenguriikide vahel. Arenguriikide sõnul annaks Maailmapanga asukoht, mille presidente nimetab USA, doonorriikidele liiga suure mõjuvõimu ja tõstaks vastuvõtjatele kulusid. Kompromissina hakkab Maailmapank tegutsema nelja aasta vältel ajutise halduri ja peremehena. Saksamaa kliima erisaadik Jennifer Morgan kirjutas X-is, et Berliin on valmis panustama uude fondi ja kaalub täiendavaid rahastamisvõimalusi. Kõik ei olnud aga sama optimistlikud. Harjeet Singh, rahvusvahelise Climate Action Networki ülemaailmse poliitika strateegia juht, ütles, et see oli kliimaõigluse jaoks pettumust valmistav päev ning süüdistas jõukaid riike väheses toetuses. USA proovis lisada joonealuse märkuse, et panustamine fondi on vabatahtlik, kuid komitee esimees seda ei lubanud, mispeale USA protesteeris. COP28 president Sultan al-Jaber tervitas komitee soovitusi ja märkis, et need sillutavad teed kokkuleppe saavutamiseks COP28-l.

article_content: Some Texas drivers have accumulated thousands of unpaid tolls, seemingly undeterred. According to the Texas Department of Transportation, a man and woman from Pflugerville have driven through toll booths without paying 14,358 times. Their outstanding bill—including tolls and fines—has reached $236,026.32 as of Wednesday. Officials issued a deadline, warning top offenders they would publicly release their names if payments were not received. The state followed through by publishing the names of its 25 most significant violators, all from the Austin area, with 16 owing over $100,000 each. Altogether, Texans owe $27 million in unpaid tolls, and more than 28,000 individuals have unpaid balances over $100. The state offers payment plans and is open to negotiating settlements. Authorities contacted these drivers by mail and phone prior to the deadline. Collecting more than 14,000 violations would require skipping toll payments twice daily for almost 20 years. If caught for a traffic offense, violators could have their vehicles impounded.
